note: DISPOSITION LEDGER for the 2026-09-09 epsilon census. Every entry was produced by a triage agent and then independently re-derived by a second agent instructed to refute it; only sites where the refutation FAILED are listed. ⚠ THIS FILE WAS THE OPEN LIST WHEN 2.14.0 SHIPPED AND IS NOW A CLOSED ONE — read the per-entry `disposition`, not the filename. Line numbers are as of the 2.13.0/2.14.0 tree; re-locate by the quoted guard text, not by the number.

defects.guarded_quantity: gg_old = _opt_dot(g, g, n) = ||g_old||^2, the SQUARED Euclidean norm of the previous gradient. Dimensions [f]^2/[x]^2 — it carries both the objective's unit and the variables' unit (rescale f by c and it moves by c^2; measure x in mm instead of m and it moves by 1e-6). Confirmed by reading: `_opt_dot` (optimize.cyr:74) is a raw sum of products with no normalisation, and g is written straight by the caller's `fncall2(grad, x, g)`. No caller normalises — the only in-tree callers (tests/hisab.tcyr:1316, tests/modules.tcyr:4368, tests/modules.tcyr:8064, tests/abuse.tcyr) pass raw hand-written or tape-backed gradients, and neither the module header nor the function's own doc block asks for a normalised gradient.
defects.protects: The division `beta = f64_div(pr_dot, gg_old)` at optimize.cyr:320 (the Polak-Ribiere+ ratio). Verified by a no-guard control run, not argued: with the guard removed entirely, f(x)=x^2 from x0=5 with tol=0 (so the loop reaches an exactly-zero gradient) returns x = NaN and fmin = NaN — 0/0 poisons d, then x. With the shipped guard, with a DBL_MIN floor, or with a bare `gg_old > 0` sign test, the same call returns x = 0.0 exactly. So a guard IS required here; only its threshold is wrong.
defects.why: All five refutation routes were tried against the shipped function and all five fail on measurement. (1) NOT dimensionless: gg_old is ||g||^2 straight from the caller's gradient, nothing bounds or normalises it. (2) NOT normalised by the caller: no caller in src/, tests/, examples/ or docs normalises, and the API does not ask for it. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: the convergence test is a SEPARATE line five above, `f64_lt(gnorm, tol)` against the caller's own tol, and it returns; this guard only silences beta. Reading the two together yields a fact the original filing missed and that sharpens it — at line 312, `sqrt(gg_old) >= tol` ALWAYS holds, because the smaller case already returned. So the guard is reachable only with gg_old >= tol^2, and an absolute 1e-12 cut is live exactly when tol < 1e-6. (4) The proposed threshold breaks NO existing test: all three in-tree CG fixtures (x^4+x^2 from 3 with tol 1e-8 / 40 iters; x^2 from 5 with tol = EPSILON_F64 / 200 iters; the (1,2) bowl with tol 1e-6 / 200000 iters) return identical rc, identical iteration counts and BIT-IDENTICAL out_x under all four guards (shipped 1e-12, DBL_MIN, 1e-24, sign) — they are 1-D or condition-number 1, where beta cannot matter. (5) The scale test DOES discriminate, and brackets the eps^2 repair. Measured on the shipped code (a verbatim copy whose mode-0 output was first proven bit-identical to the shipped entry point at all 41 scales, rc and both words, 0 mismatches): shipped returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE at 200 iterations for every k <= 0 INCLUDING k = 0, i.e. in default units with the ordinary tol = 1e-8, where the scale-free guard returns rc = 0 in 133; and it departs from the scale-free trajectory for every k <= 6, becoming bit-identical only at k >= 7 (L = 128). That break point is the squared-vs-unsquared error made visible: the band is live iff tol_L = L*1e-8 < sqrt(EPSILON_F64) = 1e-6, i.e. L < 100, which sits between k = 6 (64) and k = 7 (128) exactly as the mechanism predicts. The squaring error is what makes it bite at default scale, but it is NOT the primary class: the eps^2 = 1e-24 repair, which fixes only the squaring, still fails the same sweep for every k <= -13 (its own crossing, L*1e-8 < 1e-12 => L < 1e-4). Both errors are present; the absolute cut on a dimensioned quantity is the one that survives fixing the other, so DEFECT_ABSOLUTE_ON_SCALING is the correct class. Note also that beta itself is dimensionless (a ratio of two gradient^2 quantities), so thresholding the denominator alone imports a scale the formula does not have. Three sibling guards of the same shape sit in this file at lines 442, 609 and 675 on `sy`/`yy`, which are different quantities and out of scope for this object.
defects.fabricates: No fabricated number — a silent ALGORITHM substitution with no error channel: beta is pinned to 0, degrading Polak-Ribiere+ CG to steepest descent, reported only through the ordinary tol/max_iter path. `_opt_copy(out_x, x, n)` runs on the HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE path too (optimize.cyr:343), so a caller ignoring rc receives a far-from-optimal point that looks like an answer. Measured on the shipped binary, f = 1/2(x0^2 + 100*x1^2), x0 = (L,L), tol = L*1e-8, max_iter = 200: the returned x0/L spans 1.310575e-02 (k = -24) ... 4.995144e-08 (k = 0) ... -6.158716e-09 (k >= 7), about six decades of answer for one problem in different units, against a single bit pattern (-6.158716e-09) at all 49 scales under a scale-free guard. Iteration count is degraded even where rc = 0: 182/183/184/176/163/137 at k = 1..6 versus a flat 133.
defects.correct_threshold: gg_old >= DBL_MIN (0x0010000000000000 = 2.2250738585072014e-308) — the only value at which pr_dot/gg_old can 0/0 or overflow; equivalently, divide first and reject a non-finite beta. Both are computable without knowing the caller's units. Sharpened by what the code guarantees: because the convergence test five lines up already returned when sqrt(gg_old) < tol, the guard is only reached with gg_old >= tol^2, so a DBL_MIN floor is UNREACHABLE for every caller with a normal positive tol — it can fire only when tol is zero/subnormal AND the previous gradient is exactly zero, which is precisely the 0/0 case. Verified both ways: with no guard at all that case returns NaN; with the DBL_MIN floor (and with a bare `f64_lt(0, gg_old)` sign test) it returns 0.0 exactly, and all three in-tree CG fixtures are bit-identical to today. A repair to EPSILON_F64^2 = 1e-24 is measurably NOT correct — it keeps an absolute cut on a dimensioned quantity and merely moves the break from k <= 6 to k <= -13 (L = 1e-4), where the same family again diverges (rc = -8 with 200 iterations for k <= -20).
defects.scale_test: Similarity family, the SAME bowl in different units: f_L(u) = L^2 * f_1(u/L), grad_L(u) = L * grad_1(u/L), x0_L = L * x0_1, tol_L = L * tol_1, with f_1(x) = 1/2(x0^2 + 100 x1^2), x0_1 = (1,1), tol_1 = 1e-8, max_iter = 200. CG-from-steepest-descent is exactly covariant under it (g -> Lg, d -> Ld, both sides of the Armijo test -> L^2, alpha and beta invariant), and L = 2^k makes every rescaling exact in binary FP, so the assertion is BIT-EXACT, not a tolerance: for L = 2^k, out_x/L must be bit-identical to the k = 0 result and rc must be identical. THREE requirements the original statement did not pin down, each established by measurement here, and each of which silently vacates the test if dropped. (a) THE OBJECTIVE MUST BE ILL-CONDITIONED AND n >= 2. The same 41-scale sweep run on a condition-number-1 family — the in-tree bowl (u0-L)^2 + (u1-2L)^2 from (-0.5L, 2.5L) — is bit-identical under ALL FOUR guards (shipped 1e-12, DBL_MIN, 1e-24, sign) at 41/41 scales, because with kappa = 1 the Armijo step lands on the exact minimiser and beta never matters. A scale sweep built on the fixture the suite already has would report a clean PASS on the defective code. kappa = 100 with n = 2 is the minimum that discriminates. (b) THE RANGE MUST REACH k <= -14, not merely below the shipped break: shipped departs at k <= 6, the eps^2 mutant only at k <= -13. k in {-160,-152,...,152,160} (41 points, gg_old sweeping 2^-320..2^320 ~ 1e-96..1e96) brackets 1e-10, the shipped 1e-12, 1e-16, EPSILON_F64^2 = 1e-24, 1e-30 and 1e-50, so every absolute threshold a repair might plausibly pick dies on the same sweep; DBL_MIN and a sign test pass at every point (49/49 on a fine k in [-32,16] sweep, 41/41 on the wide one). (c) THE ASSERTION MUST BE rc AND BIT-EXACT x/L TOGETHER: at k = 1..6 the shipped guard returns rc = 0 with a different trajectory (182/183/184/176/163/137 iterations, different x), so an rc-only assertion misses six scales, and above k = 7 it agrees exactly, so a sweep confined to large L sees nothing at all. Measured today against the shipped entry point (probe validated first: mode-0 copy bit-identical to `opt_conjugate_gradient` at all 41 scales) — scale-free: rc 0 / 133 iters / one bit pattern at every scale; shipped: rc -8 / 200 iters at every k <= 0 including k = 0.

defects.guarded_quantity: sy = _opt_dot(s, y, n) = (x_new - x) . (g_new - g), the curvature product. Line 442 IS the guard (`if (f64_lt(EPSILON_F64, sy) == 1) {`); `rho = f64_div(_OPT_F64_ONE, sy)` is 443. Dimensions [x]*[f]/[x] = [f], the unit of the OBJECTIVE: invariant under a change of the variables' unit (s scales by lambda, y by 1/lambda) but LINEAR in the objective's unit. MEASURED, not argued: over the similarity family at L = 2^k, k in [-400,160], the live sy values run 0x0a98c3036547e504 (~1.7e-257) to 0x546e848200000000 (~2.7e98) — 355 decades on ONE fixture. It is not dimensionless and it is not bounded.
defects.protects: Two distinct things, which is why one magnitude test is wrong for both: (a) rho = f64_div(1.0, sy) on line 443, which fails only at sy = 0 or subnormal; (b) positive-definiteness of the BFGS inverse-Hessian update, which requires sy > 0 — a SIGN condition. Neither is a magnitude condition at 1e-12.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE ANGLES; ALL FIVE FAILED, each against the compiled library under cycc 6.6.2 (scratch copies of the tree, repo untouched). (1) "Dimensionless/bounded" — refuted by the 355-decade measured range above. (2) "Caller normalises" — refuted by reading: opt_bfgs is a public entry point taking raw `f`/`grad` function pointers; nothing normalises f, g, s, y, or even d — _opt_armijo (optimize.cyr:117) starts at alpha = 1 on the unnormalised d = -H_inv*g. (3) "It is a convergence tolerance" — refuted: `tol` is a separate parameter and the convergence test is `f64_lt(gnorm, tol)` at line 405. EPSILON_F64 at 442 gates the rank-2 update only. (4) "The repair breaks an existing test" — REFUTED BY RUNNING IT. With line 442 changed to the sign test `f64_lt(_OPT_F64_ZERO, sy)` (mutation grep-verified installed), all five suites pass unchanged: hisab 416/416, foundation 359/359, modules 1827/1827, edge_cases 233/233, abuse 776/776 = 3611 assertions, 0 failures. No existing test discriminates in either direction. (5) "The scale test does not discriminate" — refuted; see scale_test, which I ran. THE DEFECT REPRODUCES IN THE SHIPPED BINARY: on f_L(v) = L^2 * (1/2)(u0^2 + 100*u1^2) with u = v/L, x0 = L*(1,1), tol = L*1e-8, max_iter 200 — for k <= -25 the shipped guard skips 200 of 200 updates, BFGS degenerates to steepest descent, and it returns rc = -8 at x/L = (1.19e-2, 1.60e-4) with f/L^2 = 7.23e-5 instead of 0; the sign guard returns rc = 0 in 4 iterations with 0 updates skipped at every one of those scales. Even at k = 0 the shipped guard already skips 1 of 4 updates. NOTE the same guard on the same quantity is duplicated at optimize.cyr:675 (opt_lbfgs), and the same absolute-epsilon-on-a-dimensioned-quantity shape appears twice more in this file — 312 (gg_old = ||g||^2, unit [f]^2/[x]^2) and 609 (yy = ||y||^2). Four instances, one file. The tree already contains the right constant: `F64_TINY = 0x0010_0000_0000_0000` (DBL_MIN) was just added to src/error.cyr with a comment that scopes EPSILON_F64 to "a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity" — sy is not one, so this site is exactly what that comment excludes.
defects.fabricates: rc = 0 with a silently wrong answer, and separately a fabricated failure. Both measured in-library. (a) WRONG ANSWER, rc = 0: at k = -20, -15, -10 the shipped guard skips 2 of 4 updates and returns rc = 0 at x0/L = 0xbd6ed89047044000 = -8.767e-13, x1/L = 0xbd1146840c848000 = -1.534e-14, where the scale-free guard returns 0xbc55094d80000000 = -4.562e-18 and 0xbcc0b565c0100000 = -4.638e-16 at every scale — the SAME problem in different units, ~6 decades apart in x/L, both reported as success. (This reproduces the filing's claimed -8.77e-13 vs -4.56e-18 exactly; its emulation was faithful.) (b) FABRICATED FAILURE: for k <= -25 all 200 updates are skipped, H_inv stays frozen at the identity, BFGS is steepest descent with no signal, and the caller gets HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE on a kappa = 100 quadratic that is not ill-conditioned — only its unit is small.
defects.correct_threshold: `if (f64_lt(F64_TINY, sy) == 1)` — i.e. sy > DBL_MIN, using the `F64_TINY` constant now defined in src/error.cyr. This is a ONE-TOKEN change at line 442 and is the whole repair: DBL_MIN > 0, so the single test carries both duties — the sign condition BFGS's positive-definiteness needs, and the exact representability bound that makes 1/sy finite. It needs no scale chosen for it. MEASURED to be at least as robust as the bare sign test: over k in [-490,160] both are bit-exact, and in the subnormal-sy regime below k = -495 the sign test admits sy so small that rho = 1/sy overflows (it returns rc = -8 at k = -511..-499) while DBL_MIN returns rc = 0 throughout. If a numerical-quality skip is also wanted, the only scale-free form is sy >= c * ||s|| * ||y|| with c a DIMENSIONLESS cosine — never an absolute number. Apply the identical repair to the duplicate at optimize.cyr:675.
defects.scale_test: SHARPENED AND RUN, not proposed. Similarity family f_L(v) = L^2 * f_1(v/L), grad_L(v) = L * grad_1(v/L), x0_L = L * x0_1, tol_L = L * tol_1, with f_1 = (1/2)(u0^2 + 100*u1^2), x0_1 = (1,1), tol_1 = 1e-8, max_iter = 200, L = 2^k. BFGS with H0 = I is exactly covariant under it (every Armijo alpha is chosen identically because f and g.d both scale by L^2), so assert out_x/L BIT-IDENTICAL to the k = 0 result and rc identical. RANGE: use k in [-400, +160] stepping 1, NOT the filing's [-160,160] — measured, [-160,160] drives sy only over ~3.3e-113..2.7e98 and therefore does NOT kill a 1e-200 or 1e-250 threshold, while [-400,160] drives sy over ~1.7e-257..2.7e98 and does. BRACKETING (measured counts of deviating k over k in [-400,160] step 10, 57 scales): sign sy>0 = 0 deviations, DBL_MIN = 0, 1e-250 = 0; but eps^2 (4.93e-32) = 35 wrong rc, 1e-30 = 35, 1e-16 = 37, SHIPPED 1e-12 = 38, 1e-8 = 39, 1e-50 = 32, 1e-100 = 23, 1e-200 = 7. Every absolute threshold from 1e-8 down through 1e-200 dies; both scale-free repairs survive. DO NOT WIDEN FURTHER: bit-exact covariance holds for every integer k in [-490,+160] (verified exhaustively) and breaks below k ~= -495 where sy itself goes subnormal — past that the test fails for the wrong reason, which is the trap the filing's own conservative range was avoiding. SECONDARY (weaker, and the distinction is load-bearing): scaling f ALONE by c with x held fixed is NOT exactly covariant, because H0 = I is not covariant under it; for that family assert only rc = 0 and ||out_x - x*|| < tol_x for c in 10^{-20..20}, never bit-identity.

defects.guarded_quantity: yy = _opt_dot(y_newest, y_newest, n) = ||g_new - g_old||^2, the SQUARED norm of the newest stored gradient difference. Dimensions [f]^2/[x]^2. Under the similarity family x -> L*x (f fixed, degree-2 objective) it scales as L^2; under a change of the objective's unit f -> c*f it scales as c^2. Note it is NOT the divisor: the divisor is f64_mul(rho_newest, yy) = yy/sy, which is dimensioned [f]/[x]^2 (a curvature) and is scale-INVARIANT in the similarity family.
defects.protects: the division gamma = f64_div(_OPT_F64_ONE, f64_mul(rho_newest, yy)) at line 611, i.e. gamma = sy/yy, L-BFGS's initial-Hessian scaling H0 = gamma*I in the two-loop recursion. Nothing else in the block can fail; the surrounding `if (k > 0)` and line 675's store-time `sy > EPSILON_F64` already guarantee y_newest != 0, so yy == 0 exactly is unreachable except through underflow of the sum of squares.
defects.why: CONFIRMED against the compiled library, not an emulation. Every refutation avenue was checked and failed. (1) Not dimensionless: yy is squared-gradient; measured min yy across a curvature sweep spans 0x3d9bd604b0953453 (6.4e-12) at c=1 down to 0x3c00d0e3917603c3 (2.2e-19) at c=1e-6, and across a similarity sweep from 2^-1018 to 2^262 — an absolute 1e-12 asks the caller's unit. (2) The caller does not normalise: opt_lbfgs takes an arbitrary f/grad pair and never rescales; the objective's unit is entirely the caller's. (3) It is not a convergence tolerance: convergence is decided only by `f64_lt(gnorm, tol)` at the top of the loop; this guard is on the value path and its miss is silent. (4) It is squared against an unsquared epsilon, so the effective cut is ||g_new - g_old|| <= 1e-6. (5) No existing test is affected — checked, not assumed: all four live opt_lbfgs fixtures (hisab.tcyr bowl n=3/m=5/60, Rosenbrock n=2/m=7/2000, x^4+x^2 n=1/m=5/40, modules.tcyr bowl n=2/m=5/200000) run with _P609_SKIP = 0, i.e. the guard NEVER fires in the whole suite, and the repair reproduces them bit-identically (identical rc, identical iteration counts 13/673/8/1, identical out_x, identical out_fmin). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING. (a) Its claim that the cut "is crossed in the ENDGAME of essentially every run with a tight tol, not only in exotic units" is REFUTED by measurement: at unit curvature, n=50, tol swept 1e-8, 1e-9, 1e-10, 1e-11, 1e-12, 1e-13 (up to 284 iterations), skip = 0 in every row and min yy is pinned at 6.4e-12, never below 1e-12. The reason is structural — once line 675 stops storing pairs the ring FREEZES with the last good pair, so yy stops shrinking. This is a units defect, not a generic endgame defect, and the distinction matters because it is why 3574 assertions never saw it. (b) The filing's own covariance sweep (b) does not isolate this guard — see scale_test. The SECONDARY point is upheld and is in fact the better repair: the guard tests yy while the divisor is rho_newest*yy.
defects.fabricates: The gamma scaling is silently skipped, so the two-loop recursion runs with H0 = I instead of H0 = (sy/yy)*I — every search direction wrong by a factor of ~1/curvature, rc unchanged, no error channel. RE-MEASURED ON THE COMPILED LIBRARY (instrumented copy of src/optimize.cyr, real opt_lbfgs, not an emulation), n=50, m=5, f = 1/2*sum_i c*(1+9i/49)*x_i^2, x0 = ones, tol = 1e-9, max_iter = 400, line 675 held scale-free so only this guard varies: c=1e-3 shipped rc=0 in 168 iterations (151 of 167 gamma evaluations skipped) against 27 scale-free; c=1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6 shipped returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE at 400 iterations (385/399, 389/399, 394/399 skipped) where scale-free returns rc=0 in 24, 20, 17. These reproduce the filing's emulated numbers exactly. With line 675 also shipped the damage is still line 609's: c=1e-2 shipped rc=0 in 356 iterations with 335 of 355 skipped, against 49 with only 609 repaired; c=1e-3/1e-4/1e-5 shipped rc=-8 at 400, against rc=0 in 31/26/21 with only 609 repaired. Worst observed silent case: c=1e-2, rc=0 both ways — the caller is told the solve succeeded and is handed a point reached in 7.3x the iterations, with out_x differing in the 8th significant digit.
defects.correct_threshold: Guard the quantity actually divided, at DBL_MIN, and leave the gamma expression alone: `var rho_newest = load64(newest_base + 2 * n * 8); var den = f64_mul(rho_newest, yy); if (f64_lt(den, _OPT_F64_TINY) == 0 && f64_lt(den, F64_INF) == 1) { var gamma = f64_div(_OPT_F64_ONE, den); ... }` with `_OPT_F64_TINY = 0x0010000000000000` (DBL_MIN), matching geo_diff's 2.10.2 rule. No scale constant is needed: den = yy/sy is a curvature ratio and the only thing that can make 1/den fail is den underflowing to zero (gamma = +Inf) or overflowing to +Inf (gamma = 0, H0 = 0, also a fabrication) — hence both ends. PREFER THIS OVER THE FILING'S "compute gamma = sy/yy directly and require yy >= DBL_MIN": sy is NOT stored, only rho = 1/sy, so that form needs a double reciprocal and is measurably NOT bit-preserving — at c=1, n=50, tol=1e-9, where the guard never fires (skip = 0), the sy/yy form already shifts the trajectory (min yy 0x3d9bd604b0953453 shipped vs 0x3d9bd604b09533e9). The product form is bit-identical to shipped everywhere the guard does not fire (verified on all four live suite fixtures and on the full similarity sweep with 675 shipped, k in [-30, +20]), so the repair is provably confined to the fabricating branch. Guarding yy alone is strictly weaker: yy can be comfortably above DBL_MIN while rho_newest*yy underflows to 0 or overflows to +Inf.
defects.scale_test: TWO PARTS. The filing's part (a) is right and I confirm it independently; its part (b) is REPLACED because it does not discriminate. (a) REACHABILITY GATE, asserted first: with line 675 shipped, shipped-609 and repaired-609 are BIT-IDENTICAL at every scale — measured on the n=50 fixture at c=1, x0 = L*ones, tol = L*1e-9, L = 2^k for k in {-30,-20,-10,0,+10,+20}: identical rc, identical iteration counts (81/99/95/106/39/39), skip = 0 throughout, and at k=-30 seen = 0 because 675 stored no pair at all. So ANY covariance sweep run against the shipped tree attributes the whole failure to 675 and proves nothing about 609. This guard must be exercised with 675 already held scale-free (sy >= DBL_MIN), or on a fixture with yy < 1e-12 < sy, which needs curvature < 1 since gamma = sy/yy ~ 1/curvature. (b) COVARIANCE, the replacement, which brackets far more than the filing's k in [-160,160] (that only reaches yy ~ 1e-96 and cannot kill a repair that picked 1e-100 or 1e-200). Use the SIMILARITY family, not the unit-of-f family: for the degree-2 objective f = 1/2*sum_i w_i*x_i^2, set x0 = L*ones and tol = L*1e-9 with f UNCHANGED; every iterate, gradient, Armijo threshold and stored pair is then exactly homogeneous, so out_x/L must be bit-identical. (The unit-of-f family f -> c*f, tol -> c*tol is NOT usable: iteration 0 runs with H0 = I before any pair exists, so the first step is not c-covariant and the trajectory diverges bitwise whatever the guard does — measured.) Sweep k in {-480,-400,-320,-240,-160,-80,0,+80,+160} with 675 scale-free; assert out_x/L and rc identical to k=0. MEASURED: repaired (product guard) gives out_x/L = 0x3def476c4fed43c6 and 39 iterations at ALL NINE k, with min yy spanning 0x005c2ea43d8035a1 (2^-1018, ~1.1e-306) at k=-480 to 0x505c2ea43d8035a6 (2^262, ~1e79) at k=+160 — a 1385-decade band that brackets every absolute threshold on yy strictly above DBL_MIN (1e-12, 2.2e-16, 1e-24, 1e-30, 1e-100, 1e-200, 1e-300). Shipped VIOLATES it with three distinct answers for the same problem in three different units: 0x3c689a6b860cfdc0 in 80 iterations with 79 of 79 gamma evaluations skipped for k <= -80, 0x3dbda224c1a69ea4 in 49 iterations with 21 of 48 skipped at k=0, 0x3def476c4fed43c6 in 39 with 0 skipped for k >= +80. Do NOT extend to k=-500: the objective itself goes subnormal there (f = 0x1537) and both variants degrade, so that row discriminates nothing. Pair this with the reachability fixture that moves rc, since covariance alone only shows a slowdown at c=1: n=50, m=5, f = 1/2*sum_i c*(1+9i/49)*x_i^2, x0 = ones, tol = 1e-9, max_iter = 400, 675 scale-free, c = 1e-4 — shipped returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE at 400, repaired returns rc=0 in 24. A fixture that does not satisfy yy < 1e-12 < sy is worthless: a 2-D spherical quadratic is effectively 1-D, where one stored pair reproduces the exact Newton step whatever H0 is, and all four guard combinations come back bit-identical.

defects.guarded_quantity: sy = _opt_dot(s_k, y_k, n) = (x_new - x) . (g_new - g), the curvature product of the pair about to be written into the history ring. Dimensions [x]*([f]/[x]) = [f] — the units of the OBJECTIVE. Invariant under a change of the variables' unit, linear in the objective's unit; unbounded above and below, and driven toward 0 by convergence itself on any problem whose minimum is 0.
defects.protects: the division f64_div(_OPT_F64_ONE, sy) stored as rho in the ring slot (line 679), and the curvature condition sy > 0 that keeps the implicit L-BFGS Hessian positive definite so the two-loop recursion (lines 565-650) returns a descent direction. rho is subsequently MULTIPLIED by dot products of magnitude ~||s||*||q|| (line 587) and ~||y||*||q|| (line 633), so what the guard must bound is rho relative to those vectors, not rho alone.
defects.why: Every refutation avenue was tested and failed. (1) NOT dimensionless: sy carries the objective's unit; it is a raw dot product of two caller-supplied difference vectors. (2) NO caller normalisation is possible: f, grad, x0 and tol all arrive through function pointers from an arbitrary consumer; nothing in opt_lbfgs rescales them, and the only other absolute constants in the loop (Armijo's alpha0 = 1.0 and c1 = 1e-4) are dimensionless in the length-unit family, which the sweep confirms — with lines 675 and 609 both made scale-free the whole solver is BIT-IDENTICAL at 41 of 41 scales, so 100% of the observed scale dependence is these two guards. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: the convergence test is the separate caller-supplied `f64_lt(gnorm, tol)` at line 554; this one gates a data-structure write and a reciprocal. (4) NO existing test blocks the repair — all four in-tree call sites (hisab.tcyr:1162 bowl3, :1193 Rosenbrock, :1313 x^4+x^2, modules.tcyr:4370 bowl2) were re-run under five guard variants (shipped 1e-12, sy>0, sy>=DBL_MIN, relative, 1e-24) and every variant passes every assertion: rc = HSB_ERR_NONE, |x - x*| < opt_tol6, f* < TOL_1EM12. (5) The scale test DOES discriminate and DOES bracket (numbers below). ⭐ SHARPENING THE FILING'S SEVERITY: the defect is not confined to exotic units — it is already firing AT UNIT SCALE inside this repo's own fixtures, because a problem converging to a zero minimum drives sy below 1e-12 near the solution while sy/(||s||*||y||) stays O(1). Measured at k=0: in-tree bowl3 rejects 3 of 11 curvature pairs (13 iterations vs 11); Rosenbrock rejects 1 of 34; the n=50 diagonal bowl rejects 12 of 39 and takes 106 iterations where the scale-free guard takes 39 — 2.7x, at unit scale, with no change of units at all. The suite passes only because max_iter is ~3x the measured count, which is exactly the margin hisab.tcyr:1105 says is there to catch a solver "degraded to plain steepest descent".
defects.fabricates: The pair is not stored, so k never increments; with k = 0 the two-loop recursion is a no-op, d = -g, and L-BFGS is EXACTLY steepest descent — the advertised algorithm silently deleted and reported through the ordinary NO_CONVERGENCE path, indistinguishable from a hard problem, with out_x written anyway. Measured on fixture (i) (2-D bowl, m=8, tol_L = L*1e-8, max_iter 200), boundary scanned at every integer k: k <= -23 returns rc = -1 at 200 iterations having stored 0-2 pairs, with x0/L = +1.19e-2 against a converged -1.25e-11; k >= -13 returns rc = 0 in 6 iterations. ⚠ CORRECTING THE FILING'S OWN MEASUREMENT: on fixture (ii) (n=50) the shipped guard never returns rc = -1 in my run — it returns rc = 0 at 39/81/90/106 iterations depending on scale (106 at k=0, 39 at large |k|), NOT "rc -1 / 400 iters at k <= -10, 356 at k=0, 32 at k >= 10". The n >> m damage there is a silent 2.7x iteration inflation, not a NO_CONVERGENCE, so a scale test that asserts only rc would MISS it on that fixture.
defects.correct_threshold: PRIMARY: the dimensionless relative curvature test sy >= c * ||s_k|| * ||y_k|| with c a machine-epsilon-scale cosine tolerance (both norms already available via _opt_norm), which is scale-free AND is the only form that bounds rho relative to the dot products it multiplies at lines 587 and 633. MINIMUM ACCEPTABLE: the sign test sy > 0 together with sy >= DBL_MIN for the reciprocal. ⚠ SHARPENING: the bare sign test is scale-free but NOT sufficient — measured, a pair with sy = 1e-300 at ||s|| = ||y|| = 1 (near-orthogonal, i.e. catastrophic cancellation in _opt_dot, not smallness of scale) gives rho = 1e300, ai = 1e300, and beta = -inf inside the second loop, poisoning q and hence x; only the relative form rejects it. Never an absolute number. The same repair must be applied in the same change to line 609 (yy = y.y, units [f]^2/[x]^2, equally absolute) and to the identical guard at line 442 in opt_bfgs.
defects.scale_test: Similarity family, bit-exact: f_L(u) = L^2*f_1(u/L), grad_L(u) = L*grad_1(u/L), x0_L = L*x0_1, tol_L = L*tol_1, L = 2^k. L-BFGS with H0 = I is exactly covariant under it (verified: 0 of 41 points deviate once both guards are scale-free), so assert ALL THREE of rc identical, ITERATION COUNT identical, and out_x/L BIT-IDENTICAL to the k=0 result — the iteration count and bit-identity are load-bearing, because on fixture (ii) rc alone does not discriminate. ⚠ THE TEST IS JOINT OVER LINES 675 AND 609, measured: repairing 675 alone to sy > 0 while line 609 keeps EPSILON_F64 still deviates at 6 of 17 points on (i) and 10 of 11 on (ii), so a 675-only patch fails this sweep and both must land together. Fixtures: (i) f_1 = 1/2(x0^2 + 100*x1^2), x0_1 = (1,1), tol_1 = 1e-8, m = 8, max_iter = 200; (ii) n = 50, m = 5, f_1 = 1/2*sum_i (1 + 9i/49)*x_i^2, x0_1 = all ones, tol_1 = 1e-9, max_iter = 400 — the n >> m case. Both f_1 are degree-2 homogeneous, so f_L is the SAME function and the sweep is literally a change of the length unit. BRACKETING, measured on (i) over k in [-160,160] step 8 (41 points; sy = L^2*sy_1 spans ~1e-96..1e96): shipped 1e-12 deviates at 19/41, a repair to 1e-16 at 18/41, to eps^2 = 1e-24 at 17/41, to 1e-50 at 11/41 — every absolute repair fails — while sy>=DBL_MIN and the relative form deviate at 0/41. On (ii) over k in [-160,160] step 16 (21 points): shipped 20/21, eps^2 10/21, sign+DBL_MIN 0/21, relative 0/21. DBL_MIN cannot be bracketed without the objective itself underflowing, which is why it is the correct floor. ADD A UNIT-SCALE ASSERTION TOO (k = 0, no scaling), because the defect fires there: assert the stored-pair count equals the accepted-step count on the in-tree bowl3 fixture — shipped stores 8 of 11 and the repair stores 11.

defects.guarded_quantity: inv_mass = ColContact_inv_mass_a(c) + ColContact_inv_mass_b(c) — the sum of the two bodies' inverse masses, read verbatim out of the ColContact struct. Dimensions mass^-1. Not dimensionless, not bounded, not normalised anywhere: contact_new / contact_new_fric (collision_core.cyr:236-259) store both fields with no clamp, no validation and no scaling, and the module header declares no unit convention for them.
defects.protects: Two divisions by inv_mass and nothing else: line 357 `f64_div(f64_sub(v_n_eff, v_bias), inv_mass)` (normal impulse Δλ) and line 403 `f64_div(v_t_eff, inv_mass)` (tangential update). Note the sibling guard at line 397, `f64_gt(fric, EPSILON_F64)`, is on the Coulomb coefficient — genuinely dimensionless and bounded — and is CORRECT. The same constant is used correctly 78 lines later, so :319 is a mis-application, not a house convention.
defects.why: CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT; every refutation avenue was tried and each failed against the tree. (1) Not dimensionless/bounded: inv_mass is 1/mass, caller-supplied. (2) No caller normalises — `sequential_impulse` has ZERO in-tree callers (grep over src/, examples/, dist/: only its own definition), so the caller is a consumer and the constructor validates nothing, which makes the "in practice it is O(1)" defence unavailable. (3) Not a convergence tolerance — the convergence parameter is `iterations`, and the function's own comments prove the solver is idempotent after one sweep (λ = (1+e)·pen/inv_mass); :319 is a per-contact entry predicate sitting directly on top of two divisions. (4) Not a behaviour-preserving repair problem: I copied collision_core.cyr to scratch, changed :319 to `f64_lt(inv_mass, F64_TINY)`, and ran ALL FIVE suites against the patched module — 1827 + 776 + 233 + 416 + 359 = 3611 assertions, 0 failed (baseline on the unpatched tree is identical). Every fixture in the tree uses inv_mass ∈ {0, 1.0, 2.0}; the both-static case (modules.tcyr:5266, inv_mass = 0) still skips, because 0 < DBL_MIN. (5) The scale test discriminates — measured, see scale_test. ⚠ ONE CORRECTION TO THE FILING'S OWN ARITHMETIC: micrograms do NOT trip it. The guard fires when total inv_mass < 1e-12, i.e. when the effective mass exceeds 1e12 in whatever unit the caller chose; two 1000 kg bodies give 2e-3 kg^-1, 2e-9 µg^-1 (safe), 2e-12 ng^-1 (still safe, 2e-12 > 1e-12), and 2e-18 pg^-1 (fires). The claim is unchanged and is now exact: the same physical pair silently stops separating once the caller expresses mass in nanograms or finer — measured first failure at inv_mass = 2^-40 = 9.0949e-13 kg^-1.
defects.fabricates: The whole contact branch is skipped, so both output slots keep the zeros the entry loop wrote: normal impulse exactly +0.0 and friction impulse exactly +0.0, returned with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE (0) and no diagnostic. MEASURED on the shipped binary: over k = 0…1000 (inv_mass = 2^-k, pen = 1.0, e = 0, µ = 0), 961 of 1001 configurations returned bit-exact 0.0 with rc = 0, first at k = 40; the correct λ there is 2^40 = 1.0995e12, a perfectly finite double. A heavy-but-finite contact therefore never separates and the bodies interpenetrate freely, and the output is bit-identical to the correct static-static result, so no caller can distinguish the two.
defects.correct_threshold: `f64_lt(inv_mass, F64_TINY)` — error.cyr:45, DBL_MIN, already in scope (error.cyr is a declared requirement of collision_core.cyr; the patched build compiles and all 3611 assertions pass). It is simultaneously the divide guard and the physical predicate, rejects negative inv_mass exactly as the current form does, and needs no scale chosen for it. ⚠ SHARPENED — there are TWO scale-free candidates, not one, and the filing's own `why` argues for the other: `f64_le(inv_mass, _COL_F64_ZERO)` ("both static == inv_mass EXACTLY 0"). They are NOT interchangeable, measured: over k = 1024…1073 (inv_mass subnormal) the exact-zero form lets the division run and returns +Inf in 50 of 50 configurations — a fabricated infinite impulse, strictly worse than the zero it replaces — while F64_TINY returns the documented static-skip 0.0. F64_TINY is therefore the repair, at a measured cost of exactly ONE over-conservative k: at k = 1023, λ = 2^1023 is finite and representable yet F64_TINY skips. That is the deliberate price of the repo's DBL_MIN rule and it errs toward the documented value rather than toward +Inf; it should be stated in the comment rather than left for the next reader to rediscover.
defects.scale_test: MASS-UNIT COVARIANCE OF THE SOLVED IMPULSE, extended past the filing's range. Fixture: pen = 1.0, restitution = 0, friction = 0, tangent_vel = 0, inv_mass_a = inv_mass_b = 2^-(k+1) so inv_mass = 2^-k exactly; call `sequential_impulse(v, 1, 1, out)`. Closed form λ = pen/inv_mass = 2^k, exact in binary, so every assertion is a bit-compare. Powers of two, not ten. THREE CLAUSES, asserted separately (a zeroed run makes any ratio-of-two-runs read "consistent"): (a) rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and the normal slot is STRICTLY POSITIVE — never the fabricated 0.0; (b) λ(k) == 2^k bit-for-bit; (c) λ(k) is FINITE — never +Inf. ⚠ SWEEP k = 0 … 1074, not 0 … 1000. MEASURED discrimination on this tree (first k at which clause (a)/(b) fails): shipped EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 → k = 40; a "tightened" 1e-15 → k = 50; a loosened 1e-9 → k = 30; EPSILON_F64² = 1e-24 → k = 80; F64_TINY → never over 0…1000 (0 of 1001 failures). So a 12-decade sweep kills the shipped constant and nothing else, exactly as 2.11.1's quaternion sweep did. ⛔ THE FILING'S OWN 0…1000 RANGE IS STILL TOO SHORT: it cannot separate F64_TINY from `f64_le(inv_mass, 0)` — measured identical over k = 0…1022 — and they diverge in the subnormal band, where exact-zero returns +Inf for k = 1024…1073 (50 of 50) and F64_TINY returns 0.0. Clause (c) over k ≥ 1023 is the only thing that discriminates them, so the sweep must reach 1074. CONTROL: k = 0 … −60 (inv_mass growing, λ shrinking) must pass all three clauses ON THE SHIPPED CODE — measured 0 of 61 failures, which proves the positive-k failures are the threshold and not overflow, the fixture, or the solver's algebra. Probes and patched module copies under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-macro-Repos-hisab/68915bf3-8a70-4292-b984-a0be0a4996e8/scratchpad/eps/refute/ (src/ untouched). ⚠ My own first probe was wrong before the code was: the subnormal constructor shifted by a NEGATIVE amount and reported first_inf = 1022 for the exact-zero variant; the numbers above are from the corrected build.

defects.guarded_quantity: |ax - bx| — the absolute difference of two caller-supplied HVec2 x-coordinates. Dimensions: LENGTH, in whatever unit the caller's points carry; metres → millimetres multiplies it by 1000. Compared against EPSILON_F64, verified to decode to exactly 1e-12 (src/error.cyr:26, 0x3D719799812DEA11).
defects.protects: No arithmetic operation — no division, no sqrt, no domain. It is the equality leg of an ORDERING PREDICATE: it suppresses the "a is greater" answer when the two x's are within 1e-12, so the (x, then y) sort in `_col_sort_indices_by_xy` (heapsort, :511) falls through to the y tie-break at :445. The comment at :435 states its only rationale outright — bug-compatibility with the pre-2.6.15 insertion sort — never that 1e-12 is right for any caller's unit.
defects.why: Every refutation route was tried against the code and closed by measurement (simulation transliterated line-for-line from :427-:630 — comparator, sift-down, heapsort, both hull passes, `c <= +0` pop — checked against an exact-Fraction reference hull). (1) NOT dimensionless/bounded: the operand is a raw coordinate difference. (2) NO caller normalisation: `convex_hull_2d` (:533) is a public entry point that validates only `points == 0` and `n > vec_len(points)`, then sorts the caller's vec unchanged; there is no bbox pass, no scaling, and the private sort is additionally called directly by tests/modules.tcyr:6202. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: the guard sits in a comparator and protects no operation. (4) The proposed exact comparison breaks NO existing test — all seven fixtures in tests/*.tcyr reproduce identically (square+interior 4, triangle 3, collinear 2, duplicate corner 4, ab_line 2, ab_same 6-coincident 2, the 2000-point fingerprint 17, zero inversions, permutation intact); the smallest nonzero x-gap in the 2000-point fixture is 1.0, i.e. 1e12x the band, so the band is provably inert across the entire suite. ⭐ THE FILING'S SEVERITY MECHANISM (1) IS WRONG AND THE REAL ONE IS WORSE. "Whole set inside a 1e-12 box → sorted purely by y → not a valid input to the monotone chain" does not hold: 300/300 random 12-point sets inside a 1e-13 box returned a hull that was convex, CCW and set-identical to the exact reference — sorting purely by y is just the monotone chain with the axes swapped, which is still correct. The damage is in the INTERMEDIATE regime, and it is present AT UNIT SCALE: with x-values whose gaps straddle the band, the shipped code returned a hull with spurious interior vertices in 1788/4000 trials and a REPEATED INDEX in 448/4000, at coordinates in [0,1] (five generators, 20,000 trials; the exact comparator scored 0 nonconvex / 0 missing / 0 spurious / 0 duplicate on every one — the control is clean). Minimal reproducer, all coordinates exactly representable: (0,0), (1,0), (0.5+2^-41, 0.25), (0.5, 0.25) — 2^-41 = 4.547e-13 < 1e-12 — where `convex_hull_2d(pts, 4)` returns FIVE indices [0,2,3,1,2] for four points, index 2 twice, and the polygon is not convex; the exact comparator returns [0,1,2,3]. ⚠ The module's own sort test cannot ever see this: tests/modules.tcyr:6207 asserts "zero inversions" using `_col_xy_greater` as its own oracle — measured 0 inversions on the broken order above. The filing's intransitivity claim is confirmed and is scale-independent: for {(0,2),(6e-13,1),(1.2e-12,0)} all SIX input permutations come out non-lexicographic ([2,1,0], [0,2,1], [1,0,2]).
defects.fabricates: Returns 0 ("not greater") for a point whose x IS strictly greater, and there is no error channel — the function returns only a vec. Measured, the fabrication is stronger than "a plausible polygon": on the 4-point unit-scale fixture the public `convex_hull_2d` returns a vec of FIVE indices for FOUR input points with one index REPEATED and a non-convex, self-touching outline; at 60% of near-tie configurations it returns a hull containing strictly interior points. A caller that shoelaces or renders it gets a wrong area and a degenerate edge. Note the one cheap consequence: `vec_len(result) > n` and a repeated index are both scale-free, tolerance-free detectable — the output is malformed, not merely inaccurate.
defects.correct_threshold: No epsilon — an exact comparison. The x leg becomes `if (f64_gt(ax, bx) == 1) { return 1; }` and the tie-break tests exact equality (`f64_eq(ax, bx)`). Exact lexicographic order is total, transitive and scale-free BY CONSTRUCTION. ⛔ Explicitly reject the tempting repair: `_GEO_F64_TINY` = DBL_MIN, which 2.10.2 installed as this repo's standing rule for divide guards, is WRONG here and is measurably the most dangerous choice — it is a band, so it is still intransitive and still order-dependent, and it evades the filing's own scale sweep entirely (see scale_test). The 2.10.2 rule is "guard exactly what makes the DIVISION fail"; this guard protects no division, so the right amount of guard is none. If near-coincident points genuinely must be merged, that is a caller-supplied tolerance in the caller's units and belongs in the signature.
defects.scale_test: Three legs; the filing's single sweep is necessary but NOT sufficient — measured, it fails to bracket the likeliest repair. (A) PRIMARY, arithmetic-free — SPACING SWEEP ON THE SORT. For j = -1074..0, δ = 2^j, feed {(0,2), (δ,1), (2δ,0)} to `_col_sort_indices_by_xy` and assert the index order is exactly [0,1,2]. No cross products, so no underflow confound, and it fails at k=0 scale. Measured wrong-order decades: shipped 1e-12 → 1035/1075 (largest δ that fools it 2^-40); 1e-15 → 1025; 1e-9 → 1045; 1e-24 → 995; **DBL_MIN → 52 (largest δ 2^-1023)**; exact → 0. This is the ONLY leg that brackets a DBL_MIN band. (B) MALFORMED-OUTPUT ASSERTION on the public entry point, scale-free and tolerance-free: pts = (0,0), (1,0), (0.5 + 2^-41, 0.25), (0.5, 0.25); assert `vec_len(convex_hull_2d(pts,4)) == 4` and that no index repeats. Shipped returns [0,2,3,1,2]. Assert "no repeated index" on every existing hull test too — it is the cheapest tree-wide canary. (C) COORDINATE-UNIT COVARIANCE, corrected from the filing. Keep the ±2^k fixture and the bit-identical-indices invariant, but: sweep k = -500..0 ONLY, and run the exact comparator over the same sweep as the control that ESTABLISHES the window — measured, the exact comparator itself holds for k ≥ -537 and fails at k ≤ -538 from cross-product underflow, so the filing's "sweep ±500" is inside the valid window by 37 steps by luck, and a sweep to ±800 would fail the CORRECT code. ⚠ The filing's k>0 half is NOT a valid arithmetic-health control: it passes on shipped code all the way to k = +900, where every cross product has overflowed to inf. ⚠ Its adversarial pair (0,10)/(δ,0) is decorative — deleting it moves the shipped break from k = -37 to k = -39 (464 vs 462 failing k), because that point never reaches the hull; the discrimination comes from the interior cluster. ⚠ Its predicted break points are wrong: measured 1e-12 → k=-37, 1e-15 → -47, 1e-9 → -27, 1e-24 → -77 (not -0/-10/+10/-40), and DBL_MIN and any band below 2^-1023 → NO BREAK AT ALL, indistinguishable from exact. Leg (C) alone would sign off a DBL_MIN repair.

defects.guarded_quantity: |ax - bx|, the absolute difference of two raw caller x-coordinates read straight out of HVec2 (HVec2_x(pa), HVec2_x(pb)) with no normalisation anywhere on the path. Dimensions LENGTH, degree 1 in the caller's units, unbounded. Compared against EPSILON_F64 = 0x3D719799812DEA11 = 1e-12 (src/error.cyr:26, verified unchanged on the live tree). This is the tie-break leg: "if the x's are within 1e-12, decide the order by y instead."
defects.protects: No arithmetic operation — no division, no sqrt, no acos, no iteration. It selects which coordinate is the sort key for the pair. The only thing it can be said to protect is a policy of treating near-equal x as equal, and that policy is unimplementable at ANY threshold: a band |ax-bx| < e is not transitive, so it cannot be an equality. Measured 3-cycle at unit scale with the shipped constant: a=(0,10), b=(6e-13,5), c=(1.2e-12,0) gives greater(a,b)=1, greater(b,c)=1, greater(c,a)=1. Line 443 is the other half of the same predicate; the two share ONE constant, so they are consistent today and must be repaired together.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE ROUTES; ALL FIVE ARE DEAD, MEASURED. (1) Not dimensionless/bounded: |Δx| is a raw coordinate difference, degree 1 in caller units. (2) No caller normalisation: `grep -rn '_col_xy_greater|_col_sort_indices_by_xy' src/` gives exactly one caller chain — _col_sift_down -> _col_sort_indices_by_xy -> convex_hull_2d:562 — and convex_hull_2d does no bounding-box scaling; it is a public entry point on raw caller coordinates. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: nothing iterates or divides here. (4) The proposed exact-equality repair does NOT break any existing test — MEASURED, not assumed: I applied it to a copy of the live tree (`if (f64_gt(ax,bx)==1) { return 1; } if (f64_lt(ax,bx)==0) { y tie-break }`) and all five suites produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output (hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776 = 3611 assertions, 0 failures on both sides, `diff` clean on all five). The suites are simply blind to this guard: no fixture anywhere has an x-gap inside the band. (5) The scale test does discriminate — see scale_test. ⛔ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL FINDING. (a) Its partial-repair argument is mis-derived: TIGHTENING 443 does not produce a "neither greater nor x-equal" gap, it breaks ANTISYMMETRY — measured with 443 at 1e-15 and 445 at 1e-12, a=(5e-13,0) vs b=(0,5) gives greater(a,b)=1 AND greater(b,a)=1. The no-tie-break gap it describes comes from WIDENING 443 (443 at 1e-9, 445 at 1e-12: a=(1e-10,0) vs b=(0,5) returns 0 in both directions for a strictly greater point). (b) The usual remedy for this verdict — a relative band, |Δx| < e*(|ax|+|bx|) — DOES NOT REPAIR THIS SITE. Any band, absolute or relative, is intransitive and yields the same cyclic comparator; making it scale-covariant only moves which unit system is broken. Exact equality is the only repair, and that is why the verdict understates the class even while the label is right: the scale dependence is real (a length against a constant, the caller's unit picks the regime) but it is a symptom, and the disease is a band used as an equivalence relation inside an ordering predicate.
defects.fabricates: Confirmed and WORSE than claimed, measured on the compiled library (not simulated) via a probe built against a pristine copy of the tree. Single comparison: greater((0,10),(1e-13,0)) = 1, i.e. "greater" for the point with the strictly SMALLER x. Escaping into the public API at UNIT SCALE — points {(0,10), (5e-13,5), (1.2e-12,0), (1,0), (1,10)}, strictly convex, no three collinear, true hull all 5 vertices — convex_hull_2d returns a well-formed CCW polygon that DROPS a true extreme point and encloses 25% less area: 2A = 14.999999999994 (bits 4624633867356074702) where the truth is 19.999999999988 (bits 4626322717216338638). rc-free, no diagnostic, correct winding, correct vec type. At every scale k <= 0 it additionally returns a ROTATION of the correct hull (60 of 121 k in the probe's sweep) — a distinct, milder failure that the area assertion cannot see, which is why the test needs both assertions. And because the comparator is cyclic (3-cycle above), the heapsort's output is not merely "y-major inside the band" — it is an arbitrary permutation, so no bound on the hull error can be argued from the band width.
defects.correct_threshold: Exact equality, in FLOAT comparison semantics — NOT an i64 bit compare. The tie-break leg fires only when neither f64_lt(ax,bx) nor f64_gt(ax,bx) holds; line 443 becomes an unconditional `if (f64_gt(ax,bx) == 1) { return 1; }`. Together the two legs are then the exact lexicographic order: total, transitive, antisymmetric, scale-free, and needing no constant at all — the strongest form of "guard exactly what makes the operation fail and nothing more", since nothing here can fail. ⚠ The original wording "ax == bx bit-exactly" is a hazard, not a nit: this repo already recorded (2.13.0) that an antiparallel cross product returns NEGATIVE ZERO, and a raw i64 compare of -0.0 against +0.0 is false while f64_lt/f64_gt are both false — so a bit compare silently DROPS the y tie-break for such a pair and leaves their order to heapsort's internal swap sequence rather than to the specification. I could not turn that into a differing hull in two attempts, so it is a specification defect in the repair wording, not a demonstrated second bug. Verified: the f64-semantics form above passes the full covariance probe 4/4 and leaves all 3611 existing assertions byte-identical.
defects.scale_test: SHARPENED, and every number below is measured — the original sweep works but its stated control is wrong and its assertion is too weak. FIXTURE (strictly convex, so the "it's a collinear degenerate" objection cannot be raised): P(s) = {(0,10s), (5e-13*s, 5s), (1.2e-12*s, 0), (s,0), (s,10s)}, true hull = all 5 indices. ASSERT TWO scale-invariants, both taken against a REFERENCE COMPUTED AT k = +16, never a hand-written constant: (a) 2A/s^2 bit-identical at every k, (b) hull length and first hull index identical at every k. ⚠ My first probe hand-wrote the expected area as 20 and FAILED ON CORRECT CODE — the true value is 19.999999999988. Check the probe before believing the probe. SWEEP k = -500..+500 CONTIGUOUSLY, s = 2^k (powers of two, so scaling is exact and the assertions are bit-exact with no tolerance; the repo's usual 1e-k decades would force one). CONTIGUITY IS LOAD-BEARING: each candidate threshold produces a wrong AREA at exactly ONE k — shipped 1e-12 at k=0, tightened 1e-15 at k=-10, widened 1e-9 at k=+10, squared 1e-24 at k=-40 — because the catastrophic regime is the single decade where the band SPLITS the point set, not the decades where it swallows it whole; a sparse sweep {-3,0,+3} kills one mutant of four. The index-sequence assertion has the wide window (shipped wrong for all k <= 0, squared 1e-24 for k <= -39) and is what kills the deep mutants; the area assertion is what proves the failure is a genuinely wrong hull rather than a benign rotation. Both are required. ⛔ "k > 0 as the control" IS WRONG: the widened-1e-9 mutant is still wrong at k = +10, and on a pair-only fixture the SHIPPED constant is still wrong through k = +3. The control must sit above the widest candidate band — k >= +14 on this fixture. defects.protects: No arithmetic operation — no division, no sqrt, no domain restriction. It is a convexity/degeneracy CLASSIFICATION band: a collinear (zero-area) vertex must not be called strictly convex and clipped as a sliver ear. Verified as stated — nothing downstream of the comparison divides by or roots `cross`.
defects.why: I could not refute it on any of the five grounds, and each attempt was measured on the real shipped library (cycc 6.6.2), not argued. (1) NOT dimensionless: `cross` is an area, so scaling coordinates by 2^k moves it by exactly 2^2k. Every candidate constant breaks precisely where 2^2k crosses it — measured first-failing k: 1e-9 → −15, shipped 1e-12 → −20, 1e-15 → −25, 1e-24 → −40, 1e-300 → −499, DBL_MIN → −511. That is dimensional dependence, demonstrated, not asserted. (2) NO caller normalisation: `triangulate_polygon` is a public bundle entry point; vertices go from `vec_get` straight into the determinant, and the only in-tree callers are tests and benchmarks. (3) It IS a classification band rather than a divide guard, exactly as filed — but that framing does not rescue an absolute constant applied to an area; the band is the whole failure mechanism. (4) THE REPAIR BREAKS NOTHING — checked, not assumed: with the exact sign test installed at all four sites (mutant-installed proof: 4 grep hits) all five shipped suites pass 3611/3611 (hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776), and the relative-determinant-bound variant also passes 3611/3611. Every triangulate fixture (tp_q/tp_c/tp_h/tp_u/tp_w/tp_l/tpc/tpd, abuse ab_line/ab_same) uses small-INTEGER coordinates, so every `cross` is an exact integer — 0 or |cross| ≥ 1 — and 1e-12 is behaviourally identical to 0 on all of them; index sequences are identical too. The shipped suite therefore cannot discriminate the defect from the fix. (5) The scale test DOES discriminate: 2886 of 3006 assertions fail on shipped code, and the k>0 half passes 3006/3006 on shipped code, so the failure is the threshold and not the fixture, the winding or overflow. SEVERITY, real code, only the caller's unit changed on one fixed 12-gon: 6 m wide → 30/30 complete; 6 mm → 30/30; 6 MICRONS → 9/30; 6 nm → 0/30; 6 km → 30/30. ⚠ The one thing I did refute is the finding's own bracketing claim — see scale_test.
defects.fabricates: Not a plausible NUMBER — a plausible DIAGNOSIS, which is why it is worse than it looks. A strictly convex vertex is classified "not convex", stored as blocked[v] = 1, and re-rejected by the inline ear gate, so `if (ear_found == 0) { return result; }` (:851) fires early and the function returns a SHORT but well-formed index vec: measured 9 of 30 indices for a 6-micron-wide 12-gon, 0 of 30 at 6 nm. Whole triples, no rc, no error channel. The header at :640-653 tells callers to read exactly that signal as "ear clipping is only defined for SIMPLE polygons; a self-intersecting input has no ear decomposition and a short return is the honest answer". So the length channel EXISTS but carries the wrong meaning: a valid, simple, non-self-intersecting polygon is reported as non-simple, bit-identically to a genuinely degenerate one and to the n < 3 convention. A caller doing exactly what the contract instructs is misled.
defects.correct_threshold: The SIGN of the determinant — `f64_gt(cross, _COL_F64_ZERO)` for the CCW branch, `f64_lt(cross, _COL_F64_ZERO)` for the CW branch — at all FOUR sites (:706, :709, :800, :802), which must move together or the :692 contract is broken. There is no arithmetic operation to protect here, so there is no quantity from which a nonzero threshold could be DERIVED, and any nonzero constant is therefore a scale chosen for it. This is already the file's own convention for the identical quantity: `convex_hull_2d` compares `_col_cross2d` against `_COL_F64_ZERO` exactly (:580/:608 → `f64_le(c, _COL_F64_ZERO)`), and `_col_point_in_tri` (:671-673) tests its three determinants against exact zero. Polarity is preserved: cross == 0 stays "not convex", so collinear vertices remain blockers and the deliberate tie handling recorded in issues/archived/2026-08-04-perf-triangulate_polygon.md:260 is untouched. ⚠ Do NOT reach for `_GEO_F64_TINY`/DBL_MIN by analogy with 2.10.2 — that rule was "guard exactly what makes the DIVISION fail", and there is no division here; measured, DBL_MIN is a defect at this site (it breaks at k = −511). If a genuine degeneracy band is ever wanted, the only defensible form is the forward-error bound on the 2×2 determinant, |cross| <= 4·DBL_EPSILON·(|(bx-ax)(cy-ay)| + |(cx-ax)(by-ay)|), which is scale-covariant by construction; I built it and it passes the full sweep in both directions and all 3611 shipped assertions.

defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FAILED, and the verdict is confirmed by measurement rather than by argument. (1) Not dimensionless/bounded: `cross` is 2x an area, degree-2 homogeneous — measured invariance of the whole index sequence under 2^k scaling proves the quantity moves with s^2 while 1e-12 does not. (2) No normalisation: `triangulate_polygon` has NO caller anywhere in src/ (grep: the only hits are the definition at :713, tests/*.tcyr and tests/hisab.bcyr). It is a public leaf entry point consuming raw HVec2 coordinates in whatever units the caller holds. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: no iteration, no division, no domain to clamp — it is a degeneracy dead-band on a sign predicate, which the claim itself concedes. (4) CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED — the proposed exact sign test breaks NO existing test. I modelled triangulate_polygon line-for-line (blocked cache, 2-entry refresh, max_iters bail, boundary-inclusive point-in-tri) and validated the model against every asserted length in the real suite: modules.tcyr:5579/5590/5602/5616/5626/5637/5644 (6, 9, 12, 18, 6, 9, 0), modules.tcyr:6963/6974 (6, <=9 and %3==0), abuse.tcyr:1522-1551 (0,0,0,0,0). Running each fixture at eps=1e-12 and at eps=0 produces BYTE-IDENTICAL index sequences on all nine. Every fixture uses small-integer coordinates whose smallest |cross| is 2 — twelve orders of magnitude above the band — and the two degenerate cases that MUST return 0 (4 collinear vertices, 6 coincident vertices) compute cross == exactly 0.0, which the strict `>` still rejects, so "no ears" survives the repair unchanged. (5) The sweep does discriminate the four named mutants; measured first-bad k on a unit square = -15 (1e-9), -20 (1e-12 shipped), -25 (1e-15), -40 (1e-24), matching the claim's estimates. THE DEFECT IS REALISABLE, MEASURED: a unit square at k = -20 (side 9.5e-7 — a micrometre expressed in metres) returns an EMPTY vec; the CW-wound square fails at the identical k, so line 802 carries it too. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING. (A) Its repair-ordering argument is INVERTED. The filing says leaving 800 banded while repairing 706/709 is "a worse state than the current consistent-but-wrong one". Measured on a 10-point star over k = -10..-29: repairing 706/709 ALONE is a strict NO-OP (identical output to shipped at every k: 15, then 0), while repairing 800 ALONE is a COMPLETE repair (24 at every k) and gives index sequences identical to repairing all four on 400 random star-shaped polygons at unit scale. The asymmetry runs the other way than filed: 706/709 only populate the `blocked` cache, and a banded `blocked` is the CONSERVATIVE error (a near-collinear vertex stays marked blocked and merely earns an extra point-in-triangle test); site 800 is both where the damage is realised and where the repair lands. Repairing all four together is correct hygiene given the comment at 692, but it is not a correctness precondition and the "worse state" claim is refuted. (B) The prescribed sweep span is wrong at both ends — see scale_test.

Use s = 2^k over **k = -530 … +490** (not -500…+500), fixtures = unit square (n=4, expect 6) AND a 10-point star with outer radius 1e6, inner radius 1 (n=10, expect 24), each in BOTH windings; assert the complete index sequence, vec_len == 3*(n-2) exactly, and the summed-area cross-check at every k, with k > 0 as the control. defects.why: NOT REFUTED — all five refutation grounds were tested and failed. (1) NOT BOUNDED: `_col_triangle_area_2x` is a raw 2x-signed-area on unnormalised world coordinates, LENGTH SQUARED; the sibling agent's own new note at `src/error.cyr` says EPSILON_F64 is right only for "a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity — a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]". This is none of those. (2) NO CALLER NORMALISES: `triangulate_polygon` is a public entry point with ZERO in-tree callers (only tests/ and hisab.bcyr), and nothing in its body rescales `vertices`. (3) NOT A CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE: it is an orientation predicate — and the file's own sibling predicate `_col_point_in_tri` (:677-682) tests the IDENTICAL `_col_triangle_area_2x` quantity against `_COL_F64_ZERO` with NO band, so exact-sign is already this file's established convention for this quantity and the ear gate is the outlier. (4) THE PROPOSED REPAIR BREAKS NOTHING — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: exact-sign at all four sites (706/709/800/802) run against every suite gives 416+351+1798+233+776 = 3574 passed / 0 failed, identical to shipped, and at unit scale the star's triangulation is byte-identical (index checksum -6873769297671726784 CCW / 1583088700137086604 CW under both builds). MEASURED on an 8-vertex integer-coordinate concave star scaled by exact powers of two: SHIPPED is clean only on k in [-21, +509]; at k = -22 BOTH windings return 12 of 18 indices and at k <= -23 both return EMPTY, while `total_area`'s exact sign test still identifies the winding correctly — the code knows the ring is CW and then refuses to find an ear in it, exactly as filed. The exact-sign repair widens the clean window to [-538, +509], both new bounds being the FIXTURE's own IEEE underflow/overflow, not the guard. TWO CLAIMS IN THE ORIGINAL FILING ARE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE. (a) "the branch a CCW-only fixture never executes" is FALSE: `tests/modules.tcyr:5620-5627` (`tp_w`, the reversed square, shoelace -8 -> ccw = 0) DOES execute line 802. The gap is not coverage — it is that the repo's only CW fixture sits at one scale where the guard passes by ~12 orders of magnitude. (b) "fails the symmetry assertion at the first negative k" is FALSE: the partial repair (706+800 fixed, 709+802 left) was built and measured — its CW leg is clean down to k = -21 and first deviates at k = -22. Not merely proposed: it is what `_col_point_in_tri` (:677-682) ALREADY does to the same `_col_triangle_area_2x` quantity three functions up in the same file, so the repair makes the two orientation predicates consistent rather than inventing a convention. ALL FOUR SITES MUST MOVE TOGETHER: 706/709 feed the `blocked[]` cache and 800/802 are the ear gate, and the comment at :692-693 makes their agreement an explicit contract ("the SAME predicate and the SAME EPSILON_F64 threshold ... so 'not convex here' is exactly 'would be rejected as an ear tip there'"), so repairing the gate without the cache desyncs that contract. defects.scale_test: Power-of-two scaling of a fixed integer-coordinate concave fixture, so every multiply and subtract is EXACT and the only thing that changes across k is the comparison against the absolute constant. Reference fixture (measured): the 8-vertex CCW star (10,0),(2,2),(0,10),(-2,2),(-10,0),(-2,-2),(0,-10),(2,-2), n = 8, expected 3*(n-2) = 18 indices; run it FORWARD and REVERSED (the reversed ring is CW, ccw = 0, and is the only thing that reaches line 802). THE PLAIN LENGTH ASSERTION ON THE REVERSED RING IS THE DISCRIMINATOR — the winding-symmetry assertion is optional garnish; what is load-bearing is that the sweep runs the CW ring AT ALL, which `tp_w` at `tests/modules.tcyr:5625` does not, being pinned at one scale. MEASURED BRACKETING on this fixture (last clean k): eps 1e-6 -> -11, 1e-9 -> -16, 1e-12 (shipped) -> -21, 1e-15 -> -26, 1e-24 -> -41; exact sign -> -538. So k down to about -200 brackets every absolute threshold a repair could plausibly pick, and k = 0 or any k > 0 is the control. DO NOT HARDCODE +-500: it is over-wide AND fixture-dependently UNSAFE. The exact predicate itself stops being clean below k = -538 for THIS fixture (the 2x-area products go subnormal) and above k = +509 (they overflow to Inf, and NaN sign tests in `_col_point_in_tri` then change the triangulation) — so on a fixture with larger coordinates or a smaller minimum ear area, a hardcoded +-500 sweep would fail the "exact index sequence at every k" assertion ON THE CORRECT REPAIR and report a false alarm. Derive the bounds from the fixture: k_min = ceil((-1074 - log2(cross_min))/2) + margin, k_max = floor((1023 - log2(max(|cross|_max, |total_area|_max)))/2) - margin. The model was verified against the measurements — this fixture's cross_min is 4, predicting the 1e-12 break at 4*2^(2k) <= 1e-12 -> k = -21 (measured -21) and the exact-predicate floor at 4*2^(2k) >= 2^-1074 -> k = -538 (measured -538).

defects.why: Refutation attempted on all five avenues; all failed under measurement (probes in scratchpad/eps/refute/). (1) DIMENSIONLESS-AND-BOUNDED is true but insufficient, and it is the strongest defence available because error.cyr:41-45 literally lists "a parameter in [0,1]" as EPSILON_F64's territory — the clause's operative qualifier, however, is "where an absolute tolerance MEANS something". Measured: a DBL_MIN-guarded variant recovered the straight colour (1.0, 2.0, 4.0) BIT-EXACTLY on 1023 of 1023 rows spanning j = 0..1022, i.e. 307 decades. The recovered colour is degree 0 in the guarded quantity; the guard makes it depend on that quantity's absolute magnitude. F64_TINY's own first clause at error.cyr:39-41 matches this site verbatim: the guard protects a DIVISION and the only thing that can actually fail is a zero or subnormal denominator. (2) The graphics-conventional defence — small alpha amplifies quantisation noise, the reason real compositors floor alpha at ~1/255 — has NO basis in this API: grep of color.cyr for 255 / u8 / any quantised path returns nothing, every channel is f64, and f64's RELATIVE precision is scale-free, so no amplification exists. 1e-12 is also not any conventional coverage floor; it is simply the value of EPSILON_F64, which is evidence it was reached for rather than chosen. (3) CALLER NORMALISES: refuted — unpremultiply_alpha has zero call sites in src/; it is a leaf public entry point, and the file's OWN composite_src_in/composite_dst_in drive a downward multiplicatively. (4) CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE: no. (5) BREAKS A PASSING TEST: checked, not assumed — under the repair all four pinned sites stay green (abuse.tcyr:2226, 2228; modules.tcyr:7311, 7312), because the suites pin only a == 0 (modules.tcyr:7313 comment: "a == 0 is the documented guard") and the dyadic a = 0.5 round-trip. The one refutation avenue that partly landed was the scale_test, and it sharpens rather than overturns: measured, an exact-zero-only repair ALSO scores 1023/1023 on the original LEG A, so that sweep did not bracket the low side; low-side rows are now added. defects.guarded_quantity: |ndc| — a reverse-Z normalised device depth. Dimensionless, in (0,1]. Confirmed against this repo's own projection: m4_perspective_reverse_z (src/mat4.cyr:342) builds from columns c2 = (0,0,0,-1) and c3 = (0,0,near,0), so for M*v = c0*vx + c1*vy + c2*vz + c3*vw we get clip.z = near and clip.w = -z_view, hence ndc = near/|z_view|. It is the RECIPROCAL of the frustum's depth dynamic range |z|/near, and the projection has NO far plane (nothing in the matrix mentions one), so ndc has no positive lower bound.
defects.protects: The division f64_div(near, ndc) on the next line — the only operation in the function. Not an iteration, not a convergence loop, not a normalisation: a single divide with the guarded value as the denominator.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED ON ALL FIVE ROUTES; every claim below is measured, not argued (probe: scratchpad/eps/refute/probe.tcyr, run via `cyrius test` against the real included src/color.cyr on 6.6.2). (1) "Dimensionless/bounded, so an absolute epsilon is correct" is the strongest counter and it has a written basis in this repo: src/error.cyr:28's own comment carves out exactly this case — "EPSILON_F64 remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity — a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, A PARAMETER IN [0,1] — where an absolute tolerance means something." ndc IS a parameter in [0,1]. The carve-out still does not apply, because its stated condition is that the absolute tolerance MEAN something, i.e. that values far below 1 be indistinguishable from 0 downstream. Under a reciprocal map they are the opposite of indistinguishable: near/1e-13 and near/1e-12 differ by 10x, both are computed to 0.5 ulp, and the whole reason reverse-Z exists is to concentrate float precision exactly where ndc -> 0. The quantity is bounded on the wrong end — the interesting end is open. Contrast the carve-out's own examples: a cosine of 1e-13 really is 1e-13 rad from perpendicular and nothing downstream can tell. (2) "The caller normalises" — there is no caller. `grep -rn reverse_z src/ tests/ examples/` returns only the definition, m4_perspective_reverse_z, and four test lines. It is a public entry point taking a raw f64. (3) "Convergence tolerance" — one division, no loop. (4) "The repair breaks a passing test" — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: I replayed abuse.tcyr:2270, modules.tcyr:7343 and modules.tcyr:7344 verbatim against both candidate repairs; all six assertions PASS (0 < F64_TINY is true and ndc == 0 is true, so the pinned ndc=0 -> 0 behaviour is untouched, and ndc=0.5 -> 2 never reaches the guard). near=0, ndc=0 also stays 0 under both — no new 0/0 NaN. (5) "The scale test doesn't discriminate" — it does: shipped code fails 983 of 1023 rows with first-failing j = 40, the exact signature of 1e-12 (2^-39 = 1.819e-12 passes, 2^-40 = 9.095e-13 fires). EPSILON_F64 = 0x3D719799812DEA11 = 1e-12 exactly (src/error.cyr:25). The label is precise and deliberately narrow: ndc does NOT move under a unit change — near and |z| scale together — and LEG B measured that (m/mm/um give bit-identical ndc = 1e-4 and results 1e3/1e6/1e9, exactly 1000x apart, PASSING on shipped code). What ndc scales with is the frustum's depth dynamic range: the guard fires iff |z| > 1e12 * near, and an infinite-far reverse-Z projection is the technique that exists specifically for ranges that large, so it fires hardest in the regime the function was written for. The division itself fails at nothing in that window; near/0 = +Inf is arguably the correct linear depth for an infinite far plane, and near > 0 means 0/0 never arises. Both governing documents state the intended guard as exactly zero — docs/audit/2026-04-15.md H6 ("Fix: Guard ndc==0", naming color.cyr:157, which this line implements) and docs/development/threat-model.md:42 ("Division by ndc=0 | Returns 0") — so the 1e-12 window is undocumented drift from the recorded fix. NEW: an f32 reverse-Z depth buffer, the normal source of this input, represents ndc down to 1.175e-38 normal (1.4e-45 subnormal) with a full 24-bit mantissa at every one; the guard discards 26 decades of legitimately representable, precision-rich depth.

defects.why:
REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE ANGLES AND FAILED ON ALL FIVE. Verdict stands, unchanged. Recording what was tried, so the next reader does not repeat it:

(1) DIMENSIONLESS/BOUNDED? No. d is built from the caller's operands by two multiplies with nothing in between. Not refutable.

(2) CALLER NORMALISES? Checked with a word-boundary grep over all of src/, not assumed. The only in-tree cx_div call is linalg_precision.cyr:1430, `phase = cx_div(x1, cx_real(abs_x1))`, guarded one line above by `f64_gt(abs_x1, EPSILON_F64)` on the UNSQUARED modulus, so d = abs_x1^2 > 1e-24 and the shipped guard is unreachable from there. The claim already conceded this and it is correct. ⭐ It cuts BOTH ways and the claim understated its own case: F64_TINY is equally unreachable from that site, so the repair is a provable NO-OP for every in-tree caller and cannot regress the QR path. The exposure is the public API only (cx_div is `#must_use`, complex.cyr is listed in cyrius.cyml `[lib]` line 69, and the guard is present verbatim at dist/hisab.cyr:1735).

(3) CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE? No. It gates a return, not an iteration; the function has no loop.

(4) BREAKS AN EXISTING TEST? Checked, not assumed — all six assertion sites that reach this guard or its two siblings: edge_cases.tcyr:478 (asserts the HANDLE is non-null, not the value), :848 (cx_div by 1e-9 -> d = 1e-18, above BOTH thresholds, unchanged), :850, :852, :855-856 (exact zero -> d = 0 < DBL_MIN, still fires, still returns 0), abuse.tcyr:2435-2437 (exact zero, same), modules.tcyr:3458 (unit scale). Not one moves under F64_TINY. The 2.6.13 regression pin at edge_cases.tcyr:848 is specifically what would have caught a threshold that went UP; it says nothing about one that should go down.

(5) SCALE TEST DOESN'T DISCRIMINATE? It discriminates. I re-derived all five counts independently in exact f64 and got 241 / 235 / 170 / 93 / 89 with first-wrong decades -7 / -13 / -78 / -155 / -158 — reproducing the claim to the digit.

⛔ ONE ANGLE I THOUGHT WOULD LAND AND WHICH THE REPO ITSELF REFUTES. I tried to argue the precedent is a FALSE ANALOGY — that F64_TINY = DBL_MIN is dimension-exact only for an UNSQUARED denominator (d < DBL_MIN <=> d subnormal <=> 1/d degrades), and that geo.cyr's cited sites are all unsquared ray-direction components (verified: geo.cyr:546/583/620/767/809/849 all guard `f64_abs(dx)`-shaped scalars). That would have made cx_div's squared d a different case. It does not land: src/vec3.cyr:180's own comment calls its guarded `denom = |a|*|b|` "a length SQUARED, so it scales as the square of the caller's units" and guards it with F64_TINY at :197. Applying F64_TINY to a squared quantity IS the repo's settled shape, decided deliberately. The claim's appeal to precedent is stronger than it argued.

THE DEFECT ITSELF, restated with the units named: d is in u^2 and EPSILON_F64*EPSILON_F64 = 1e-24 is a dimensionless constant. Changing the caller from metres to millimetres multiplies d by 1e6 while the threshold does not move, so the same problem in different units gets a different answer. The effective cutoff is |b| < 1e-12, an absolute magnitude on a quantity with no absolute meaning. |b| = 1e-13 is an ordinary double whose reciprocal 1e13 is ordinary; the division cannot fail there. Reproduced: cx_div(1+0i, 1e-13+0i) -> d = 1e-26 < 1e-24 -> cx_zero(), where the truth is 1e13+0i.

The two byte-identical siblings are cx_inv (complex.cyr:94) and cx_powf (complex.cyr:129); cx_inv's own in-tree caller (linalg_ext.cyr:1163) is likewise pre-guarded at linalg_ext.cyr:1150.

SHARPENED — the claim's one-token `f64_lt(d, F64_TINY)` is right in direction and is NOT the measured optimum. Three candidates, ranked by measurement over the 401-decade sweep, all preserving the singularity pin:

(a) `f64_lt(d, F64_TINY)` — DBL_MIN, src/error.cyr:45, spelled as at src/vec3.cyr:197 and via geo.cyr:26's alias. ONE-TOKEN edit at complex.cyr:62 and the two siblings :94 (cx_inv) and :129 (cx_powf). 93/401 fail. Recovers 142 decades. Verified no existing test moves and no in-tree caller can reach it. (b) `d == 0` only — the LITERAL reading of the rule 2.10.2 settled ("guard exactly what makes the division fail and nothing more"). ⭐ THE CLAIM DID NOT BRACKET THIS AND IT BEATS THE CLAIM'S OWN PROPOSAL: 89/401 fail vs 93.
