Neither threshold needs a scale chosen for it.
defects.scale_test: The round 2-sphere of radius r is the same geometric problem at every scale and its sectional curvature is exactly 1/r^2, so the assertion is the scale invariant K == 2^-2k BIT-EXACTLY. Build the constant-curvature (1,3) Riemann once (R^0_101 = 1, R^0_110 = -1, R^1_010 = 1, R^1_001 = -1 — r-independent, and equal to the true equatorial round-sphere Riemann), set metric = diag(r^2, r^2), u = e0, v = e1, and sweep r = 2^k. THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING'S RANGES, each measured: (A) METRIC SWEEP k = -255..255 (511 scales), NOT -250..250. Every value stays normal (at k = -255, denom = 2^-1020, two binades above DBL_MIN = 2^-1022; at k = 255, denom = 2^1020) and the backstop must not fire, which needs k > -256. Measured: shipped 265 exact / 246 zero / 0 other, failing tail k in [-255,-10]; repair 511/511 exact; mutant |denom| < 1e-6 fires for k <= -5 (251 zeros); mutants |denom| < 1e-24 and "sqrt(|denom|) < EPSILON_F64" fire for k <= -20 (236 zeros); mutant |denom| < 1e-300 fires for k <= -250 (6 zeros); DBL_MIN-only and no-guard are 511/511 exact. On the filing's narrower [-250,250] the 1e-300 mutant is caught by EXACTLY ONE point — the widening is what makes that kill robust. (B) TANGENT-RESCALE SWEEP j = -255..255 at fixed r = 1, u = s*e0, v = s*e1, s = 2^j, K bit-exactly 1.0 at all 511 — NOT the filing's [-120,120], which is measurably insufficient: the 1e-300 mutant scores 241/241 exact over [-120,120] and is not detected at all, while over [-255,255] it fails 6. Measured on the wide range: shipped 265 exact / 246 zero, failing tail j <= -10 (the filing's "j <= -5" is wrong — that is the 1e-6 mutant, measured at 251 zeros with tail j <= -5); 1e-24 mutant tail j <= -20; repair 511/511. This is the cleaner statement of the defect because nothing about the SPACE changed, only the caller's choice of basis vectors. (C) TWO COMPANION ASSERTIONS, without which a repair could simply delete the guard: (i) genuine degeneracy must still return 0 — u = s*e0, v = 2s*e0 over j = -255..254, measured 510/510 zeros for shipped, for the repair and for DBL_MIN-only, and 0/510 for no-guard, so it kills deletion; (ii) the LORENTZIAN NULL CASE g = diag(-1,1), u = v = (1,1), which must return exactly 0 — measured: the relative test alone does not fire (uu*vv = 0) and returns NaN, only the F64_TINY backstop fires. Companion (ii) is the only one of the three sweeps that kills a "relative test, no backstop" repair, and it is absent from the filing. Every threshold a repair might plausibly choose is therefore bracketed: 1e-12 (shipped), 1e-6, 1e-24 / sqrt-first, 1e-300, guard deleted, and relative-without-backstop; the two scale-free guards are the only survivors.

defects.guarded_quantity: |y| -- the raw, unnormalised absolute DIVISOR. Degree 1 in the caller's units, unbounded over (0, DBL_MAX]. REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED: f64_fmod has ZERO call sites anywhere in src/ (grep over src, tests, examples: only the definition plus 8 test assertions). It is a leaf public export of the distributed bundle -- f64_util.cyr is listed in cyrius.cyml [lib] line 60 and the function appears verbatim at dist/hisab.cyr:69 -- so every real caller is an external consumer whose units this repo never sees. There is no normalising caller to appeal to, and no possible one.
defects.protects: The single division f64_div(x, y) on line 30, whose quotient is truncated and multiplied back: x - trunc(x/y)*y. Not a convergence tolerance -- there is no loop, no iterate, no residual; one division, one trunc, one FMA-shaped subtraction. The only failure a |y|-only predicate can genuinely address is y == 0 (quotient +-inf or NaN -> inf*0 = NaN -> x - NaN = NaN). The doc comment on line 22 states exactly that contract: "Returns 0 if y == 0".
defects.why: VERDICT UPHELD; three of the finding's supporting claims REFUTED by measurement and corrected here. Upheld because fmod is exactly homogeneous of degree 1 in both operands and for k = 2^n the identity fmod(kx, ky) = k*fmod(x, y) is bit-exact -- measured: the unguarded formula reproduces glibc fmod bit-for-bit at ALL 2095 scales n = -1074..1020 for both (3,5) and (7,3), zero failures. |y| moves with the caller's unit choice; EPSILON_F64 (0x3D719799812DEA11, decoded = 1e-12 exactly) does not. Shipped guard fails 978 of the 2041 scales in n = -1020..1020 (family A; 979 for B), onset at n = -43. All five refutation routes were checked and all fail: (1) |y| is neither dimensionless nor bounded; (2) no caller normalises because there is no caller -- it is a bundle-leaf public API; (3) not a convergence tolerance; (4) no existing test breaks under repair -- every y in tests/*.tcyr is 0, 3, -3 or 2 (abuse.tcyr:2313-2315, modules.tcyr:6494-6508; the finding's cited modules.tcyr:6439 is the WRONG LINE, it is 6508); (5) the sweep does discriminate the shipped value. CORRECTIONS. (a) The finding's headline example is FABRICATED and impossible on its face -- it claims f64_fmod(1e6, 1e-13) returns 9.99999999392329e-14 "against a true 1.0000000000851952e-13", but a remainder can never be >= its divisor. Measured: the formula returns exactly 0, true fmod is 2.625443659963001e-14. The ratio-hazard point survives and is worse than stated (silent 0, 100% error, at a |y| the guard PERMITS). (b) DBL_MIN's stated rationale -- "exactly the set that breaks the division and nothing more" -- is FALSE. The overflow hazard is a ratio condition and straddles DBL_MIN on both sides: f(1e10, 1e-300) = -inf with y NORMAL and passing a DBL_MIN guard, and f(1e300, 1e-11) = -inf TODAY at a y the shipped 1e-12 permits (true 9.4666e-12). DBL_MIN separates nothing. (c) Worse, DBL_MIN is itself a scale chosen for the caller, 296 decades lower: for a subnormal divisor with a comparable dividend the formula is EXACT (x = 3*2^-1074, y = 5*2^-1074 -> exactly 3*2^-1074) and a DBL_MIN guard fabricates 0 there -- 50 of the extended sweep's scales for family A, 51 for B. Its only genuine catch, subnormal y with large x, it converts from a LOUD -inf into a SILENT 0 (x = 1.0, y = 3*2^-1074: true 4.94e-324, zero-test gives -inf, DBL_MIN gives 0). Same class as complex.cyr:58, just quieter. So the repair is the exact-zero predicate, not DBL_MIN.
defects.fabricates: Exactly 0 -- bit-indistinguishable from the legitimate 0 a correct fmod returns for an exact multiple. No rc, no error channel, value returned directly. Measured fabrications on the shipped code: f64_fmod(3e-13, 5e-13) returns 0 where the exact answer is 3e-13 (100% relative error; the unguarded formula returns it bit-exactly), and f64_fmod(1e-300, 1e-13) returns 0 where the exact answer is 1e-300 (unguarded formula bit-exact, quotient 1e-287, nowhere near any limit). Whenever |x| < |y| < 1e-12 the true answer is x itself and the function returns 0. The band is ~312 decades wide (1e-12 down to the smallest subnormal 4.94e-324), and measurement shows it is entirely untested: the 8 assertions that touch this function pass only y in {0, 3, -3, 2}.
defects.correct_threshold: SHARPENED, and it is NOT the F64_TINY/DBL_MIN the finding proposed -- measurement kills that: use the EXACT-ZERO predicate, `if ((y & 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF) == 0) { return 0; }` (equivalently `f64_lt(f64_abs(y), 4.94e-324)`, the smallest subnormal, which is the same set). The bit form is preferred because it is the one already used two lines down in f64_copysign and it catches -0.0, which an ordered comparison against 0 handles but which the 2.6.15 copysign defect proves this file has gotten wrong before. Rationale, all measured: (i) the trunc formula is bit-exact at every representable scale including the full subnormal range, so any threshold above zero fabricates over some correctly-computable region -- DBL_MIN over 50 scales of the sweep, 1e-12 over 978; (ii) DBL_MIN does not bound the overflow hazard it claims to (y = 1e-300 normal, x = 1e10 -> -inf), so it buys no property; (iii) where DBL_MIN does fire it replaces a detectable -inf with an undetectable 0, which is the fabricating-guard class it was meant to repair. The -inf on |x/y| > DBL_MAX and the precision loss above |x/y| > 2^53 are a separate algorithmic repair (scaled reduction, or return a non-finite so the caller can see it); they are ratio conditions and no |y|-only threshold, DBL_MIN included, can address them -- that must not be used to justify keeping either 1e-12 or DBL_MIN. Test-safety verified by inspection of every call site: abuse.tcyr:2313 and modules.tcyr:6508 both pass y = +0.0 and both still return 0; modules.tcyr:6494-6505 use y in {3, -3, 2}, untouched.
defects.scale_test: AXIS 1, SCALE COVARIANCE, with the finding's range EXTENDED because measurement shows the original does not bracket its own recommendation. For k = 2^n assert f64_fmod(k*x0, k*y0) == k*expected BIT-EXACTLY (no tolerance, no f64_to -- 2.13.0's rule), on (x0, y0, exp) = (3, 5, 3) [the |x| < |y| branch, nothing removed] and (7, 3, 1) [q != 0], sweeping n = -1074 .. +1020, i.e. 2095 scales spanning the entire representable range down to the smallest subnormal. The extension is load-bearing and is the correction to the finding: over its proposed n = -1020..1020 the smallest divisor reached is 5*2^-1020 = 4.45e-307, so thresholds of 1e-307, 1e-310, 1e-320, the smallest subnormal AND a pure zero test ALL survive with 0 failures -- its claim that "a DBL_MIN repair is the only one that survives" is measurably false. Measured kill counts over the extended range (family A / family B): 1e-12 -> 1032/1033, 1e-15 -> 1022/1023, machine eps 2.22e-16 -> 1020/1021, 1e-30 -> 973/973, 1e-150 -> 574/575, 1e-300 -> 76/76, 1e-307 -> 52/53, 1e-310 -> 42/43, 1e-320 -> 9/10, DBL_MIN -> 50/51, exact zero -> 0/0. Every candidate a repair might reach for is killed, including the finding's own; only the exact-zero predicate survives, and the raw formula is bit-exact at all 2095 scales so the expectation is well founded (verified: 0 exactness failures with the guard removed). AXIS 2, RATIO -- the finding's version is BROKEN and is replaced. Its family (3,5), (7,3), (1e6,3), (1e12,3) tops out at |x/y| = 3.33e11, while a relative guard |y| < 1e-12*|x| fires only above |x/y| = 1e12: measured, not one member of that family fires any relative candidate, so the axis fails to discriminate the exact repair it exists for. Use instead x = 9007199254740991 (2^53-1), y = 3 -> remainder exactly 1 (ratio 3.0024e15, formula verified bit-exact against glibc), and its negation -(2^53-1) mod 3 -> exactly -1, which re-checks trunc-not-floor at high ratio in the same assertion. That kills eps_r = 1e-12 and 1e-15 while a zero or DBL_MIN guard never fires on it. LIMIT, recorded rather than papered over: a machine-eps relative guard (2.22e-16) fires only above |x/y| = 2^52, and a search over that band found NO input with a nonzero, exactly-computable remainder -- the formula's own exactness region ends there. It therefore cannot be killed by any value assertion and must be caught by interrogating the predicate DIRECTLY (assert the guard is false for every y != 0 across a decade sweep), which is 2.11.0's lesson that a guard has to be asked, not inferred from outputs.

defects.site: src/geo_advanced.cyr:1056 (siblings :1060 and :1067 are the same defect and must be repaired together)
defects.guarded_quantity: :1056 and :1060 compare hvec3_length_sq(e1) — the SQUARED length of a Minkowski-difference edge, dims L^2 — against the unsquared EPSILON_F64 (1e-12); effective cutoff |e1| < 1e-6. The sibling at :1067 compares hvec3_length_sq(hvec3_cross(e1, e2)) — dims L^4, since a cross of two length-L vectors is O(L^2) — against the same 1e-12; effective cutoff |e1||e2|sin(theta) < 1e-6, i.e. L < ~1e-3. Both are absolute thresholds on quantities that carry units.
defects.protects: Nothing that can fail. :1056/:1060 are the "is this vertex genuinely distinct from v0" selector; :1067 is the "is the set planar rather than a segment" selector. Neither divides. The only division downstream is inside _epa_unit, which carries its own scale-free `f64_gt(l, 0) == 0` guard (:496-498), so removing these thresholds entirely cannot expose a division by zero.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED on all five avenues; the finding is CONFIRMED by measurement, and two of its own fields were too lenient. (1) Not dimensionless: measured sweep of L over 1e-100..1e100 on the fixture the code's own comment names (gjk_epa_3d:1274, two coplanar zero-height boxes) gives |dot(n, z)| = 0 for 51 of the 131 decades in 1e-30..1e100 — the returned "separating direction" lies IN the contact plane, so translating along it never separates the shapes. The exact answer is scale-invariant (+/-z for every L), so the verdict changing with k is definitional proof the quantity scales: e1 ~ L, length_sq(e1) ~ L^2, cross ~ L^2, length_sq(cross) ~ L^4. (2) The caller does not normalise: gjk_epa_3d:1277 stores the return value straight into out_normal and returns 1; measured end-to-end, the caller receives the fabricated vector with rc = 1 and depth 0. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: it is a one-shot selector over a fixed simplex, and the SAME FILE repaired the identical expression to `f64_gt(hvec3_length_sq(dir), 0) == 0` at :266 in 2.9.0 with the reasoning "the only value that is genuinely unusable is zero -- and testing against zero is scale-free". That sweep stopped 790 lines short. (4) The proposed repair breaks NOTHING: patched copies of geo_advanced.cyr run against all four suites that include it produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output (hisab 416, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776, 0 failed) — which is also the mutation evidence that 3252 assertions are blind to this guard, because modules.tcyr:8908-8910 is the only place the degenerate normal's DIRECTION is ever asserted and it runs at scale 1 only. (5) The scale test does discriminate, but the claim got two details wrong in the lenient direction, corrected below.
defects.fabricates: THREE distinct fabrications, all measured, none reporting an error. (a) L <= 1e-7: the :1060 test fires and the function returns a hard-coded hvec3_unit_x() — a unit vector lying IN the z=0 contact plane, so the caller cannot tell it is fabricated. (b) 1e-6 < L <= 1e-4: e1 survives but the L^4 test at :1067 fails, control reaches :1069, and _epa_perp(e1) returns a unit IN-PLANE perpendicular — also |dot(n,z)| = 0. Measured with AXIS-ALIGNED boxes, so _epa_perp does NOT rescue this case (see scale_test). (c) L >= 1e77 (24 decades): length_sq(cross) ~ L^4 overflows to +Inf, +Inf passes the `> EPSILON_F64` test, _epa_unit divides by hvec3_length = +Inf and returns the ZERO VECTOR — measured hvec3_length_sq(out_normal) == 0 with gjk_epa_3d returning rc = 1. That is precisely the NULL/zero normal the 2.8.3 comment at gjk_epa_3d:1274 says the degenerate path exists to prevent ("Returning 0 here left out_normal holding the NULL HVec3 for every caller that trusted 'returns 1 => out_normal is a normal'"), and modules.tcyr:8907/8908 assert against it at scale 1 only.
defects.correct_threshold: TWO changes; the claim's single proposal is necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT — measured. (i) :1056 and :1060 — replace `f64_lt(hvec3_length_sq(e1), EPSILON_F64) == 1` with `f64_gt(hvec3_length_sq(e1), 0) == 0`, the exact 2.9.0 repair form used at :266 of this file. Nothing divides, so DBL_MIN is not needed; zero is the only unusable value. (ii) :1067 — testing the raw cross against 0 is NOT enough: measured, the `> 0` repair alone still fails 24 of 131 decades (all of L >= 1e77) because the L^4 quantity OVERFLOWS to +Inf before it is ever compared, and _epa_unit then returns the zero vector. The quantity must be made dimensionless instead of merely re-thresholded: `var c = hvec3_cross(_epa_unit(e1), _epa_unit(hvec3_sub(_gjk_simplex_get(simplex, j), v0)));` then `if (f64_gt(hvec3_length_sq(c), 0) == 1)`. That is sin^2(theta) between two unit vectors — bounded in [0,1], degree-0 homogeneous, cannot overflow or underflow from operand magnitude, and 0 is exactly the collinear case the branch is asking about. Measured: 0 of 131 decades wrong, and all four suites byte-identical to baseline. (_epa_unit already returns hvec3_zero() on a zero input, so a duplicate vertex still reads as collinear and correctly falls through to the segment branch.)
defects.scale_test: _epa_degenerate_normal is degree-0 homogeneous: for a zero-volume Minkowski difference, scaling BOTH shapes by k must return the SAME unit vector up to sign. FIXTURE (corrected — the claim's 45-degree rotation is NOT load-bearing): the axis-aligned pair modules.tcyr:8896 already builds — _mpr_mkbox(0,0,0,L,L,0) against _mpr_mkbox(L/2,L/2,0,L,L,0) — measured to fail on exactly the same 51 of 131 decades as the rotated version, because GJK's simplex diagonal is not axis-aligned and _epa_perp therefore does not land on +z. Rotating is harmless but buys nothing. BAND (corrected — must NOT reach 1e-100): sweep L in decade steps over 1e-30 .. 1e100, 131 decades, asserting f64 bit-exact |dot(n(L), (0,0,1))| == 1 AND hvec3_length_sq(n) == 1. Do not extend below ~1e-54: measured, _gjk_core_3d there returns a COLLINEAR simplex for this fixture even under a fully correct repair, so the assertion fails for a reason that has nothing to do with this guard and the test would false-fail (that is a separate finding). BRACKETING (measured, not argued): shipped code 51/131 wrong; unsquare-only 1e-6 wrong on the same low band; eps^2 = 1e-24 at :1067 still needs L > 1e-6, wrong on 1e-30..1e-6; DBL_MIN at :1067 clears the low end but dies on the 1e77..1e100 half where the L^4 operand is +Inf before any threshold is consulted; the claim's own `> 0` repair leaves 24/131 wrong (the same top band); only the normalise-before-cross form is 0/131. A sweep confined to 1e-3..1e3 kills none of them, and a sweep that stops at 1e30 fails to distinguish `> 0` from the correct repair.

defects.guarded_quantity: hvec3_length_sq(e1) — the SQUARED length of the first simplex edge e1 = v_i - v_0 of the Minkowski difference A (-) B, units [world length]^2 — compared against the unsquared EPSILON_F64 (src/error.cyr:26 = 1e-12). Effective cutoff |e1| < 1e-6, and it scales as k^2 while the threshold is fixed.
defects.protects: Nothing that can fail. There is NO division, sqrt or acos at the site; the guard is a rank classification of the affine hull — the early return that declares the whole simplex a single point and answers with a cardinal axis. The only downstream division is inside _epa_unit (:486-490), which already self-guards on `f64_gt(l, 0)` and whose own comment (:482-485) says in as many words: "Normalise without EPSILON_F64's ABSOLUTE cutoff ... which silently kills every direction in a scene scaled to 1e-6."
defects.why: Every refutation avenue was tried and each one is refuted by measurement, not by argument. (1) NOT dimensionless: e1 is a difference of two Minkowski-difference support points, so it carries world length units and its square carries them squared; the same geometry in metres and micrometres produces length_sq values 1e24 apart. (2) The caller does NOT normalise: gjk_epa_3d (:1239-1282) hands raw support functions and raw shape data straight through, and the whole surrounding stack is deliberately built to be scale-free — _gjk_core_3d's sibling guard was repaired to `> 0` in 2.9.0 at :266 with a comment naming exactly this failure ("A scene at scale 1e-9 has |dir|^2 ~ 1e-18, so every direction GJK ever computed was declared degenerate"). So GJK now correctly delivers a valid micro-scale simplex, and this function throws it away. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: no iteration, no residual, no bound — one comparison, one early return, one fabricated answer. (4) The proposed repair breaks NO existing test: I installed `f64_gt(length_sq, 0) == 0` at :1056/:1060 and `> 0` at :1067 in a scratch copy of src/ and ran all five suites against it — hisab 416/416, foundation 359/359, modules 1827/1827, edge_cases 233/233, abuse 776/776, 3611 passed, 0 failed. MEASURED at the PUBLIC entry point on a 1-D-hull fixture (two collinear zero-thickness segments along x at scale k, hull is a segment, so the only correct answer is any n with dot(n, unit_x) == 0): shipped gjk_epa_3d returns a correct perpendicular for k = 1e100 down to 1e-6, and from k = 1e-9 through k = 1e-160 it returns exactly unit_x — |dot(n, unit_x)| = 1.000000000, i.e. a direction PARALLEL to the hull that provably does not escape the set — with rc = 1 and depth 0 and no error channel. With :1060 alone repaired the same sweep is correct from 1e100 down to 1e-160. Reason nothing saw it: the only assertions on a degenerate normal in the tree are modules.tcyr:8905-8910, all at scale 1, and the 2^-20 dyadic sweep at modules.tcyr:9187-9196 uses sphere/box tangency fixtures only while _ag_eval (modules.tcyr:772-816) never inspects the normal at all.
defects.fabricates: hvec3_unit_x() — unit length, rc = 1, depth 0, no error channel. Measured stronger than "plausible": on the collinear-segment fixture at k <= 1e-9 the returned unit_x is exactly PARALLEL to the 1-D hull (dot = 1.0), the one direction that cannot separate the pair; on the coplanar-flat-box fixture it lies IN the z = 0 plane (dot with the true normal = 0). |n|^2 measured 1.000000000 in every wrong case, so the suite's own "normal is a unit vector" assertion (modules.tcyr:8908) cannot see it — only a DIRECTION assertion can.
defects.correct_threshold: `f64_gt(hvec3_length_sq(e1), 0) == 0`, matching this file's own 2.9.0 repair at :266 — correct in kind and measured to hold the segment fixture from k = 1e100 down to k = 1e-160. Two sharpenings from measurement. (a) It is not exactly scale-free: L^2 underflows to +0 for |e1| < ~2.2e-162, so the repaired fixture first fails at k = 1e-165. If the guard must be exact all the way to DBL_MIN in L rather than in L^2, test the components against zero (or hvec3_length(e1) > 0), not the square. (b) Repairing :1060 ALONE is provably insufficient for the planar case: the :1060-only repair is BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped at all 18 decades of the coplanar-box fixture, because :1067 guards hvec3_length_sq(cross(e1, ...)) — a quantity that scales as L^4 — and fires two decades EARLIER (last correct k = 1e-3, first wrong k = 1e-6), routing to the in-plane _epa_perp fallback. :1056, :1060 and :1067 must be repaired together. Separately filed by the same sweep, NOT this guard: at k = 1e100 the L^4 cross product overflows to +Inf, _epa_unit scales by 1/Inf, and both shipped and repaired code return the ZERO vector with rc = 1 — an overflow defect at :1067/_epa_unit.
defects.scale_test: The claim's proposed test DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE and must be replaced — measured, not argued. On the 45-degree/coplanar-box fixture a :1060-only repair scores identically to shipped at every decade (:1067's L^4 term masks :1060 completely), and a ">= 200 decade" span rejects the CORRECT repair at both ends for reasons that are not this guard (L^4 underflow at k <= 1e-81 gives an in-plane answer; L^4 overflow at k = 1e100 gives a zero vector on shipped and repaired alike). Use instead a 1-D-HULL fixture, where :1060 is the only guard on the path: two collinear zero-thickness boxes along x — a = box(c=0, h=(L,0,0)), b = box(c=(L/2,0,0), h=(L,0,0)) — through the public gjk_epa_3d, sweeping L = 1e100 .. 1e-165. The single assertion is on DIRECTION, `|dot(n, unit_x)| == 0` (assert unit length too and it discriminates nothing — |n| measured 1.0 in every wrong case, the same lesson as 2.11.1's fabricated-identity quaternion). Measured brackets, so every threshold a repair might plausibly choose is separated: shipped (EPSILON_F64 on L^2, |e1| < 1e-6) last correct 1e-6, first wrong 1e-9; a 1e-24-on-L^2 repair (|e1| < 1e-12) fails below ~1e-12; a DBL_MIN-on-L^2 repair fails below ~1.5e-154; `> 0` on L^2 holds to 1e-160 and fails at 1e-165; a relative or component-wise-against-zero repair passes the whole span. Run the coplanar-box fixture BESIDE it, bounded to L in [1e-75, 1e75], to score :1067.

defects.guarded_quantity: hvec3_length_sq(hvec3_cross(e1, vj - v0)) — the SQUARE of the cross product of two Minkowski-difference edge vectors, dimension L^4 — compared against the unsquared EPSILON_F64 (1e-12). Equivalent to |c| > 1e-6, i.e. an absolute AREA cutoff of 1e-6 in scene units squared. MEASURED breakpoint on the shipped coplanar-flat-box fixture (Minkowski edge = 4L, so |c| = 16 L^2 sin θ): correct at L = 1e-3, fabricating at L = 1e-4, exactly the predicted 16 L^2 > 1e-6 → L > 2.5e-4.
defects.protects: Nothing that can fail. It is the planar-vs-segment CLASSIFICATION: it selects which of two different answers the function returns (the plane normal _epa_unit(c), or the segment fallback _epa_unit(_epa_perp(e1))). The only division downstream is inside _epa_unit, which carries its own independent and correct guard (`if (f64_gt(l, 0) == 0) { return hvec3_zero(); }`, geo_advanced.cyr:487) — so this guard is not standing in for a divide-by-zero test, and removing it entirely would not produce a NaN or an Inf, only a different classification.
defects.why: Reclassified from DEFECT_SQUARED_VS_UNSQUARED, on measurement. The original filing was right that the guard is broken and right about the mechanism (an L^4 quantity against a fixed 1e-12) but wrong about the repair implied by its label: unsquaring is NOT the fix and the filing's bracket ran the wrong way. Isolating this guard (with the sibling e1 guard at :1056 repaired so it cannot mask) and sweeping L over 1e0..1e-12 on the shipped fixture: shipped `|c|^2 > 1e-12` first fabricates at L = 1e-4; the unsquare-only candidate `|c| > 1e-12` first fabricates at L = 1e-7 — three decades LOWER, not 1.5 decades higher as the filing's "3e-2" claimed. Squaring a sub-unit quantity makes the test HARDER to pass, so the shipped guard misclassifies over a WIDER range than any unsquared form; unsquaring merely relocates the same absolute cutoff. The defect is therefore that an ABSOLUTE threshold is applied to a quantity that scales as the fourth power of scene scale, and no choice of constant can be right for it. All four refutation angles were tested and all four failed: (1) not dimensionless — measured, a rigid rescale of the same geometry changes the returned normal; (2) no caller normalises — gjk_epa_3d:1277 passes the user's raw support functions and shapes at world scale; (3) not a convergence tolerance — it is a one-shot branch selector, and the division it might be thought to protect is already guarded in _epa_unit; (4) the proposed threshold does NOT break an existing test — on modules.tcyr:8892 (coplanar flat boxes, which asserts the normal has no x and no y component) all five candidate guards return exactly (0,0,-1), identical to shipped. Separately confirmed the fabrication's shape by hand-trace and by measurement: for an in-plane e1 that is a DIAGONAL of the patch, _epa_perp crosses e1 with the cardinal axis it is least aligned with — z for an xy-plane edge — giving a vector lying IN the contact plane. The 45-degree rotation the filing asked for is unnecessary; the shipped axis-aligned fixture already produces a diagonal e1.
defects.fabricates: A unit in-plane vector presented as the escape direction for a planar contact, written to out_normal with rc = 1 and depth 0 — a "separating direction" that does not separate. MEASURED on the shipped gjk_epa_3d with two coplanar flat boxes (half-extent L, offset L/2, plane z = 0): at L = 1e-4, 1e-5 and 1e-6 the returned normal is (-0.447213595, -0.894427191, 0), whose dot with the true plane normal is exactly 0. It is unit length and depth is exactly 0, so modules.tcyr:8908's `_ac_len_sq_e9(ep_n) == 1000000000` and the agreement sweep's classification/depth counters all pass on it — the same trap recorded for the fabricated identity quaternion in 2.11.1. Below L ~ 2.5e-7 the sibling guard at :1056 takes over and the function returns (1,0,0) instead, which is a second fabrication attributable to that guard, not this one.
defects.correct_threshold: The dimensionless sin form this file already uses at :530 and :682: f64_le(hvec3_length(c), f64_mul(EPSILON_F64, f64_mul(hvec3_length(e1), hvec3_length(hvec3_sub(vj, v0))))) as the REJECT test — |a x b| = |a||b| sin θ, so the ratio is bounded in [0,1] and scale-free. Verified correct at every decade from 1e0 to 1e-12 and byte-identical to shipped on both unit-scale fixtures. TWO SHARPENINGS the original filing missed. (1) The `f64_gt(hvec3_length_sq(c), 0)` alternative it offered as "if a pure divide-guard is preferred" is the wrong framing and must not be chosen on that ground: this guard protects no division (the division has its own guard in _epa_unit), so `> 0` is not a divide-guard here but a classification threshold of zero — it accepts a simplex whose collinearity is broken only by rounding and then hands _epa_unit a cross product whose DIRECTION is pure noise. Measured, `> 0` is indistinguishable from the relative form across all 12 decades of the scale sweep, so the scale sweep cannot choose between them; the choice must be made on a sliver (near-collinear) simplex at fixed scale, where only the relative form rejects. (2) The repair is UNOBSERVABLE below L ~ 2.5e-7 unless the sibling guard at :1056 (`f64_lt(hvec3_length_sq(e1), EPSILON_F64)`, an L^2 quantity against the same absolute 1e-12) is repaired in the SAME change: measured at L = 1e-10 with :1056 left as shipped, all five candidate c-guards return (1,0,0) identically. Fix both or the sweep proves nothing about either.
defects.scale_test: Take the SHIPPED fixture at modules.tcyr:8892 verbatim — _mpr_mkbox(0,0,0,L,L,0) against _mpr_mkbox(L/2,L/2,0,L,L,0) — and run it at every decade of L, asserting |dot(n, (0,0,1))| == 1 exactly. No rotation is needed: e1 comes out a diagonal of the patch, so _epa_perp already picks z and returns an in-plane vector. MEASURED breakpoints, which correct the filing's inverted bracket — with :1056 repaired so it cannot mask, shipped `|c|^2 > 1e-12` first fabricates at L = 1e-4 (not 1e-3), the unsquare-only candidate `|c| > 1e-12` first fabricates at L = 1e-7 (not 3e-2 — three decades BELOW shipped, not above), and `|c|^2 > DBL_MIN`, the relative-sin form and `|c|^2 > 0` are all still correct at L = 1e-12. So L in 1e0..1e-8 already separates shipped from every repair and separates the unsquare candidate from the rest; the filing's demand for 200 decades is right only for splitting DBL_MIN from the relative form, whose crossover is at |c| ~ 1.5e-154, i.e. 16 L^2 ~ 1.5e-154 → L ~ 3e-78, so 1e-100..1e100 is required for THAT pair and for nothing else. Two things this sweep provably CANNOT do, both measured: it cannot separate `|c|^2 > 0` from the relative form at any scale (identical over all 12 decades tested — that pair needs a near-collinear sliver simplex at fixed scale, where the relative form rejects and `> 0` accepts a rounding-noise direction), and it cannot see any c-guard repair at all below L ~ 2.5e-7 while :1056 stands (all five candidates return (1,0,0) at L = 1e-10). Guard the assertion against the OTHER fabrication too: assert the normal is not (1,0,0) as well as |dot| == 1, so a fix that merely trades one fabrication for the other cannot score green.

defects.site: src/geo_advanced.cyr:1516 (siblings: :1530 dy, :1544 dz — one defect, three copies)
defects.guarded_quantity: |dx|, the x component of GeoRay.direction. Dimensionless ONLY if the direction is unit, and it is not guaranteed to be: GeoRay is #derive(accessors) at geo.cyr:35, so the public GeoRay_set_direction stores whatever it is given (the hazard is documented in-tree at geo.cyr:409 and geo.cyr:477). ⚠ But normalization is not even a mitigation here, which is the sharpest correction to the original filing: for direction (9e-13, 1, 0), sqrt(1 + 8.1e-25) rounds to EXACTLY 1.0, so geo_ray_new hands the guard dx = 9e-13 bit-for-bit with |d| = 1.0 (measured). The quantity that actually decides whether the slab matters is |dx| * t_range against the box extent, and neither t_range nor the extent appears in the test — so even the bounded, unit-direction case has no correct constant.
defects.protects: the reciprocal f64_div(F64_ONE, dx) on line 1517 (and 1531 / 1545) that feeds the slab arithmetic. It is a divide-by-zero guard, not a tolerance: nothing below it converges, iterates, or compares two quantities for equality.
defects.why: Could not refute; all five refutation routes were tried and each is closed by measurement. (1) BOUNDED/DIMENSIONLESS — fails: with |d| = 1.0 exactly, the widened fixture below returns MISS for every dx in [DBL_MIN, 1e-13] where the truth is HIT, so the threshold is wrong even where the quantity IS dimensionless. (2) CALLER NORMALISES — fails twice: bvh_query_ray passes the ray through untouched, and geo_ray_new's normalization leaves dx = 9e-13 unchanged because the length rounds to 1.0. (3) CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE — fails: it guards a division, and the else branch is straight-line slab algebra. (4) EXISTING TEST WOULD CHANGE — checked, does not: every ray reaching bvh_query_ray in tests/*.tcyr and tests/*.bcyr has direction components exactly 0 or +-1 (hvec3_unit_x, hvec3_unit_z, F64_ONE, hvec3_zero) or NaN — modules.tcyr:8862/8868/8874/8879/8881/8888, abuse.tcyr:1763/1785, hisab.bcyr:719/908. f64_lt(0, DBL_MIN) is still 1, so exact-zero components keep taking the parallel branch, and NaN compares false under both constants. The repair is bit-identical on the whole suite — which also means the suite cannot notice it being reverted. (5) SCALE TEST DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — this one landed partially and is corrected below rather than refuting the finding. Confirmed positively: the file is a pre-2.10.2 copy of the slab code (geo.cyr:546/583/620 — NOT :527/564/601 as filed — now read _GEO_F64_TINY), and the rationale at geo.cyr:499-507 applies verbatim. The consequence is strictly worse than in geo.cyr: geo_ray_aabb returns a wrong t, this returns a wrong PRUNE, and the function's own header (geo_advanced.cyr:1487) says pruning a node "discards its ENTIRE subtree".
defects.fabricates: a confident 0 (= miss). _bvh_query_ray_rec:1566 tests `== 0` and returns immediately, so a whole subtree the ray genuinely enters is discarded and bvh_query_ray hands back a short or empty vec with no error channel and no sentinel. The filed fixture reproduces exactly as claimed (simulated against the shipped arithmetic): box x in [0,1], y,z in [-1e12,1e12], origin (-0.5,-1e12,0), unit direction (9e-13,1,0) — true entry t = 5.5556e11, true exit t = 1.6667e12; current guard -> parallel branch -> ox = -0.5 < bmin.x = 0 -> 0; with DBL_MIN -> 1.
defects.correct_threshold: DBL_MIN, spelled as a file-local alias `var _GA_F64_TINY = F64_TINY;` beside the existing _GA_F64_POS_INF/_GA_F64_NEG_INF (geo_advanced.cyr:21-22), then `f64_lt(f64_abs(dx), _GA_F64_TINY) == 1` at :1516/:1530/:1544 — textually identical in shape to the shipped geo.cyr:546/583/620. Use the alias, not a fresh hex literal: error.cyr:45 already holds F64_TINY = 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 and the alias form matches geo.cyr:26, quat.cyr:12 and autodiff.cyr:17, so scripts/check-constants.sh gains no new hand-encoded constant to verify. Do NOT "improve" on DBL_MIN toward the true finite-reciprocal cut (~5.56e-309, where 1/x last stays under DBL_MAX): DBL_MIN is deliberately ~4x conservative, subnormal reciprocals lose precision, and byte-identity with geo.cyr is the point. geo_ray_obb's `!= 1` spelling (geo.cyr:767/809/849) is equivalent — pick it only if it makes the two functions read the same.
defects.scale_test: Two assertions; BOTH filed versions needed correcting, and as filed neither is sound. (1) DIRECTION-MAGNITUDE COVARIANCE — bvh_query_ray must return the same hit set for direction d and k*d. ⚠ The fixture choice is load-bearing and the filing omitted it: swept over k = 2^p, the three existing modules.tcyr BVH rays (interior (0.5,0.5,0.5), face (1,0.5,0.5), corner (0,0.5,0.5), all dir +x) are 0/511 non-covariant under the CURRENT guard — they kill nothing, because when the guard fires the parallel branch's inside-slab test accepts anyway. The origin must lie OUTSIDE the box in the shrinking component: with origin (-3,0.5,0.5) into the [0,1]^3 pair, 246/511 sampled k disagree under 1e-12 and 0/511 under DBL_MIN (measured). ⚠ And the range must be p in [-1020, +1020], not the filed +-1000: a repair that chose 1e-307 is non-covariant at exactly 1 of the 511 samples (p = -1020) and SURVIVES a +-1000 sweep; 1e-300 survives with only 3 disagreeing samples there. (2) UNIT-DIRECTION FALSE NEGATIVE — ⛔ the filed fixture cannot carry the sweep it is asked to carry: with y,z extents of 1e12 the y slab exits at t = 2e12 while entry needs t = 0.5/dx, so the TRUTH is already MISS at dx = 1e-15 and all five candidate thresholds agree from there down — it brackets 1e-12 vs 1e-6 and nothing below. Widen as: box x in [0,1], y in [-1e308,1e308], z in [-1,1]; origin (-0.5,0,0); direction (dx, sqrt(1-dx*dx), 0), which is unit to the last bit. Measured discriminating dx values on that fixture, one per candidate repair: 1e-7 (kills 1e-6), 1e-13 (kills the shipped 1e-12), 1e-17 (kills DBL_EPSILON 2.2e-16), 1e-100 (kills EPSILON^2 = 1e-24), 1e-305 (kills 1e-300), and dx = DBL_MIN itself plus 4e-308 (kills 1e-307 — the only pair the covariance sweep barely reaches). ⛔ Assert MISS, not HIT, at dx = 1e-310, 1e-320 and 0: 1/1e-320 overflows to +Inf and the REPAIRED code returns 0 there too, so the filed sweep endpoints would fail against the correct repair. The filed rule "truth is hit for every dx whose reciprocal is finite" is wrong in both directions — false above (1e-320's reciprocal is not finite) and false below (dx in [5.56e-309, DBL_MIN) has a finite reciprocal that geo.cyr's contract deliberately treats as parallel). State the property as the DBL_MIN cut itself. Mutation-proof it by reinstating EPSILON_F64 at :1516 only (dy/dz left repaired) and confirming the dx assertions fail — and grep the mutant in place before believing the count.

defects.guarded_quantity: |dy| = f64_abs(HVec3_y(GeoRay_direction(ray))), the y component of the ray direction. Its dimension is scene-length per unit of ray parameter t, i.e. it is only "bounded to [0,1]" if the direction is unit — and |d| is precisely the unit in which t is measured, so it is not a dimensionless quantity, it is a scale factor. Same quantity, same missing precondition as :1516 (x) and :1544 (z).
defects.protects: the reciprocal at :1534, `var iy = f64_div(F64_ONE, dy)` — a plain divide-by-zero guard, not a tolerance and not a convergence test.
defects.why: CONFIRMED by measurement, and every refutation avenue was tried and closed. (1) NOT dimensionless: what decides whether the y slab may be deleted is |dy| * t_range against the box's y extent; none of those three appear in the test, which compares a per-unit-t rate against a bare 1e-12. (2) The caller does NOT protect — it is the opposite: `geo_ray_new` NORMALISES, and normalisation is what manufactures the tiny component. Measured witness, direction unit to 16 digits (asserted): box x[0,4e12] y[0,1] z[0,1], origin (0, -0.9, 0.5), direction (1, 9e-13, 0). `geo_ray_aabb` — the sibling geo.cyr repaired in 2.10.2 onto `_GEO_F64_TINY` — returns t = 1e12, a real forward hit at the y = 0 face; `_bvh_ray_hits_aabb` returns 0 and `bvh_query_ray` returns an EMPTY vec. One primitive, so the leaf IS the root: the entire tree is discarded. This is geo.cyr:486-488's own recorded failure ("the same box expressed both ways answered 0 and 4.5e12") reproduced one level up, now between geo.cyr and geo_advanced.cyr. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance — it guards a division literally. (4) The proposed correct_threshold breaks NO existing test — CHECKED, not assumed: with all three slabs on F64_TINY, 3611/3611 assertions pass (hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776), byte-identical counts to the pristine baseline, with the patch grep-proven installed both before and after the run. The one test that pins this exact branch, modules.tcyr:8881 `br_miss` "parallel ray outside the y slab -> 0", has dy bitwise +0.0 (asserted), and +0.0 < DBL_MIN, so it stays on the parallel branch and still returns 0. (5) The all-parallel path also lacks geo_ray_aabb_face's `slabs` counter, so a zero direction returns 1 for every node — a second, opposite fabrication in the same function that this threshold repair does not address and that should be filed separately.
defects.fabricates: Returns 0, "no hit" — and since `_bvh_query_ray_rec` returns immediately on 0, the node AND ITS WHOLE SUBTREE are pruned. There is no error channel: the predicate's only outputs are 1 and 0, so a false 0 is indistinguishable from a true miss, and `bvh_query_ray` hands the caller a short (or empty) candidate list with no signal. Measured: 1 candidate is the truth, `vec_len` = 0 is returned, while `geo_ray_aabb` on the identical box returns 1e12.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, 2.2250738585072014e-308) — the smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is finite, which is exactly and only what the `f64_div(F64_ONE, dy)` at :1534 needs. Spell it as a module-local alias `var _GA_F64_TINY = F64_TINY;`, matching geo.cyr:26 `_GEO_F64_TINY`, autodiff.cyr:17 `_AD_F64_TINY` and quat.cyr — geo_advanced.cyr today has no TINY alias, only `_GA_F64_NEG_INF`/`_GA_F64_POS_INF`. Apply to all THREE slabs (:1516 dx, :1530 dy, :1544 dz) in one change; a partial move makes the function disagree with itself across axes, which is the same self-contradiction geo.cyr:486-488 records. Verified: the three-slab move compiles clean and leaves all 3611 existing assertions passing.
defects.scale_test: SHARPENED — the proposed test is inadequate two ways, both measured. (a) A single 9e-13 witness with x and y exchanged kills only the shipped 1e-12: a 1e-15 alternative repair PASSES it (measured: D1 passed on the 1e-15 mutant). It does not bracket. (b) Worse, uniform scene scaling — the ordinary "same problem in different units" — DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE AT ALL here, because the direction is unit and therefore scale-INVARIANT: scaling origin and box by 1e0..1e40 leaves |dy| untouched, and 41 of 41 scales answer identically on the shipped tree, on the 1e-15 mutant AND on the repair. Use instead, on all three axes: (1) DIRECTION-SCALE COVARIANCE — the predicate is homogeneous of degree 0 in d (scaling d by k>0 reparameterises t but does not move the ray as a point set), so assert `_bvh_ray_hits_aabb(ray_k, box) == (geo_ray_aabb(ray_k, box) != 0)` for d scaled by k = 1e-320 .. 1e+60 via `GeoRay_set_direction`. Measured: shipped fails 296/381 (top bad decade e = -295), the 1e-15 mutant fails 293/381 (top bad e = -295), the DBL_MIN repair passes 381/381 — so it brackets EPSILON_F64, every intermediate candidate and DBL_MIN itself, with the tail below e = -295 where dy flushes to zero agreeing on all three because 1/dy is genuinely not finite there. (2) A DECADE SWEEP of the guarded quantity itself: |dy| = 9e-j for j = 1..300, box x extent sized to 4 * (0.9/|dy|) so the ray really does climb into the y slab, asserting sibling agreement with `geo_ray_aabb`. Measured: shipped first contradicts at j = 13 (288/300 bad), the 1e-15 mutant at j = 16 (285/300 bad), the repair 0/300. (3) Keep the public-API witness as the named regression guard: a one-primitive BVH where `vec_len(bvh_query_ray(tree, ray))` must equal 1 while `geo_ray_aabb` on the same box returns 1e12 — it names the symptom (a whole subtree silently lost) that a slab-level assertion does not.

defects.guarded_quantity: |dz|, the z component of GeoRay_direction. NOT a length: geo_ray_new (src/geo.cyr:38-44) calls hvec3_normalize, so on the constructed path this is a DIMENSIONLESS direction cosine bounded by 1. Measured: |dz| is bit-identical across 41 binary decades of unit change (2^-20..2^+20) and moves <= 1e-14 relative (2 ulp) across 13 decimal decades.
defects.protects: Nominally the division f64_div(F64_ONE, dz) on the else branch. Its actual effect is a SEMANTIC branch: when it fires the z slab is deleted from the intersection entirely and replaced by an origin-containment test.
defects.why: The finding survives but its CLASS was wrong. |dz| is dimensionless and bounded, so it does not scale with the problem's length units - src/error.cyr:40-44 names exactly this case ("EPSILON_F64 remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity - a normalised cosine") as the exemption. I tested that exemption and it is defeated by measurement, not by dimensional analysis: an absolute tolerance on a bounded quantity is right only when "below the tolerance" implies "the answer does not change", and here it changes on 287 of 299 measured decades. The quantity that decides whether deleting the z slab is safe is |dz| * t_range against the box's z extent; none of those three appear in the test. That is the library's own settled wording for the sibling it already repaired: src/geo.cyr:489 - "That threshold is scale-free and the consequence is not." geo_ray_aabb was moved to _GEO_F64_TINY in 2.10.2; the three slab guards in this BVH copy (1516/1530/1544) were never migrated, so a normalised ray gets one answer from geo_ray_aabb and the opposite from _bvh_ray_hits_aabb on the same ray and the same box. Secondary, weaker witness on the non-normalising public path (GeoRay_set_direction, which the geo_ray_aabb header already names as reachable): the predicate must be degree-0 in |d|, since scaling d reparameterises t but leaves the ray as a point set unchanged - measured, it answers HIT at 20 of 41 magnitudes of the SAME ray and flips at |d| = 2, where |dz| crosses 1e-12. That is a reparameterisation invariance, not a unit change, so it does not rescue the ABSOLUTE_ON_SCALING label either.
defects.fabricates: A silent false MISS - the subtree prune, measured, not argued. Box x in [0, 4e13], y and z in [0,1]; ray origin (0, 0.5, -0.9), direction normalize((1, 0, 9e-13)) with hvec3_length asserted bit-exactly F64_ONE. |dz| = 9e-13 is below EPSILON_F64 (1e-12) so the guard fires, oz = -0.9 < bmin_z = 0, and the function returns 0. In the same library geo_ray_aabb returns a real forward t whose hit point is inside the box on all three axes. bvh_query_ray on a one-primitive tree therefore returns an EMPTY vec: the only leaf, discarded, with rc = 0 and no error signal. |dz| here is 295 decades above DBL_MIN, so 1/dz is finite and exact - the division the guard exists for could not have failed.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000) - unchanged from the claim, now verified rather than asserted, and for the same reason src/geo.cyr gives: guard exactly what makes the division fail and nothing more. Apply to all three slabs (1516 dx, 1530 dy, 1544 dz), not 1544 alone, and reach it through a _GA_F64_TINY alias so geo_advanced matches _GEO_F64_TINY / _AD_F64_TINY / _QUAT_F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:28-45). CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: patching 1544 alone, and patching all three, leaves all five suites BYTE-IDENTICAL against shipped - 3611/3611 passing (hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776). The existing parallel-ray fixtures (tests/modules.tcyr:8881 "parallel ray outside the y slab -> 0") carry dz and dy of exactly +0.0, which is below DBL_MIN, so they stay on the parallel branch and are untouched.
defects.scale_test: REPLACED - the claimed test ("the :1516 sweep with x and z exchanged", framed as the same problem in different units) is REFUTED by measurement: it discriminates nothing, because geo_ray_new normalises and a unit change leaves |dz| bit-identical, so shipped and every candidate repair answer identically at every scale. The sweep that does discriminate holds the direction UNIT and varies t_range instead. Fixture Z(k), k = 1..299: box x in [0, 4e+k], y and z in [0,1]; origin (0, 0.5, -0.9); direction normalize((1, 0, 9e-k)) - |d| is bit-exactly 1.0 for every k >= 9. The ray enters the z slab at t = 1e+k, well inside the x extent, so the truth is a HIT at every k, independently confirmed by geo_ray_aabb (299/299 hits) and by an exact rational slab reference. It BRACKETS every threshold a repair might plausibly choose, each flipping to a wrong MISS at its own decade: EPSILON_F64 1e-12 at k=13 (measured on shipped: right on 12 of 299, first wrong at exactly k=13), DBL_EPSILON ~1e-16 at k=17, _GEO_F64_EPS_SQ 1e-24 at k=25, 1e-30 at k=31, 1e-100 at k=150; DBL_MIN never flips anywhere in range. Pair it with the MISS control that stops a repair from turning everything into a hit: same near-parallel dz with the x extent 100x short (k = 4..59), truth MISS, and both shipped and the DBL_MIN repair answer MISS on all 56.

defects.guarded_quantity: speed = hvec3_length(vel_b - vel_a), a relative SPEED with dimensions L/T. It scales linearly with the length unit and inversely with the time unit. Measured: the function's answer flips at exactly this threshold (rc = 1 at speed 2^-39 = 1.819e-12, rc = 0 at 2^-40 = 9.095e-13) for a physically identical problem.
defects.protects: the division f64_div(F64_ONE, speed) on the next line (:2023) that builds the unit direction u0, which is used only to probe the Minkowski difference's extent (gscale). Nothing else in the function consumes speed; the loop's own tolerances are separate and both relative (_GA_TOI_REL at :1944, tol = gscale * _GA_TOI_TOL_REL at :2032).
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED on every axis; the defect is now measured rather than argued. (1) Not dimensionless: speed is L/T. Held the geometry at unit scale and changed only the TIME unit (velocity x 2^-m, max_t x 2^m) — out_t * speed is BIT-IDENTICAL for every m tested, and rc flips 1 -> 0 at exactly m = 40 (speed 9.095e-13), with the fast side clean to 2^+200. A guard that decides "never collides" on the choice of second is not measuring anything physical. (2) No caller normalises: it is a public entry point taking raw HVec3 velocities; the two suites that call it feed 0 and 5e-7..200. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: it guards the division on the following line, and the file's own convergence tests are relative and elsewhere. (4) The repair breaks nothing: the only inputs whose behaviour changes are speeds in (0, 1e-12), and no assertion in tests/*.tcyr supplies one — abuse.tcyr:2035 and modules.tcyr:6691 use speed exactly 0, which f64_gt(speed,0)==0 still answers 0. The branch itself is sound (overlap at t = 0 is ruled out above, so zero relative velocity IS a correct "never collides"); only the threshold is invented, and it contradicts _epa_unit's stated rule at :482-487 in the same file and error.cyr:41-44's explicit "NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR EPSILON_F64" note for division guards. What DID fall to the refutation is the proposed scale_test, corrected below.
defects.fabricates: return 0 — "no collision within max_t", a confident negative with no error channel, and out_t/out_normal are left holding whatever the caller had. Measured, not hypothesised: two unit spheres with a surface gap of 1e-3 closing head-on at 2^-39 = 1.819e-12 per unit time with max_t = 1e12 return rc = 1 and out_t = 5.4975581e8 (= gap/speed); the SAME configuration at 2^-40 = 9.095e-13 returns rc = 0 with out_t untouched, although the impact at t = 1.0995e9 is three decades inside the horizon. Expressing the identical problem in millimetres (speed 9.095e-10) answers it correctly.
defects.correct_threshold: if (f64_gt(speed, 0) == 0) { return 0; } — this file's own _epa_unit rule (:482-487). NOT f64_lt(speed, F64_TINY): measured, the two are behaviourally IDENTICAL here and the >0 form is strictly better. `speed` comes from hvec3_length, which squares before the sqrt, so any relative velocity below 2^-538 has its square underflow and the length is returned as exactly 0 (verified: 2^-537 -> nonzero, 2^-538 -> exactly 0, i.e. the guarded quantity is either 0 or >= 2.3e-162 and can never be subnormal). DBL_MIN is therefore unreachable as an observed value and adds nothing over > 0, while > 0 additionally catches a NaN velocity that f64_lt(speed, F64_TINY) and the shipped f64_lt(speed, EPSILON_F64) both fall through (verified: f64_lt(NaN, EPSILON_F64) == 0). Nothing between 2.3e-162 and 1e-12 makes the division fail.

defects.guarded_quantity: |b_j|, the magnitude of one blade coefficient of the right multivector operand, compared against EPSILON_F64 (1e-12) as `f64_lt(f64_abs(bj), EPSILON_F64) != 1`

The sign-agnostic form also keeps NaN flowing through (f64_abs(NaN) != 0), matching the current guard's behaviour (`f64_lt(NaN, eps)` is 0, so `!= 1` is true), so NaN propagation is unchanged. defects.scale_test: Three probes, all bit-exact (every factor a power of two, so no rounding), all with a = e12 held at UNIT magnitude so the outer guard at :2358 cannot fire and only :2361 is under test. Baseline: rc(e12, e1) = -e2 (already pinned at tests/hisab.tcyr:419). P1 — brackets EPSILON_F64: assert rc(e12, 2^-40·e1) has blade[2] == -2^-40 (0xBD70000000000000). 2^-40 = 9.0949e-13 sits just under 1e-12, so this pins the threshold tightly rather than merely far below it. P3 — brackets a NORM-RELATIVE repair, which no uniform scaling can reach because a relative threshold is itself scale-covariant and passes P1 and P2: put two scales inside ONE operand, b = e1 + 2^-80·e2, and compare all 32 result blades against an oracle built only from guard-clean unit-magnitude evaluations, ref = rc(e12, e1) + 2^-80 · rc(e12, e2) (using cga_mv_scale, which has no guard). MEASURED on the shipped tree: P1, P2, P3 all FAIL (blade reads 0). defects.guarded_quantity: |nsq| = |scalar part of B * reverse(B)|, a norm SQUARED (dims L^2 for a Euclidean blade; exactly k^2 for a blade scaled by k). Measured on the shipped binary: for B = k*e12 the shipped cga_norm_sq returns bit-exactly k^2 across k = 2^-39 .. 2^500. For a conformal sphere blade it is r^2 IN EXACT ARITHMETIC ONLY -- in double it is r^2 plus a cancellation residual of order eps_mach*|centre|^4.
defects.protects: the division f64_div(F64_ONE, nsq) on the next line -- but the comment at :2424-2426 gives it a SECOND job, classifying a null blade (conformal points, nsq == 0 exactly) so cga_project/cga_reject return the documented zero sentinel. One constant is doing both jobs, which is why no single value can be right.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON FIVE ROUTES; the verdict survives, the fixtures do not. (1) Dimensionless/bounded: NO -- measured, k*e12 gives nsq == k^2 bit-exactly over 2^-39..2^500, so the guarded quantity scales as L^2 with the caller's units. (2) Caller normalises: NO -- cga_project/cga_reject (:2437, :2443) hand the caller's blade straight through; there is no normalisation on any path. (3) Convergence tolerance: NO -- it is a singularity classifier, and its errors are caller-visible in BOTH directions. (4) Existing test breaks under the repair: CHECKED, NO -- every CGA test (hisab.tcyr:455-487, modules.tcyr:7988-7990) uses unit blades with nsq == +-1, or the exactly-zero multivector where every candidate threshold agrees; modules.tcyr:7990 only asserts the returned POINTER is non-zero, which cga_mv_zero() satisfies. So the repair is test-neutral. (5) The scale_test does not discriminate: REFUTED THE CLAIM'S FIXTURE A, three ways, all measured by running the shipped code (probe1/probe2 under CYRIUS_ALLOW_ABSOLUTE_INCLUDES=1, cycc 6.6.2). (5a) cga_sphere(0,0,0,r) is NOT a scaled blade: it tends to the fixed null point (0,0,0,-0.5,+0.5) as r->0, because cga_point hard-codes a unit length in (|p|^2 +- 1)/2. For r <= 1e-9 the shipped nsq is bit-exactly 0x0 (ep rounds to exactly -0.5 once r^2/2 < ulp(0.5)/2, i.e. r < 1.05e-8); for r >= 1e10 ep == em bit-for-bit and nsq is 0x0 again (measured at 1e10, 1e20, 1e50, 1e70 -- so the fixture dies of cancellation ~60 decades below the claimed overflow cap). Roughly 150 of the fixture's ~230 decades assert a bit-exact inverse of a blade whose nsq is EXACTLY ZERO: unsatisfiable by every candidate threshold including the claim's own, so it discriminates nothing. The information is destroyed by the embedding before the guard runs. (5b) In the live band the fixture cannot separate the shipped guard from the claim's own repair: magsq is exactly 0.5 for every small-r origin sphere, so EPSILON_F64*magsq = 5e-13 versus the absolute 1e-12 -- a factor 2 in nsq, sqrt(2) in r, invisible to decade steps. Measured decisions are IDENTICAL on every point of the claim's own list: both fire at r = 7.07e-7 (nsq = 4.9982e-13) and neither fires at r = 1e-6 (nsq = 1.00003e-12, invep = -4.9998e11). (5c) The bit-for-bit form is unachievable anyway -- nsq is not bit-equal to fl(r*r) at general r (r = 1e-3 gives nsq = 1.0000000000010001e-06). WHAT SURVIVES, measured: the guard is wrong in both directions, just not at the radii claimed. Too HIGH: cga_project(k*e1, k*e12) -- the same geometry in different units -- returns exactly k*e1 at k = 1 and silently returns ZERO at k = 2^-20 (~9.5e-7), 2^-30, 2^-45, because nsq = k^2 falls under 1e-12 for any k < 1e-6. A micrometre-scale problem posed in metres loses its answer. Too LOW: at coordinate scale 1e2 a conformal point's cancellation residual exceeds 1e-12 for 753/3000 (25.1%) of pseudo-random points, and the function then divides by pure rounding noise -- worst returned component 5.50e11x the input's largest component (scale 1e3: 758/3000, 1.72e10x; worst raw residual 1.68e7 at scale 1e6). NEW, and the claim missed it: cga_blade_inverse is not the only absolute epsilon in this path. cga_geometric_product (:2272,:2275), cga_outer_product (:2297,:2300) and both contractions (:2328,:2331,:2358,:2361) DROP any input component with |c| < EPSILON_F64, so a blade is silently annihilated below k = 1e-12 no matter what the inverse's guard does -- measured: k = 2^-40 (9.09e-13) gives nsq = 0x0, k = 2^-39 (1.82e-12) gives nsq = 2^-78. Four more instances of the same class, and they set a hard floor on what repairing this one guard can reach. [measured: scratchpad probe1-probe4, RUNS OF THE SHIPPED CODE built by cyrius 6.6.2, not an emulation]
defects.fabricates: Two different plausible answers, both measured on the shipped binary. Below the threshold: cga_mv_zero(), a legal multivector -- cga_project(k*e1, k*e12) returns 0 instead of k*e1 for every k < 1e-6, silently, rc-free. Above it: no guard fires at all, so it divides by rounding noise and returns a blade whose largest component is up to 5.50e11 times the input's (25.1% of pseudo-random points at coordinate scale 1e2, 25.3% at 1e3), which cga_project then propagates.
defects.correct_threshold: Split the two jobs, and use a factor MEASURED rather than reused. (1) Divide-by-zero: f64_lt(f64_abs(nsq), F64_TINY) -- DBL_MIN, the only value that makes the division fail. This case is common, not theoretical: nsq is bit-exactly 0x0 for every conformal point, for every origin sphere with r < 1.05e-8, and for every origin sphere with r > ~1e8. (2) Null-blade CLASSIFICATION, relative to the blade's own magnitude: |nsq| <= FACTOR * sum_i b_i^2. SHARPENED: the claim's FACTOR = EPSILON_F64 (1e-12) is measured to be ~4500x too loose and throws away resolvable geometry -- a sphere of radius 10 centred at 1e4 has nsq = 100 exactly, ratio 2.0e-14, i.e. 90x above the noise floor, yet 1e-12 * magsq = 5.0e3 would declare it null. The measured bound on the null residual is 1 machine epsilon and it IS scale-free: max |nsq| / sum b_i^2 over 3000 pseudo-random conformal points per scale is 2.13e-16, 2.22e-16, 1.109e-16, 1.110e-16, 1.110e-16, 1.110e-16, 1.108e-16 at coordinate scales 1, 10, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e6, 1e8. Use FACTOR = 8 * DBL_EPSILON = 1.776e-15 (8x margin over every measured null; keeps the r=10@1e4 sphere at 11x above the bound). Do NOT reuse EPSILON_F64 for it -- that is the constant that caused this. (3) The repair does not reach below k = 1e-12 unless the four sibling filters (cga_geometric_product :2272/:2275, cga_outer_product :2297/:2300, cga_left_contraction :2328/:2331, cga_right_contraction :2358/:2361) drop their absolute EPSILON_F64 component test as well -- they zero the blade before nsq is ever formed. [measured: probe3/probe4 on the shipped binary]
defects.scale_test: FIXTURE A REPLACED -- the claim's origin-sphere sweep is refuted above (nsq is bit-exactly 0 over ~150 of its 230 decades, and its two live decades give the shipped guard and the proposed repair IDENTICAL answers). Use a blade that actually scales. A' (invertible blade, threshold too high): B_k = k*e12 (cga_mv_set(b, 6, k)); shipped cga_norm_sq returns k^2 bit-exactly, and cga_blade_inverse(B_1) == -e12 exactly, so assert cga_mv_scale(cga_blade_inverse(B_k), k) == cga_blade_inverse(B_1) BIT-FOR-BIT with k stepped over powers of two, k = 2^-39, 2^-30, 2^-20, 2^-10, 2^0, 2^10, 2^100, 2^200, 2^400, 2^500. Powers of two make degree -1 homogeneity exact -- verified on the shipped binary: back-component is 0xbff0000000000000 (-1.0) at every k >= 2^-10 and 0x0 (guard fabricated zero) at 2^-20, 2^-30, 2^-39. Bracketing: the shipped 1e-12 on nsq is crossed at k = 1e-6 (between 2^-20 and 2^-19); a sqrt-style repair testing the unsquared norm crosses at k = 1e-12; a 1e-24 threshold at k = 1e-12; DBL_MIN at k = 2^-511. The lower cap is 2^-39, NOT DBL_MIN: below k = 1e-12 the four sibling component filters annihilate the blade regardless of this guard, so a sweep that goes lower fails the CORRECT repair and reads as a refutation -- run that sub-range only as a separate, explicitly-xfail probe of those four sites. Add the caller-visible form, which is the same problem in metres vs micrometres: cga_project(k*e1, k*e12) must equal k*e1 for every k in the sweep (shipped returns exactly k*e1 at k = 1 and exactly 0 at k = 2^-20). B (null blade, threshold too low -- the direction a sqrt-style repair makes WORSE): for P = cga_point(x,y,z) the answer must be cga_mv_zero() for EVERY point; sweep coordinate scale over 1, 10, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e6, 1e8 with several hundred pseudo-random directions per decade and assert the zero result. Shipped fails from scale 1e2 upward (753/3000 escapes at 1e2). Both are required and BOTH are needed to pin the factor: A' kills a repair that only lowers the constant (and any DBL_MIN-only repair, which passes A' but fails B); B kills a sqrt-style repair (residual 0.25 at scale 1e4 has sqrt 0.5, nowhere near any absolute epsilon) and any repair that only raises the constant; only a relative test passes both. Add a third assertion to pin the FACTOR itself, since A' and B are both satisfied by a factor anywhere in [2.2e-16, 1e-12]: a sphere of radius 10 centred at (1e4,0,0) has nsq == 100 exactly and must NOT be classified null -- that assertion fails under the claim's originally-proposed EPSILON_F64 factor and passes under 8*DBL_EPSILON.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = f64_sqrt(nx*nx + ny*ny + nz*nz) — the LENGTH of the caller's normal vector, dims L (or whatever unit the caller's normal carries). Compared against EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 (src/error.cyr:26, absolute). The routine's stated job is to normalise that vector, so its magnitude is by construction a free scale.
defects.protects: the division inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) on line 2479 — and nothing else. It is a divide-by-zero guard, not a tolerance: the file declares its convergence tolerance separately and relatively (_GA_EPA_REL_TOL, 1e-10, src/geo_advanced.cyr:477, commented "Relative, not absolute").
defects.why: Refutation attempted on all five paths; all five fail on the finding, though the fifth lands on the finding's own test. (1) Not dimensionless: norm is the caller's supplied length, an explicitly free scale. (2) No caller normalises — a tree-wide grep for `cga_plane` (excluding dist/) returns the definition, one doc mention, and ONE call site: tests/modules.tcyr:7989. It is a public entry point with zero internal callers, so nothing upstream can bound norm. (3) Not a convergence tolerance — see `protects`; and this same file already documents the correct rule for this exact situation at :484-:491, where `_epa_unit` uses `f64_gt(l, 0) == 0` with the comment "Normalise without EPSILON_F64's ABSOLUTE cutoff ... silently kills every direction in a scene scaled to 1e-6". The defect is the file disagreeing with its own note. (4) No existing test breaks: the sole call site is `assert_neq(cga_plane(0, 0, F64_ONE, 0), 0, ...)`, which compares the returned ALLOCATION HANDLE against 0 — vacuous with respect to every number in the function — and passes a unit normal (norm = 1), on which no proposed threshold changes behaviour. Even the norm == 0 -> cga_mv_zero() path stays green, because cga_mv_zero() returns a non-null alloc (:2203). (5) The scale test's PREMISE is right — the blade is degree-0 homogeneous under the joint scaling (n,d) -> (kn,kd); with the metric this file builds (e_inf = ep + em, e_0 = (em-ep)/2, verified against cga_point at :2450) the plane satisfies P·pi = x·n - d, so leaving n un-normalised denotes the plane x·n_hat = d/|n| — but the sweep as written is a broken instrument and is corrected below rather than accepted. Verdict stands.
defects.fabricates: A well-formed multivector denoting the WRONG plane, silently — the function has no error channel and always returns an allocated blade. Reproduced numerically: cga_plane(1e-13, 0, 0, 5) returns (e1, ep, em) = (1e-13, 5, 5), i.e. 1e-13*e1 + 5*e_inf, the plane at distance 5e13 where the caller asked for 5. The error factor is 1/|n|, unbounded. cga_plane(0, 0, 0, 5) returns 5*e_inf — not a plane at all (the point at infinity), rc-free. Note the corollary that makes it silent in a scaled scene: for |n| = 1e-13 the CURRENT code returns a blade whose e1 component is 1e-13, so a caller sanity-checking "is the normal unit-length" sees 1e-13, not the fabricated 1.0 of the identity-fabrication class — the fabrication is in the DISTANCE, which nothing downstream can re-derive.
defects.correct_threshold: `if (f64_gt(norm, 0) == 0) { return cga_mv_zero(); }` then divide unconditionally — this file's own _epa_unit rule (:488). Sharpened on two points found by measurement. (a) The alternative offered, `f64_lt(norm, F64_TINY)`, is NOT a meaningfully different choice here and DBL_MIN is decoration: norm is always a sqrt output, and sqrt's smallest nonzero result is 2.2227587494850775e-162 — 1e146x ABOVE DBL_MIN (2.2250738585072014e-308) — so the two predicates disagreed 0 times over 400,000 random sqrt-produced norms. DBL_MIN is the right threshold when guarding a division by a RAW operand; it is unreachable when the operand has been through a sqrt. The two forms differ on exactly one input, NaN: f64_lt(NaN, F64_TINY) == 0 takes the divide path and returns an all-NaN blade, while f64_gt(NaN, 0) == 0 routes it to the error return. Prefer the `>0` form for that reason and for consistency with :488. (b) Scope limit that must be stated so the repair is not later judged by a failure it does not own: the threshold fix restores exact degree-0 homogeneity only over |n| in [~1.5e-154, ~1.3e154]. Below ~1.6e-162 the SQUARES underflow (nx*nx -> 0, so norm == 0 for a perfectly good nonzero normal) and between ~1.6e-162 and ~1.5e-154 they are subnormal and lose up to 2^-24 relative; above ~1.3e154 they overflow to +Inf. That is a separate defect requiring max-component scaling (hypot-style), and it is the reason the sweep below is bounded.
defects.scale_test: The proposed sweep is REFUTED as written and replaced; the property it tests is right. MEASURED against a scale-free repair: decade steps k = 1e-160..1e+150 with bit-exact `component[1] == 1.0 && component[4] == 5.0` FAIL at 89 of 311 sample points ON THE REPAIRED CODE — 83 of them in the fully-normal range where the only error is the rounding of k*(1/k) and 5k*(1/k) (k = 1e-151 gives component[4] = 4.999999999999999; k = 1e-138 gives component[1] = 0.9999999999999999). A test that fails identically on the defect and on its repair discriminates nothing, and it invites the wrong fix — raising the threshold until it goes green. The other 6 failures are below ~1.6e-162, where nx*nx underflows to 0 so norm == 0 for EVERY threshold choice; and the claim that the span "separates DBL_MIN" is false, per the 0/400,000 disagreement above. CORRECTED SWEEP — k = 2^j, j = -511..+511 (1023 points, ~307 decades), base (nx,ny,nz,d) = (1,0,0,5). Powers of two make every step exact (k^2 in [2^-1022, 2^1022] is normal, 1/k is exact, k*(1/k) and 5k*(1/k) are exact), so bit-exactness is legitimate; the bounds are the largest range over which that holds. Assert ALL five components: component[1] == 1.0, component[2] == component[3] == 0.0, component[4] == component[5] == 5.0 — components 4 and 5 are what kill a repair that normalises n but forgets d, and 2/3 catch a wrong-slot write. MEASURED KILL TABLE on that sweep (failing j): current 1e-12 -> j <= -40 (472 of 1023); 1e-6 -> j <= -20; 1e-9 -> j <= -30; 1e-15 -> j <= -50; 1e-24 (EPSILON_F64^2) -> j <= -80; DBL_MIN -> 0 failures; f64_gt(norm,0) -> 0 failures. So it brackets every threshold a repair might plausibly choose, above and below the incumbent, and passes only for the scale-free forms. Two cases must be interrogated DIRECTLY rather than left to the sweep, since no perturbed sample reaches them: cga_plane(0,0,0,5) must return a blade a caller can detect as failed (not 5*e_inf), and cga_plane(1e-200,0,0,5e-200) must be recorded as the SEPARATE sum-of-squares underflow defect, expected to fail until the hypot-style scaling lands.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = sqrt(ax^2+ay^2+az^2), the LENGTH of the caller's rotation axis, in the caller's own units. The header comment one line above the fn (geo_advanced.cyr:2513) states "Axis (ax, ay, az) is normalized internally", i.e. the contract explicitly accepts any nonzero magnitude, so the magnitude is a free scale of the problem and the function is degree-0 homogeneous in it. Compared against EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 (src/error.cyr:26).
defects.protects: the single division f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) at geo_advanced.cyr:2522 that normalises the axis. No iteration, no convergence, nothing else downstream of it. VERIFIED the only reachable failure of that division is norm == 0.0 exactly: norm can never be subnormal (see correct_threshold), the smallest nonzero value it can take is sqrt(DBL_TRUE_MIN) = 2.2228e-162, and 1/2.2228e-162 = 4.4989e+161, finite and exact. At norm == 0, 1/0 = +Inf and az*(+Inf) = NaN, so the guard's true job is exactly "norm == 0".
defects.why: Every refutation avenue was checked against the tree and all five fail. (1) NOT dimensionless/bounded: norm is a raw caller-supplied length, and line 2513 documents that the axis is normalised internally, so the same rotation described with a shorter axis vector must yield the identical rotor. (2) NO caller normalises first: a repo-wide grep (excluding .git/build) finds cga_rotor at exactly three places outside its own definition — docs/architecture/math.md:124 (prose), tests/modules.tcyr:7987, and the dist/hisab.cyr:7238 bundle mirror. It has ZERO internal callers; it is a public entry point of a SHA-locked distributed bundle whose only real callers are the ten consumers. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: it guards one divide, no loop. (4) The proposed DBL_MIN threshold breaks NO existing test — the only test in the whole suite is assert_neq(cga_rotor(0, 0, F64_ONE, F64_PI_2), 0, "cga_rotor builds a rotor") at tests/modules.tcyr:7987, a UNIT axis whose assertion inspects only the returned pointer for non-null and cannot see a component value at all; hisab.tcyr's 79 cga_ sites contain no "rotor", and abuse/edge_cases/foundation contain zero cga_ anything. Under DBL_MIN that test is byte-identical. (5) The scale test does discriminate, but the finding stated it wrongly in three ways, all corrected below rather than fatal. Measured on a faithful IEEE-754 simulation of the exact op sequence: the shipped guard returns the identity for every axis with |a| < 1e-12 (2^-40 = 9.095e-13 -> identity, 2^-39 = 1.819e-12 -> correct rotor), while a DBL_MIN-guarded implementation returns the bit-exact correct rotor at every one of 1049 power-of-two scales from 2^-537 to 2^511. This is the same class repaired in quat.cyr in 2.11.1 and it is the sibling of cga_plane at geo_advanced.cyr:2479, which is worse still (falls back to inv = F64_ONE and silently emits an UNNORMALISED plane normal).
defects.fabricates: The IDENTITY rotor (scalar = F64_ONE, all 31 other blades 0), with no error channel and without the requested angle ever being read. It is a UNIT rotor (cga_norm = 1), so any assertion that only checks normalisation passes — the exact discrimination failure recorded in 2.11.1 ("the fabricated identity IS unit, so the assertion checks DIRECTION"). cga_rotor(1e-13, 0, 0, F64_PI_2) means "no rotation" and cga_sandwich then leaves every point where it was. NOTE a SECOND, distinct fabrication in the same function that the guard does not cover and the DBL_MIN repair alone does not fix: for |axis| >~ 1.34e154 the sum of squares overflows to +Inf, so inv = 1/Inf = 0, every n component becomes 0, and the function returns scalar cos(theta/2) beside a bivector of NEGATIVE ZERO — an object with |R| = 0.7071 that is not a versor at all. Measured at k = 2^512 and above. That one is NOT unit, so a norm assertion catches it while the component assertion catches both.
defects.correct_threshold: f64_lt(norm, _GA_F64_TINY) with a new var _GA_F64_TINY = F64_TINY declared beside the existing _GA_F64_* block at geo_advanced.cyr:18-22; F64_TINY already exists at src/error.cyr:45 (0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN) and is already aliased this exact way at quat.cyr:12, geo.cyr:26 and autodiff.cyr:17. SHARPENING the finding: DBL_MIN here is behaviourally IDENTICAL to f64_eq(norm, 0), because norm = sqrt(sum of squares) can never be subnormal — anything whose square underflows to zero gives norm exactly 0, and the smallest nonzero norm is sqrt(DBL_TRUE_MIN) = 2.2228e-162, a normal number 146 decades ABOVE DBL_MIN. DBL_MIN is still the correct written form (it matches the three sibling aliases and stays correct if the norm is ever recomputed by a scaled/hypot route that can produce subnormals), but the finding must not claim a test can observe the difference. The repair is INCOMPLETE unless it also rejects the overflow side: add a companion check that norm is finite (or scale the axis by max(|ax|,|ay|,|az|) before squaring), otherwise |axis| >~ 1.34e154 still silently returns the non-unit -0-bivector object described in `fabricates`.
defects.scale_test: cga_rotor is degree-0 homogeneous in the axis: cga_rotor(k*ax, k*ay, k*az, theta) must return the SAME rotor for every k > 0. Sweep axis (0,0,1) scaled by k = 2^j for every integer j in [-537, +511] (1049 points, ~315 decades) with theta = F64_PI_2, and assert component[0] == cos(pi/4) AND component[6] == -sin(pi/4) BIT-EXACTLY, plus |R| == 1. THREE CORRECTIONS to the originally proposed sweep, each measured: (1) Step in powers of TWO, not decades. With k = 10^e the reciprocal 1/norm rounds and k*(1/k) != 1.0, so strict == on component[6] fails for 49 of the 309 in-range decades EVEN ON A CORRECTLY REPAIRED IMPLEMENTATION — including k = 1e-11, one decade from the shipped threshold, off by 1 ULP. The decade form as written would be read as "the repair did not work". With k = 2^j the reciprocal is exact and the repaired implementation gives 0 failures in 1049, while the shipped code fails 498 (every j <= -40). (2) The sweep CANNOT bracket DBL_MIN and must not claim to: below j = -538 the square underflows to exactly 0 and BOTH the shipped and any sub-2.22e-162 threshold return the identity, so DBL_MIN, 1e-160 and "norm == 0" are mutually indistinguishable through axis scaling. What the sweep must bracket is the OBSERVABLE candidate set, and 2^j does: 1e-6 (2^-20), 1e-9 (2^-30), EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 (2^-40), 1e-15 (2^-50), EPSILON_F64^2 = 1e-24 (2^-80), and the true 0/nonzero boundary at j = -538 vs -537. (3) EXTEND the top to j = +530 (the original stopped at 1e+150 and missed this): assert |R| == 1 there, because at j >= 512 the sum of squares overflows and the function returns a bivector of -0 with |R| = 0.7071 — a second live fabrication the DBL_MIN repair does not fix. Additionally assert with a 4-ULP tolerance (not ==) on a generic axis such as (0,0,1e-160) and (k,k,k) in the band 2.22e-162 <= |a| <= 1.49e-154, where the sum of squares is subnormal and sqrt loses up to ~11 bits — measured 4e-6 relative error on component[6] at k = 1e-160 — which is inherent to the unscaled norm and must not be conflated with the guard.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = sqrt(qw^2+qx^2+qy^2+qz^2) — the Euclidean 4-norm of the caller's raw quaternion, read straight off HQuat_{w,x,y,z}(q) with no prior normalisation. Dimension: whatever units the caller's components carry; homogeneous of degree 1 in them (measured exactly so — norm(2^e * q) == 2^e * norm(q) bit-exactly for e = -537..511).
defects.protects: the division inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) on the next line, used to normalise the quaternion. It is a divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance and not a near-degeneracy test.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE GROUNDS; ALL FAILED. (1) Not dimensionless/bounded: norm is degree-1 homogeneous in the caller's raw components, while the function's contract — its own comment, "Construct from raw quaternion components (w, x, y, z). Normalizes." — is degree-0. A degree-1 quantity compared against a fixed 1e-12 is the defining shape of this class. (2) Caller does not normalise: the ONLY in-tree caller is lie_ext.cyr:366 (se3_from_mat4), which builds q from a rotation matrix and so passes norm ~= 1; I traced the degenerate case too (an all-zero mat4 takes the r00-largest branch and yields q = (0.5,0,0,0), norm 0.5), so no in-tree path can reach the guard. That makes the defect INVISIBLE in-tree — it is the reason the suite is silent, not evidence the guard is correct. su2_from_quat is a public entry point in dist/hisab.cyr and its doc comment advertises accepting non-unit input, so the caller is arbitrary by design. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: it guards f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) three lines down; there is no iteration. (4) F64_TINY changes NO existing test — checked, not assumed: modules.tcyr:3626 (the only su2_from_quat call in tests/) feeds su2_to_quat(su2_from_axis_angle(...)), norm exactly 1.0; modules.tcyr:7688's se3_from_mat4 round-trip likewise; abuse.tcyr:2526 exercises su2_from_axis_angle's SEPARATE guard on `len`, a different quantity at a different site. No test input lands in the changed interval [DBL_MIN, 1e-12). (5) The scale_test DOES discriminate, but the version as filed is a BROKEN INSTRUMENT — see scale_test; it is rewritten rather than refuted. MEASURED, exact power-of-two scaling of q = (w = cos(pi/4), x = sin(pi/4), 0, 0): shipped EPSILON_F64 is bit-exact only on e = -39..+511, fabricating the identity for every e <= -40; F64_TINY is bit-exact on e = -537..+511 — 1049 consecutive binary exponents, 315 decades, zero ulp deviation, exact even where the squares are subnormal. The repair widens the correct window by 498 binary exponents (~150 decades) and the division it protects fails only at norm = 0, another 537 exponents below where the shipped guard fires.
defects.fabricates: _su2_alloc(F64_ONE, 0, 0, 0) — the identity element: a valid unit quaternion, rc = 0, no error channel, indistinguishable from a real answer.
