Worst-case plausible, because for a scaled +w-only quaternion the fallback happens to BE right, which is exactly how a suite can pass while the wrong rotation is returned. ⚠ A SECOND, DISTINCT FABRICATION LIVES ON THE SAME LINE AND NEITHER THRESHOLD CAN REACH IT: for |q| >= 2^512 (~1.34e154) the squares overflow to +Inf, norm = +Inf, inv = f64_div(1, +Inf) = 0, and the function returns (0, 0, 0, 0) with rc = 0 — not a unit quaternion, not the identity, not any group element. `f64_lt(norm, T)` is false for +Inf under every T, so a threshold-only repair leaves it live. Measured: bit-exact through e = +511, all-zero from e = +512 (decades: correct through 1e154, zeros from 1e155).
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000) on `norm` — the smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is finite, i.e. precisely what makes f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) fail, and nothing more. The constant is already in the tree at src/error.cyr:45, whose own comment states this exact rule and names EPSILON_F64 as the wrong choice when the guard protects a division; quat.cyr:102/123 (hquat_normalize/hquat_inverse) is the same predicate on the same quantity already repaired this way in 2.11.1, and geo's _GEO_F64_TINY is the 2.10.2 repair of the same class. No overflow risk from the widening: norm >= DBL_MIN gives inv <= 4.49e307 (finite), and each component satisfies |q_i| <= norm so |q_i * inv| <= 1. Keep the identity fallback for the norm == 0 case — it matches hquat_normalize's convention. ⚠ TWO SCOPE NOTES A THRESHOLD-ONLY REPAIR MUST NOT SILENTLY INHERIT: (a) F64_TINY is the right guard for the DIVISION, but it does not make the function scale-free to DBL_MIN — the squared-norm accumulation loses the input first, flushing to 0 at e <= -538 (|q| ~ 1e-162), where the identity is then returned for a reason that is no longer the guard's; (b) the +Inf/(0,0,0,0) path above is unguarded at any threshold and needs its own fix (test norm for non-finiteness, or scale by the max component before squaring). Fixing the threshold alone is correct but partial, and should be recorded as such.
defects.scale_test: HOMOGENEITY OF DEGREE 0, SCALED BY POWERS OF TWO — NOT DECADES. su2_from_quat(k*q) must be BIT-IDENTICAL to su2_from_quat(q) for every k > 0. Fix q = hquat_new(sin(pi/4), 0, 0, cos(pi/4)) — a 90-degree rotation about x, so BOTH w and x are non-trivial (a w-only q cannot discriminate: the fabricated identity has the right shape and would let every mutant live). Take k = 2^e via ldexp/scalbn, e = -537..+511 (1049 exponents), asserting _su2_w == 0x3fe6a09e667f3bcd and _su2_x == 0x3fe6a09e667f3bcc at every one. ⛔ THE FILED DECADE VERSION IS A BROKEN INSTRUMENT AND WOULD FAIL ON CORRECTLY REPAIRED CODE — three measured defects. (i) Its central claim, "j = 0..12 all return 0x3fe6a09e667f3bcd/0x3fe6a09e667f3bcc, bit-identical across 13 decades", is FALSE: 4 of those 13 are 1 ulp off (j=1 w+1, j=4 x+1, j=10 both +1, j=11 w-1), because 10^-j is not representable so k*q is itself a rounding — and WHICH decades fail depends on how you scale (multiplying by 10^-j fails {1,4,10,11}; dividing by 10^j fails {1,4,5,9,10,11}). Over j = 0..154 only 96/155 are bit-exact. A test asserting decade bit-identity fails at j=1 on BOTH shipped and repaired code, reads as "the repair did not work", and the obvious rescue — loosening to a tolerance — is exactly the move that makes an assertion vacuous. (ii) Its span is wrong: "run to j=160, qw*qw underflows at j ~ 162" — measured, under F64_TINY the decade results are already 148 ulp off at j=155, 10,847 at j=156, 1.05e8 at j=158, 3.5e10 at j=160 and 3.8e13 at j=161, because the squares go SUBNORMAL near j ~ 154 and bleed bits long before reaching zero; j=155..161 is a garbage zone belonging to neither leg. (iii) Its mirror leg's j <= 150 cap steps around the +Inf -> (0,0,0,0) fabrication, so a threshold-only repair would be declared complete with half the range still fabricating. Powers of two fix all three: the scaling is exact, so bit-identity is a TRUE property, and it stays exact even where the squares are subnormal (at e = -511 each square is 2^-1023 and the sum 2^-1022 — powers of two, so subnormal arithmetic is exact). MEASURED WINDOWS: shipped EPSILON_F64 bit-exact on e = -39..+511 only; F64_TINY bit-exact on e = -537..+511 with zero ulp deviation. BRACKETING (first exponent at which each candidate fires, norm = 2^e exactly): 1e-6 at e=-20; sqrt(DBL_EPSILON) 1.4901e-8 at e=-27; the shipped 1e-12 at e=-40; 1e-15 at e=-50; DBL_EPSILON 2.22e-16 at e=-53; 1e-100 at e=-333 — all strictly inside the leg, so e = -537..0 kills every one, and only F64_TINY survives (it cannot fire anywhere in range). Add TWO separately-labelled boundary assertions so the partial-repair scope is explicit: at e = -538 the result IS the identity and must be asserted to be reached because the squared-norm expression underflowed to 0 (not because the guard chose a scale); at e = +512 the result is currently (0,0,0,0) — assert the intended post-fix value there, and pin the CURRENT value as a known-defect marker until the overflow path is fixed.

defects.guarded_quantity: len = f64_sqrt(ax^2 + ay^2 + az^2) at src/lie.cyr:99 — the Euclidean LENGTH of the caller's rotation axis, in the caller's own units. Dimension length^1, homogeneous of degree 1: writing the same axis in millimetres instead of metres multiplies it by 1000. It is not dimensionless, not bounded, and not a residual. The `angle` argument, which is the only place the rotation magnitude lives, is a separate parameter and is never inspected by the guard.
defects.protects: the division `var inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, len)` at src/lie.cyr:102, which normalises the axis. f64_div is a cycc primitive with no internal guard of its own (checked: the only EPSILON_F64 division guard in f64_util.cyr is f64_fmod's, a different function), so the sole failure mode is len == 0 (or subnormal, where 1/len overflows to +Inf and ax*inv becomes NaN).
defects.why: All five refutation avenues were tested and all five fail. (1) NOT dimensionless/bounded — `len` is |axis| in caller units, degree 1; error.cyr:40-44 states this repo's own rule verbatim ("EPSILON_F64 remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity — a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]"), and `len` is none of those. (2) NO caller normalises — grep over src/, tests/ and examples/ finds ZERO internal call sites (the only src/ hits besides the definition at :93 are three history comments); it is a public entry point whose own header says "Automatically normalizes on construction" and whose body comment is "# Normalize axis", i.e. arbitrary magnitude IS the contract. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance — it is three lines above the division it guards, one-shot, no loop. (4) The F64_TINY repair is test-neutral, MEASURED not assumed: a scratch tree with only line 100 changed to `f64_lt(len, F64_TINY)` runs hisab 416 / foundation 359 / modules 1827 / edge_cases 233 / abuse 776 = 3611 passed, 0 failed — BIT-IDENTICAL pass counts to the shipped tree built in the same directory. The one test that pins the fabrication path, abuse.tcyr:2525-2527 (`hvec3_zero()`), still passes: len is exactly 0, 0 < DBL_MIN, so the designed zero-axis identity return is preserved and only the fabrication BAND is removed. (5) The scale_test discriminates in substance but is WRONG as written — see scale_test below. Decisive precedent: `hquat_normalize` (src/quat.cyr:100-107) is the same three lines in the same shape (`len = length; if (len < T) return identity; inv = 1/len`) and was already moved to `_QUAT_F64_TINY` in 2.11.1; lie.cyr's su2 pair was simply missed by that sweep (`su2_from_quat`, src/lie.cyr:78, is the same defect on `norm` and should be repaired in the same edit).
defects.fabricates: _su2_alloc(F64_ONE, 0, 0, 0) — the identity of SU(2), a valid unit quaternion every downstream consumer (su2_to_quat, su2_to_rotation_matrix, so3_from_quat, se3_new) accepts, returned with no error channel. MEASURED on the shipped binary: su2_from_axis_angle(hvec3_new(1e-13,0,0), pi/2) returns w = 0x3FF0000000000000 (1.0), x = 0x0, where a unit axis returns w = 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCD (0.7071067811865476), x = 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCC. Worse than "a small rotation is dropped": holding the axis at 1e-13 and sweeping the angle, EVERY angle from 1e-6 through pi returns (1.0, 0) — a full 180-degree rotation discarded because a direction vector was short. Under the F64_TINY repair the same k = 1e-13 returns, at angle = pi, w = 0x3C91A60000000000 (6.123e-17 = cos(pi/2)) and x = 0x3FF0000000000000 (1.0), bit-identical to the unit-axis answer.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN) on `len` — exactly what makes f64_div(F64_ONE, len) fail and nothing more. Use the existing constant, matching src/quat.cyr:102's already-repaired `hquat_normalize`; do not introduce a fourth local alias. Apply the identical change to su2_from_quat (src/lie.cyr:78), which guards `norm` with EPSILON_F64 for the same division at :82. NOTE, and file separately rather than folding in: the repair does NOT make the function scale-free at the extremes, because the SUM OF SQUARES overflows/underflows before the guard is reached — measured, k^2 -> +Inf gives x = 0 with w still correct from k = 1e155 up, and k^2 -> 0 gives the full identity from k = 1e-162 down. Only a max-component-scaled (hypot-style) length is scale-free everywhere; F64_TINY is the correct threshold for the guard as the guard is written.
defects.scale_test: HOMOGENEITY OF DEGREE 0 IN THE AXIS, ANGLE HELD FIXED: su2_from_axis_angle(k*axis, angle) must equal su2_from_axis_angle(axis, angle) for every k > 0. ⛔ THE ORIGINAL FORM OF THIS TEST WOULD FAIL ON CORRECTLY-REPAIRED CODE and must be sharpened — MEASURED: with the F64_TINY repair in place and k = 10^-j, _su2_x reads 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCB at j = 5, 9, 11, 18 and 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCC elsewhere, a 1-ULP wobble that is INHERENT to the normalisation (fl(sqrt(fl(k*k))) does not round-trip to k for a decimal k) and not a defect; a hand-normalised control shows the same wobble at the same j. Bit-exactness on `_su2_x` for decimal k is therefore an over-strict assertion. Sharpened, three legs: (A) LOW LEG, EXACT POWERS OF TWO — axis = hvec3_new(2^-j, 0, 0), angle = pi/2, j = 0..537: assert _su2_w == 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCD AND _su2_x == 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCC BIT-EXACTLY. k*k is exact for a power of two while 2j <= 1074, so the repaired path is bit-exact with no wobble at all — VERIFIED bit-exact at j = 0,17,...,527 and fabricating at j = 544 (2^-1088 underflows), so cap at 537. This spans 10^0 down to ~2.3e-162 and brackets every threshold a repair might plausibly pick: 1e-6 (fires j=20), 1.49e-8 (j=26), 1e-12 as shipped (j=40), 1e-15 (j=50), 2.2e-16 DBL_EPSILON (j=52), 1e-100 (j=333), 1e-150 (j=499). F64_TINY is the ONLY candidate that never fires in range. (B) HIGH MIRROR, j = 0..511 only (2^512 squared overflows to +Inf — that is the separate overflow defect noted above; capping keeps the two from being conflated). (C) DECIMAL / UNITS LEG, which is the one that speaks in the units the defect is about (metres -> millimetres is x1e3): k = 10^-j, j = 0..154, assert _su2_w BIT-EXACT (w = cos(angle/2) does not depend on the axis at all and IS bit-identical at every k — measured) and |_su2_x - 0x3FE6A09E667F3BCC| <= 2 ULP. (D) SECOND LEG, THE ONE THAT SEPARATES THIS FROM A SMALL-ANGLE COMPLAINT: hold k = 1e-13 and sweep angle over 1e-6, 1e-5, ... 1, and pi; assert each result is BIT-IDENTICAL to su2_from_axis_angle(hvec3_new(1,0,0), angle). MEASURED: shipped returns (1.0, 0) for all eight; repaired returns all eight bit-identical to the unit-axis reference. This is what proves an arbitrarily LARGE rotation is being thrown away by a guard on a quantity that does not carry it — and a unit-norm assertion would not discriminate here at all, since the fabricated identity is itself unit, so the assertion must check DIRECTION.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = f64_sqrt(ox^2+oy^2+oz^2) = |omega|, the magnitude of the tangent vector, which by this function's own documented convention IS the rotation angle in radians. Dimensionless as a UNIT (an angle is invariant under any change of length/time units) but NOT bounded and NOT normalised: it is the caller's free scale parameter (a body rate times a timestep, a subdivision of a twist, a finite-difference step h). Measured range of the expression itself: it can only ever produce exactly 0.0 or a NORMAL double >= 2.2e-162 — f64_sqrt of the smallest positive subnormal (4.9e-324) is 2.2e-162, and the sum-of-squares underflows to 0 below that (verified: f64_mul(0x1,0x1) = 0x0, and su2_exp's own norm reads 0x0 from theta = 1e-162 down). The guarded quantity therefore has no subnormal regime at all.
defects.protects: The division sinc = f64_div(f64_sin(half), norm), with half = norm/2 — i.e. the sinc term sin(|omega|/2)/|omega| that carries the tangent (x,y,z) part. Nothing else in the function divides; f64_cos(half) is total.
defects.why: All five refutation routes were tried against measurement on cycc 6.6.2 and all five fail. (1) NOT dimensionless-and-bounded in the sense error.cyr:37-43 reserves EPSILON_F64 for ("a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]"): |omega| is an unbounded free input and the guard fires on the SMALL side, where nothing whatsoever fails. (2) NOT caller-normalised: the only in-tree caller, se3_exp (lie_ext.cyr:443), pre-filters theta at the SAME 1e-12 and so never reaches this guard — but su2_exp is a public bundle export (dist/hisab.cyr:19939), called directly by tests, and reachable by every one of the ten SHA-locked consumers. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: the division is perfectly conditioned everywhere the guard fires, and I measured that it is EXACT, not merely well-conditioned — f64_sin(half) returns half bit-for-bit for every theta <= 1e-8, so sinc = 0.5 exactly and _su2_x == theta/2 to the last bit for all 154 decades j=8..161 (first_inexact = -1, none). A Taylor switch would return (1, omega/2), which is precisely what the full formula already computes exactly; the shipped fallback returns (1, 0), the ZEROTH-order truncation, which is a different and strictly worse thing. (4) NOT covered by an existing test: I snapshotted src+tests, flipped line 151 to F64_TINY, and ran all five suites both ways — 416/359/1827/233/776 = 3611 passed, 0 failed, IDENTICAL on both sides; no assertion in the repo touches the changed region (zero omega still returns identity, verified directly: w = 0x3ff0000000000000, x = 0x0). (5) The scale test DOES discriminate — measured first-collapse decade per candidate threshold, where "collapse" is the ratio 2*_su2_x/theta dropping below 0.5: 1e-6 -> j=7, sqrt(DBL_EPSILON) 1.49e-8 -> j=9, shipped 1e-12 -> j=13, 1e-15 -> j=16, DBL_EPSILON -> j=16, 1e-100 -> j=101, DBL_MIN -> never over j=0..161. The step is confirmed as a discontinuity, not rounding: theta=1e-12 gives _su2_x = 0x3d619799812dea12 (exactly theta/2), theta=1e-13 gives 0x0 where the truth 0x3d2c25c268497683 is an ordinary normal double. The broken covariance is not a change of units (an angle has none) — it is the exponential map's own one-parameter-subgroup homogeneity, deg-1 in the tangent part, the same property 2.10.0 used to catch geo_ray_sphere. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING'S OWN INSTRUMENT, both measured: (a) its assertion "_su2_x == theta/2 to within 1 ulp for j = 0..160" is FALSE ON CORRECT CODE for j=0..7 — at theta=1, sin(0.5)/1 = 0.479425538604203, a 4.1% deviation, and j=7 is still 3 ulp out; written as stated it would fail the repair and get the repair reverted; (b) its companion leg "_su2_w == f64_cos(theta/2)" is VACUOUS over the entire defect region — cos(theta/2) rounds to exactly 1.0 for every theta <= 1e-8, which is also what the fabricated identity returns, so the w leg cannot see this defect anywhere it exists. The tangent part is the only discriminator.
defects.fabricates: su2_identity() = (1,0,0,0) — a valid, unit, plausible quaternion, returned as a normal pointer with no error channel and no way for a caller to tell it apart from a genuine near-identity result. It is unit length, so any "is the result normalised" assertion agrees with it; only DIRECTION discriminates. Composed N times it is still the identity, so an integrator taking 1e6 steps of 1e-13 rad ends exactly where it started instead of 1e-7 rad away, and a Lie-derivative or finite-difference probe with h < 1e-12 reads exactly zero, making exp/log non-invertible near 0.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000, already defined at src/error.cyr:45) on `norm` — exactly what makes the sinc division fail and nothing more. Measured refinement: because f64_sqrt of the smallest positive subnormal is 2.2e-162 and the sum-of-squares underflows to 0 below that, this expression never yields a subnormal, so on THIS site F64_TINY is exactly equivalent to `norm == 0.0` — and at norm == 0 the identity fallback is not a fabrication but the true exponential, so the existing return stays. Verified non-breaking: 3611/3611 assertions across hisab/foundation/modules/edge_cases/abuse pass unchanged with the flip applied. Two scope notes that the repair must not be mistaken for: repairing line 151 does NOT repair the SE(3) path — se3_exp (lie_ext.cyr:443) short-circuits on its own EPSILON_F64 before ever calling su2_exp — and the sibling absolute guards on the same quantity in this pair of files (lie.cyr:79 su2_from_quat, :100 su2_from_axis_angle, :172 su2_log, :399 lorentz_boost, :440 lorentz_rotate; lie_ext.cyr:200 so3_exp, :215 so3_log, :443 se3_exp) are separate sites, of which so3_exp's must move with su2_exp's if the pinned double-cover invariant su2_to_rotation_matrix(su2_exp(w)) == so3_exp(w) is to stay exact below 1e-12.
defects.scale_test: DEGREE-1 HOMOGENEITY OF THE TANGENT PART, in the corrected form (the filing's literal wording fails on correct code — see `why`). For n_hat = (1,0,0) and theta = 10^-j, j = 0..161: assert the RATIO r = 2*_su2_x(su2_exp(theta*n_hat))/theta stays near 1 — a plain `r > 0.5` is enough to discriminate every candidate and needs no closed form, since the fabrication drives r to exactly 0 while the truth is 1 - theta^2/24 (r = 0.9589 at j=0, and >= 1-1e-16 from j=8 down). Tighten the tail with the bit-exact leg, which measurement says holds with no slack at all: for j = 8..161, _su2_x MUST equal f64_mul(theta, F64_HALF) EXACTLY (measured: 0 mismatches over all 154 decades under DBL_MIN). Do NOT assert exactness for j = 0..7 (sinc genuinely differs there) and do NOT rely on the _su2_w leg at all (cos(theta/2) == 1.0 exactly for theta <= 1e-8, so it agrees with the fabricated identity). MEASURED first-collapse decade, which is the bracketing proof: 1e-6 -> j=7, 1.49e-8 -> j=9, 1e-12 (shipped) -> j=13, 1e-15 -> j=16, DBL_EPSILON -> j=16, 1e-100 -> j=101, DBL_MIN -> never; so the j=0..161 span brackets every threshold a repair might plausibly choose and only DBL_MIN survives it. Stop at j=161: at j=162 ox*ox underflows to 0 so norm reads 0x0 (measured), which is the norm expression's own limit, not this guard's. UNIT-FREE GROUP LEG (put this one in the suite, it needs no closed form) — but not as the filing writes it, which is both infeasible and false on correct code: use repeated SQUARING, q_k = su2_exp(omega/2^k) composed with itself 2^k times via k squarings, k = 0..520 (520 compositions total, versus the 10^12 su2_compose calls and 32 TB of never-freed 32-byte allocations the "N = 10^j composed N times" form literally demands), and assert |_su2_x(q_k) - _su2_x(su2_exp(omega))| < 1e-6, NOT equality. The tolerance is load-bearing and measured: composition rounding alone plateaus at 1.786e-9 for every k >= 30, so my own first run of this leg at a 1e-9 tolerance reported failure at k=26 for EVERY threshold including DBL_MIN — the instrument, not the code. At 1e-6 it brackets cleanly, first-failing k = 20 / 27 / 40 / 50 / 53 / 333 / never for 1e-6 / 1.49e-8 / 1e-12 / 1e-15 / DBL_EPSILON / 1e-100 / DBL_MIN, with the shipped guard deviating by 0.4794 (total collapse) against that 1.79e-9 floor.

defects.guarded_quantity: |sin(ganita_f64_acos(w))| where w = f64_clamp(_su2_w(s), -1, 1), the scalar part of a unit quaternion. Dimensionless, bounded in [0,1], degree 0 — it does NOT scale with any unit choice, so no scale sweep applies. Mathematically it equals |v| = sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2), but it is COMPUTED through acos(w), whose input has already lost the information: w = cos(theta/2) rounds to exactly +-1.0 for all theta within 2.1e-8 of 0 or 2*pi.
defects.protects: the division sc = f64_div(theta, sin_half) at src/lie.cyr:176 (and notionally sin_half == 0 exactly at w = +1). Per src/error.cyr:40-45's own rule — F64_TINY when the guard protects a DIVISION whose only failure is a zero/subnormal denominator, EPSILON_F64 only for a genuinely dimensionless bounded quantity — this is the division case, and the bounded-quantity exemption does not rescue it because the bounded quantity is a destroyed proxy for the divisor that matters.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FAILED, and the measurements strengthen the filing rather than weaken it. (1) "Dimensionless/bounded, so an absolute epsilon is correct" — the dimensional half is TRUE (degree 0, no scaling axis, so DEFECT_ABSOLUTE_ON_SCALING is the wrong label and a scale sweep is meaningless here) but it does not save the guard, because the number is not the variable. MEASURED on the shipped binary (probe3): sin(acos(w)) = 0.0 at w = +1, 1.2246063538223773e-16 at w = -1, 1.4901161193847656e-08 at w = 0x3FEFFFFFFFFFFFFF (largest double < 1), 1.490116131630829e-08 at w = 0xBFEFFFFFFFFFFFFF. The reachable set is {0} U {1.22e-16} U [1.49e-08, 1] — EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 sits in the hole, so the guard fires IFF w == +-1.0 exactly, and every threshold in (1.23e-16, 1.49e-8) is behaviourally identical. (2) "The caller normalises" — it does, and that is the CAUSE, not the cure: unit-ness is exactly what forces w to round to +-1.0. (3) "It is a convergence tolerance" — no, it guards a divide at line 176. (4) "The repair breaks an existing test" — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED (probe2, built against src/lie.cyr + src/lie_ext.cyr): modules.tcyr:5918-5921 su2_log(su2_exp(lw)), lw = (1/3,1/2,1/5), shipped x-bits 4599676419421066580 vs repaired ...582 (true value ...581) — 1-2 ulp apart against LOOSE_TOL_M = 1e-8, eight orders of slack; modules.tcyr:5934-5938 se3_log's omega is bit-identical to that same pair; abuse.tcyr:2528-2529 identity returns (0,0,0) and a non-null pointer under BOTH. Nothing flips. (5) "The scale_test does not discriminate" — PARTLY TRUE, and it is the one real correction: the claimed mirror leg theta = pi - 10^-j probes w -> 0, the BEST-conditioned point, not w -> -1; MEASURED, shipped and repaired agree bit-for-bit at every j = 0..19 on that leg, and theta saturates at pi from j >= 16, so the leg kills zero mutants. The true w -> -1 mirror is theta = 2*pi - 10^-j (see scale_test). DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE that the threshold is not the variable (probe4): with the guard DELETED — which is where "lower EPSILON_F64 to DBL_MIN" and every other threshold choice lands — q = su2_from_axis_angle(x_hat, 1e-8) returns NaN and q = su2_from_axis_angle(x_hat, 2*pi - 1e-8) returns 256538985.08980078 rad, while the shipped guard returns 0.0 and the truth is 1e-08 and 6.283185297179586. NO value of the threshold produces a correct answer at either input; the atan2(|v|, w) form returns both bit-exactly.
defects.fabricates: hvec3_new(0,0,0) — "this element is the identity, there is no rotation" — with a valid Vec3 pointer and rc = 0, on BOTH branches, and the -1 branch is far worse than originally filed. w -> +1 branch: every rotation of magnitude <= 2.1e-8 rad about any axis (MEASURED: theta = 1e-8 about x_hat holds x = 5e-9, a normal double, and returns exactly 0x0). w -> -1 branch: every theta >= 2*pi - 2.1e-8, where the function's OWN convention (theta = 2*acos(w) in [0, 2*pi], which it honours at theta = 2*pi - 1e-7) says the answer is ~6.2832 — an absolute fabrication of a full 2*pi rad, i.e. relative error 1.0, MEASURED as ol=0x0 at j = 8..19 on the 2*pi leg. And on that same branch the acos path is already wrong BEFORE the guard ever fires, with no error channel: theta = 2*pi - 1e-6 returns 6.282905038986482 (4.4e-5 relative), theta = 2*pi - 1e-7 returns 6.356724824889811 — 0.0735 rad, 4.2 DEGREES wrong — against a bit-exact repaired result. A pose solver measuring residual as ||su2_log(dR)|| reads exactly 0.0 ("converged, bit-exact") at up to 2.1e-8 rad of true residual, or reads 0.0 for a near-2*pi element; a finite-difference or Lie-derivative probe at the identity reads exactly zero gradient.
defects.correct_threshold: Guard the divisor that actually carries the answer: vnorm = sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z) compared against F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN — vnorm >= 0, so no f64_abs is needed), and recover the angle as theta = 2*ganita_f64_atan2(vnorm, w) instead of 2*ganita_f64_acos(w); then sc = theta/vnorm, which tends to 2 smoothly as vnorm -> 0 with the error in vnorm cancelling between numerator and denominator. THE REPAIR IS A CHANGE OF QUANTITY, NOT OF NUMBER: leaving acos in place and lowering EPSILON_F64 to DBL_MIN measurably makes it worse, not better (NaN on the +1 branch, 2.57e8 rad on the -1 branch — probe4). MEASURED behaviour of the repaired form: bit-exact round trip for theta = 10^-j at j = 0..161 (j = 162 returns 0 for both forms, because x*x underflows to +0 there — a separate limitation of the plain sum-of-squares norm, not of this guard); bit-exact on the whole theta = 2*pi - 10^-j leg, j = 0..19; branch convention preserved (atan2(vnorm, w) is in (pi/2, pi) for w < 0, so theta stays in (pi, 2*pi) exactly as 2*acos(w) did — j = 0 of that leg agrees bit-for-bit with shipped); within 1-2 ulp of shipped on every existing test input. The one remaining (0,0,0) return is vnorm == 0 exactly, i.e. q = +-1: correct for +1, and for -1 it is a genuine mathematical ambiguity (every axis at angle 2*pi maps there), which shipped and repaired answer identically. Keeping the f64_clamp on w is harmless — atan2 has no domain restriction — but is no longer load-bearing.
defects.scale_test: ⚠ A THRESHOLD SWEEP CANNOT DISCRIMINATE THIS ONE (the reachable set has a hole from 1.23e-16 to 1.49e-8 and 1e-12 lies inside it), and ⚠ THE ORIGINALLY FILED MIRROR LEG IS WRONG AND MUST BE REPLACED: theta = pi - 10^-j drives w -> 0, the best-conditioned point, and MEASURED shipped == repaired bit-for-bit at every j (plus theta saturates at pi from j >= 16), so it kills nothing. Use TWO legs, both with a UNIT axis so su2_from_axis_angle's own len guard provably cannot fire and its components are exactly (cos(theta/2), sin(theta/2), 0, 0). Leg A (w -> +1): q = su2_from_axis_angle(hvec3_new(1,0,0), 10^-j), assert su2_log(q) == (10^-j, 0, 0) to 4 ulp RELATIVE, j = 0..161. Leg B (w -> -1, the true mirror): theta = 2*pi - 10^-j over j = 0..19, assert su2_log(q) == (theta, 0, 0) to 4 ulp relative. MEASURED TODAY on the shipped binary: leg A round-trips bit-exactly for j = 0..7 and returns exactly 0x0 for every j = 8..161; leg B is already 1.7e-10 relative off at j = 3, 2.9e-9 at j = 4, 4.4e-5 at j = 6, 1.17e-2 (4.2 degrees) at j = 7, then exactly 0x0 for j = 8..19 — so leg B fails even a LOOSE_TOL_M = 1e-8 ABSOLUTE assertion from j = 4, four decades above the cliff, which is the earliest available discriminator. Together the legs bracket every repair a maintainer might reach for, and every acos-based variant fails at the SAME j on leg A — shipped 1e-12, sqrt(DBL_EPSILON) = 1.49e-8, DBL_EPSILON = 2.2e-16, 1e-100 — which is the signature that says "the threshold is not the defect". The two mutants a narrow test would let live, both MEASURED: (i) guard deleted / threshold lowered to DBL_MIN returns NaN on leg A and 256538985.08980078 on leg B — note a mere "result is not exactly zero" assertion PASSES this mutant on leg B, so the assertion must be the relative-error one; (ii) any acos-based variant with a different constant, which is bit-identical to shipped. Only the atan2(vnorm, w) form with the guard on vnorm passes both legs. Stop leg A at j = 161: at j = 162 the x*x+y*y+z*z sum-of-squares underflows to +0 on its own (a scaled/hypot norm would carry it to ~1e-300), a separate limitation that must not be charged to this guard.
defects.disposition: DEFERRED — needs a small-angle SERIES, not a threshold. Lowering the guard alone introduces a NEW defect: the log/exp maps divide by theta^2 and theta^3, and at theta <= 2.2e-162 both theta*theta and 1-cos(theta) are exactly 0, so the coefficient becomes 0/0 = NaN. Grouped with so3_log (lie_ext:215/:220), se3_exp (:443) and se3_log (:477), which were never on this list but have the same shape.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = f64_sqrt(nx^2+ny^2+nz^2) — the Euclidean LENGTH of the caller's boost-direction Vec3 `dir`. Dimension: length^1, homogeneous of degree 1 in the caller's unit choice (mm vs m: x1000; AU vs m: x1.5e-11). REFUTATION ATTEMPT 1 FAILED: it is not dimensionless and not bounded — `dir` is a raw public-API parameter, and the function's own comment (lie.cyr:395, "dir is a Vec3 (will be normalized)") states that the function, not the caller, does the normalising, i.e. the magnitude is by construction arbitrary. REFUTATION ATTEMPT 2 FAILED: there are ZERO internal callers (`grep -n "lorentz_boost(" src/` returns only the definition), so no caller pre-normalises. REFUTATION ATTEMPT 3 FAILED: it is not a convergence tolerance — the guarded statement is one line above `var inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm);`.
defects.protects: The division `inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm)` at lie.cyr:402, used to normalise the direction before building Lambda^0_i = n_i*sinh(eta) and Lambda^i_j = delta_ij + (cosh(eta)-1)*n_i*n_j.
defects.why: NOT REFUTED — confirmed by execution against the shipped source. The contract is scale-free (only the DIRECTION of `dir` is meaningful), yet the arbitrary magnitude is tested against a fixed absolute 1e-12 (EPSILON_F64 = 0x3D719799812DEA11, src/error.cyr:26), so the identical physical boost is honoured at |dir| = 1 and silently discarded at |dir| = 1e-13. MEASURED on the 2.13.0 tree under cycc 6.6.2 (probe.tcyr/probe2.tcyr, 22/22 assertions pass): lorentz_boost(hvec3_new(0x3D3C25C268497682 /* exactly 1e-13 */, 0, 0), eta=1) returns L00 = 0x3ff0000000000000 and L10 = 0x0, against the 0x3ff8b07551d9f550 (cosh 1) and 0x3ff2cd9fc44eb982 (sinh 1) the same call with dir = (1,0,0) returns — the claim's literal MEASURED string reproduces bit for bit. On an exact power-of-two ladder k = 2^-j the guard first fabricates at j = 40 (k = 9.09e-13) and only 40 of the 538 representable rungs are honoured; 498 rungs of perfectly well-determined direction are discarded. The division itself fails only at norm == 0 — and because norm is a SQRT, it can never even be subnormal (sqrt of the smallest positive subnormal is 2.2227587494850775e-162, a normal number; asserted directly as `f64_lt(f64_sqrt(1), F64_TINY) == 0`), so 1/norm is finite for every nonzero norm and the guard fires ~296 decades above anything that can fail. This is the same class the repo already repaired in `hvec3_angle` (src/vec3.cyr:198) under its own stated rule — "guard exactly what makes the operation fail and nothing more; a threshold that needs a scale chosen for it IS the defect" — with the constant already extracted as `F64_TINY` in src/error.cyr; lie.cyr was never swept. Sibling instances of the identical shape on the identical scale-free quantity: lie.cyr:441 (`lorentz_rotate`, same file, 42 lines down), lie.cyr:79 (`su2_from_quat`), lie.cyr:100 (`su2_from_axis_angle`). NOT a sibling: lie.cyr:151 (`su2_exp`), where `norm` is a rotation-vector ANGLE whose magnitude is meaningful — that one needs a separate small-angle analysis and must not be swept in with these.
defects.fabricates: lorentz_identity() — a valid, exactly Lorentzian 4x4 matrix returned with no error channel. MEASURED: `lorentz_is_valid()` on the fabricated matrix returns 1, so the repo's own validity predicate cannot detect the substitution (probe assertion A5). It does not perturb the requested boost, it DISCARDS it: a rapidity-1 boost (v = 0.7616c) becomes "no boost". The magnitude is independent of eta — MEASURED: eta = 10 (gamma = 11013) is dropped just as silently (probe assertion D1). ⚠ Separate, adjacent fabrication found while bracketing the upward leg and explicitly NOT scored against this guard: at |dir| >= 2^512 (1.34e154) the nx*nx+ny*ny+nz*nz sum OVERFLOWS to +Inf, so norm = Inf, inv = 0, n = (0,0,0), and the function returns L00 = cosh(eta) with a unit spatial block and zero off-diagonals — a matrix that is not even Lorentzian. That is a defect in the norm EXPRESSION (no hypot-style scaling), not in this threshold.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY — the constant ALREADY DEFINED at src/error.cyr (0x0010000000000000, DBL_MIN), the smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is still finite, i.e. exactly what makes `f64_div(F64_ONE, norm)` fail and nothing more. No new constant is needed and no `f64_abs` is needed (a sqrt result is never negative): `if (f64_lt(norm, F64_TINY) == 1) { return lorentz_identity(); }`. ⭐ SHARPENED by measurement: because norm is a SQRT it is never subnormal, so on this function `norm < F64_TINY` is EXACTLY `norm == 0`, and every threshold at or below 2.2227587494850775e-162 is behaviourally indistinguishable (1e-300 also never fires). F64_TINY is therefore chosen by the project's stated rule and by consistency with vec3.cyr:198 / calc_ext.cyr:434 / autodiff.cyr:71 — NOT because the ladder singles it out. REFUTATION ATTEMPT 4 FAILED (checked, not assumed): the repair breaks no existing assertion. The only tiny-direction test in tests/*.tcyr is abuse.tcyr:2533, `assert_neq(lorentz_boost(hvec3_zero(), F64_ONE), 0, "zero direction allocates")` — with norm = 0 the F64_TINY guard STILL fires and still returns an allocated identity, so it still passes (asserted directly, probe E1); foundation.tcyr:1225 uses hvec3_unit_x() (norm = 1), unaffected. Secondary, and genuinely out of this guard's scope: the sum of squares underflows to 0 below |dir| ~ 1.11e-162 and overflows to +Inf above |dir| ~ 1.34e154; carrying the scale-free contract past those needs a scaled/hypot norm, not a different threshold.
defects.scale_test: HOMOGENEITY OF DEGREE 0 IN THE DIRECTION: lorentz_boost(k*dir, eta) must be BIT-IDENTICAL to lorentz_boost(dir, eta) for every k > 0. ⛔ THE ORIGINALLY-PROPOSED DECIMAL LADDER IS UNSOUND AS WRITTEN AND MUST NOT BE USED — MEASURED on the real tree: at k = 1e-5, 1e-9 and 1e-11 the guard does NOT fire (rungs are honoured) yet L10 comes back 0x3ff2cd9fc44eb981, one ULP BELOW sinh(1), because nx = k*fl(1/f64_sqrt(k*k)) is not exactly 1.0 for those k. A bit-exact L10 assertion on a decimal ladder therefore FAILS ON CORRECTLY REPAIRED CODE at j = 5, 9, 11 (probe assertions G1-G3). USE AN EXACT POWER-OF-TWO LADDER instead, built by repeated exact halving/doubling from 1.0 — MEASURED: L00 and L10 are bit-exact on every honoured rung of both legs (probe B3, C1, C2), so both assertions are sound. TEST: fix dir = hvec3_new(k,0,0), eta = 1. DOWNWARD leg k = 2^-j, j = 0..537 (538 rungs; stop at 537 — at j = 538, k = 1.11e-162 and nx*nx underflows to 0, which is the norm expression's limit, not this guard's). UPWARD leg k = 2^+j, j = 0..511 (512 rungs; stop at 511 — at j = 512, k = 1.34e154 and nx*nx overflows to +Inf, again the expression, not the guard). On all 1050 rungs assert m4_get(L,0,0) == 0x3ff8b07551d9f550 AND m4_get(L,1,0) == 0x3ff2cd9fc44eb982 bit-exactly. MEASURED against shipped code: downward leg honours only j = 0..39 and fabricates the identity on j = 40..537 (498 failures); upward leg is clean, which is what makes the downward leg's asymmetry the finding. BRACKETING (measured first-firing rung on the 2^-j ladder, so the ladder brackets every threshold a repair might plausibly choose): 1e-6 at j = 20, sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)=1.49e-8 at j = 27, the shipped 1e-12 at j = 40, 1e-15 at j = 50, DBL_EPSILON=2.2e-16 at j = 53, 1e-100 at j = 333 — and F64_TINY/DBL_MIN never fires anywhere before the norm expression itself underflows at j = 538. SECOND LEG (proves the fabrication is unbounded, not a perturbation): hold k = 1e-13 and sweep eta over 1e-3 .. 1e1; every one returns L00 = 0x3ff0000000000000. ⚠ DO NOT assert `lorentz_is_valid(L) == 1` anywhere in this test — MEASURED (probe A5): the fabricated identity PASSES lorentz_is_valid, so that assertion discriminates nothing, exactly as asserting unit length failed to discriminate the fabricated quaternion identity in 2.11.1. The discriminating property is DIRECTION AND MAGNITUDE OF THE BOOST, i.e. the L00/L10 bit compare.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = f64_sqrt(nx^2+ny^2+nz^2) — the Euclidean LENGTH of the caller's rotation axis. Dimension: length^1, homogeneous of degree 1 in the axis; changes by 1000 between metres and millimetres. Not bounded, not dimensionless, not normalised anywhere upstream: `lorentz_rotate` has exactly ONE call site in the entire tree (tests/foundation.tcyr:1226) and is a public entry point of dist/hisab.cyr, so the magnitude is whatever the consumer hands in.
defects.protects: the division inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) on the very next line (src/lie.cyr:443), used to normalise the axis. It is a divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance — there is no iteration in this function.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FIVE FAIL, THREE OF THEM BY MEASUREMENT ON THE REAL BINARY (cycc 6.6.2, probe under scratchpad/eps/refute/, built against src/lie.cyr unmodified). (1) Bounded/dimensionless? No — `norm` is length^1 and the comment at src/lie.cyr:436 states the contract, "axis is Vec3 (normalized internally)", so only the direction carries meaning and the magnitude is arbitrary by construction. (2) Caller normalises? No — one call site tree-wide, and it is a bundled public API. (3) Convergence tolerance? No — it guards a reciprocal two lines below. (4) Would F64_TINY break an existing test? MEASURED NO: the only assertion in tests/ that reaches this function is `assert_eq(lorentz_is_valid(lorentz_rotate(hvec3_unit_z(), F64_PI_2)), 1)` and hvec3_unit_z() has norm exactly 1.0, far above both thresholds. Worse, that assertion is non-discriminating: measured, lorentz_is_valid(lorentz_identity()) = 1 AND lorentz_is_valid(lorentz_rotate(1e-13*x_hat, pi/2)) = 1, so the tree's lone test returns 1 for the fabrication and could never have caught this. (5) Does the scale_test discriminate the thresholds? Yes for the thresholds — but the claim's ASSERTION FORM is unsound and its RANGE is scoped to miss a second fabrication; both are corrected below. The claimed measurement itself is CONFIRMED exactly: k=1 gives m4_get(R,2,2) = 0x3c91a60000000000 and m4_get(R,3,2) = 0xbff0000000000000; the guard fires from k < 1e-12 (first identity at j=13) returning bit-exact 0x3ff0000000000000 / 0x0. (My own first instrument was the wrong one and I checked it before believing it: a libm C simulation gave cos(pi/2) = 0x3c91a62633145c07, disagreeing with the claim — because hisab's f64_cos is a cycc polyfill, not libm. The claim's hex was right and my sim was measuring a different function.) Non-axis-aligned confirmation: axis = (1e-13, 1e-13, 1e-13), norm = 1.73e-13, also returns the bit-exact identity, so this is not an artifact of a single-component axis.
defects.fabricates: lorentz_identity() — a valid Lorentz matrix, rc = 0, no error channel; MEASURED lorentz_is_valid() = 1 on it, so the repo's own validity predicate certifies the fabrication. A requested 90-degree spatial rotation becomes no rotation at all, and the fabrication is independent of `angle`, so a pi rotation is dropped as silently as a small one. ⚠ A SECOND, DISTINCT FABRICATION LIVES AT THE OTHER END AND THE CLAIM MISSED IT: when the SUM OF SQUARES overflows while no component does — measured at axis = (1e200, 1e200, 0), and on a single component from k >= 1e155 — norm = +Inf, `f64_lt(norm, EPSILON_F64)` is FALSE so the guard does not fire, inv = 1/Inf = 0, the axis normalises to (0,0,0), and the function returns diag(1, cos t, cos t, cos t): R22 = 0x3c91a60000000000, R32 = 0x0. That is neither the identity nor a rotation; lorentz_is_valid() = 0 on it. Swapping the threshold does NOT fix this arm.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308) on `norm` — the constant this repo already established for exactly this rule at src/geo.cyr:26 (_GEO_F64_TINY) and src/autodiff.cyr:17 (_AD_F64_TINY): guard exactly what makes the division fail and nothing more. It is the right bound in both directions — norm >= DBL_MIN implies 1/norm <= 4.49e307 < DBL_MAX, so the reciprocal cannot overflow either. ⚠ BUT F64_TINY ALONE IS AN INCOMPLETE REPAIR, and this is the sharpening the original claim needs: it leaves the +Inf arm above entirely live (measured: axis = (1e200,1e200,0) still returns a non-Lorentzian diag(1,cos t,cos t,cos t) with rc = 0). The guard must be `norm` finite AND >= F64_TINY, i.e. reject non-finite norm explicitly — or, better and fixing both ends at once, hoist by m = max(|nx|,|ny|,|nz|) before squaring, so the sum of squares can neither overflow nor underflow and the only unrecoverable case is m == 0. Without the hoist there remains an honest floor no threshold can lift: at axis = (1e-200,1e-200,0) the sum of squares underflows to +0 before the guard is reached, so norm == 0 and every threshold including DBL_MIN fires (measured: identity, valid = 1). Note also lorentz_boost (src/lie.cyr:399) and lie.cyr:79/100/151 carry the identical shape and must be repaired in the same pass.
defects.scale_test: ⛔ THE CLAIM'S SCALE_TEST IS DEFECTIVE AS WRITTEN AND MUST NOT BE USED — MEASURED. It asserts m4_get(R,3,2) is BIT-IDENTICAL to 0xbff0000000000000 for every k, and that assertion FAILS ON THE SHIPPED CODE at scales the guard never touches: R32 comes back 0xbfefffffffffffff (1 ULP below -1.0) at k = 1e-5, 1e-9, 1e-11 and at 22 of the 151 positive decades (1e11, 1e21, 1e26, 1e30, 1e37, 1e38, 1e42, 1e58, 1e65, 1e88, 1e99, 1e104, 1e111, 1e121, 1e128, 1e136, 1e141, 1e148, 1e150, 1e151, 1e152). Cause: nx_hat = k * fl(1/fl(sqrt(fl(k*k)))) rounds 1 ULP low; it is normalisation rounding, not the guard, and a correct F64_TINY repair does not change it. WHICH decades fail depends on how k is generated (repeated /10 gave j=5,10; ganita_f64_pow gave j=5,9,11), so the failure set is not even stable. As written the test reports ~25 false failures on BOTH sides of the repair and cannot distinguish the guard defect from rounding. CORRECTED TEST — HOMOGENEITY OF DEGREE 0 IN THE AXIS. Fix axis = hvec3_new(1,0,0), angle = F64_PI_2. Per k, assert TWO legs: (A) m4_get(R,2,2) == 0x3c91a60000000000 BIT-EXACT. This entry is cos(angle) + (1-cos)*ny*ny with ny = 0, so it is mathematically independent of k and MEASURED bit-stable across all 341 decades j = -170..+170 whenever the guard does not fire; the fabricated identity gives 0x3ff0000000000000, so leg A is exactly discriminating and needs no tolerance. Never assert on R11 or on R22-of-the-rotation-axis, which agree with the identity and let every mutant live. (B) m4_get(R,3,2) within 1 ULP of -1.0, i.e. bits in {0xbfefffffffffffff, 0xbff0000000000000, 0xbff0000000000001} — a set membership, NOT a bit-equality. Leg B is what kills the +Inf arm, where R32 = 0x0. RANGE: k = 10^-j for j = 0..161 and k = 10^+j for j = 0..170 — the claim capped the positive leg at 150 and thereby scoped the test so it could not see the overflow fabrication at all; it must run past 1e154. MEASURED bracketing of every threshold a repair might plausibly choose: 1e-6 fails at j=6, 1.49e-8 at j=8, the shipped 1e-12 at j=13, 1e-15 at j=15, 2.2e-16 at j=16, 1e-100 at j=100 — all on leg A; and the unguarded +Inf arm fails on leg B from j=+155. Only "finite AND >= F64_TINY" survives both legs over the whole range. Stop the negative leg at j=161: at j >= 162 the sum of squares underflows to +0 (measured norm = 0 exactly), so no threshold below ~1.5e-162 is distinguishable through this entry point — state that limit rather than papering over it. Third leg, mixed magnitudes, which single-component scaling cannot reach: assert leg A + leg B on axis = (1e200, 1e200, 0) (currently returns the non-Lorentzian diag, lorentz_is_valid = 0) and record axis = (1e-200, 1e-200, 0) as the known underflow floor. Fourth leg: hold k = 1e-13 and sweep angle over 1e-3 .. pi, asserting the result is bit-identical to lorentz_identity() at every angle, to show the whole rotation is discarded rather than perturbed. ⚠ Do NOT gate any of this on lorentz_is_valid(): measured 1 for the fabricated identity, so it is blind to the defect that matters.

defects.guarded_quantity: norm = f64_sqrt(nx*nx + ny*ny + nz*nz), the Euclidean LENGTH of the caller's axis vector (dimension length^1, in the caller's own units). Unbounded dynamic range in both directions, and its magnitude carries zero information: lines 122-123 compute inv = 1/norm and divide it straight back out. Only the DIRECTION survives into the Rodrigues formula.
defects.protects: the single division inv = f64_div(F64_ONE, norm) at src/lie_ext.cyr:122 (one division, then three multiplies that consume it).
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE GROUNDS; ALL FAIL. (1) NOT BOUNDED: the quantity is a raw length with free scale. The file makes the bounded-quantity argument explicitly for a DIFFERENT constant 20 lines earlier -- _SO3_ORTHO_TOL, lie_ext.cyr:26-31: "Every entry of a rotation matrix is bounded by 1, so an ABSOLUTE tolerance is the right scale here -- there is no dynamic range to normalise against." That sentence is exactly what line 119 cannot say. (2) NO CALLER NORMALISES: the only in-tree call site is so3_exp (lie_ext.cyr:203), which passes the UN-normalised rotation vector omega with theta = |omega|; and so3_exp guards theta against the same 1e-12 first, so line 119's guard never fires on that path -- the only way to reach it with a nonzero axis is a DIRECT public call. so3_from_axis_angle is exported in dist/hisab.cyr to 10 SHA-locked consumers with no unit-axis precondition documented anywhere in the file. (3) NOT A CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE: one-shot division, no iteration. (4) DOES NOT BREAK AN EXISTING TEST -- CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: sandbox copy, line 119 mutated EPSILON_F64 -> F64_TINY, mutation proven installed by grep, all five suites run: modules 1827/1827, abuse 776/776, edge_cases 233/233, hisab 416/416, foundation 359/359 = 3611 passed, 0 failed. The one test that touches this function (tests/modules.tcyr:7611) uses hvec3_unit_z(), |axis| = 1; abuse.tcyr:2530-2531 exercises so3_exp(hvec3_zero()), where norm = 0 and BOTH thresholds fire. (5) THE SCALE TEST IS FLAWED, BUT AGAINST THE FILING, NOT THE DEFECT -- see scale_test below. MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED TREE (sandbox copy of src/, unmutated, cyrius 6.6.2), axis (0,0,2^k), angle 0.5, correct R[0][1] = sin(0.5) = 0x3fdeaee8744b05f0 and R[0][0] = cos(0.5) = 0x3fec1528065b7d50: k = 0, -10, -20, -26, -30, -39 all bit-exact; k = -40 (9.0949e-13) and every k below it return R01 = 0x0, R00 = 0x3ff0000000000000, i.e. the identity. The cliff sits exactly on 1e-12. UNIT-FREE REACHABILITY (no exotic units needed, measured): build the axis the textbook way, as cross(a,b) of two UNIT vectors misaligned by eps -- |a x b| = sin(eps). eps = 1e-6, 1e-8, 1e-10, 1e-12 all return the correct sin(0.5); eps = 1e-14 gives |axis| = 1e-14 and returns the IDENTITY, for an axis whose direction (+z) is exact and whose reciprocal is finite. Every input on that path is dimensionless. The units argument is a second, independent route: a cross-product axis scales as length^2, so 1 mm edges give |a x b| ~ 1e-6 in metres (accepted, exact) and ~1e-12 in kilometres (on the cliff; halve the edge and it is 2.5e-13, rejected) -- same geometry, different answer. Nothing about 1e-12 relates to what fails: 1/norm is finite for every norm >= DBL_MIN.
defects.fabricates: TWO different fabrications, and the second is worse. LOW END (norm < 1e-12): m3_identity() -- a structurally valid rotation, returned with no rc and no error channel, so a caller cannot distinguish "no rotation was asked for" from "the axis was shorter than a hard-coded constant". It propagates into so3_compose / so3_log / se3_* as a genuine rotation and passes so3_from_mat3's membership check. HIGH END (|axis| >= 2^512 ~ 1.34e154, MEASURED, and NOT fixed by the threshold change): nx*nx overflows to +Inf, norm = +Inf, inv = 1/Inf = 0, so nx = ny = nz = 0 and the Rodrigues formula returns cos(0.5) * I -- measured R00 = 0x3fec1528065b7d50, R01 = 0x0. That is not the identity and not a rotation: det = cos^3(0.5) ~ 0.674, so it is the one fabrication so3_from_mat3 WOULD reject, silently manufactured by the constructor. The filing missed it because its sweep stops at 1e+150 < 2^512.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308) -- the project constant that exists for exactly this rule, whose own comment states it: "the right threshold when the guard protects a DIVISION and the only thing that can actually fail is a zero (or subnormal) denominator", as against "EPSILON_F64 remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity". VERIFIED BY MUTATION (sandbox copy, mutant proven installed by grep at :119): with EPSILON_F64 -> F64_TINY the probe returns bit-identical sin(0.5) AND cos(0.5) for every exact power of two from 2^-537 to 2^511 -- 1049 consecutive binades, including k = -40, -50, -100, -511, -537 where the shipped code returns the identity -- and all 3611 assertions across the five suites still pass. ⚠ THE THRESHOLD IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: the guard fixes the low end only, and only down to where the NAIVE sum-of-squares survives. Measured limits of the F64_TINY repair: 2^-538 still returns the identity (correctly -- (2^-538)^2 = 2^-1076 is below the smallest subnormal 2^-1074, so Sum x^2 flushes to 0 and norm really is 0), and 2^512 still returns cos(0.5)*I ((2^512)^2 = 2^1024 overflows to +Inf). Completing the repair means computing norm with a max-component prescale (hypot-style: divide by max|x| before squaring), which extends exactness to roughly [2^-1074, 2^1023] and removes the high-end fabrication as well. Guard first, prescale second; they are separable and the guard is the one this site is about.
defects.scale_test: ⛔ THE FILING'S PROPOSED TEST IS WRONG AND WOULD REJECT A CORRECT REPAIR -- REPLACE IT. Its "decimal half-decades over 1e-150...1e+150, R[0][1] BIT-IDENTICAL to the s=1 result" fails at ORDINARY scales for a reason that has nothing to do with the guard: normalisation rounding. MEASURED on the shipped tree with correctly-rounded decimal literals -- s = 1e-5 (0x3ee4f8b588e368f1), 1e-9 (0x3e112e0be826d695) and 1e-11 (0x3da5fd7fe1796495) ALL return R01 = 0x3fdeaee8744b05ef, one ulp below the s=1 answer 0x3fdeaee8744b05f0, because s*(1/sqrt(s*s)) = 0x1.fffffffffffffp-1 rather than 1.0. Simulating the filing's own sweep: 85 of its 601 samples are 1 ulp low, at scales up to 1e+42 and as high as 1e-2.5 -- seven or more orders above every candidate threshold. A DBL_MIN repair leaves all 85 exactly as they are, so the test fails a correct fix at 14% of its samples and reports a "defect" that is not one. CORRECT TEST -- EXACT POWERS OF TWO, where s*(1/sqrt(s*s)) is 1.0 by construction so the ONLY thing that can move the answer is the guard: for every integer k in [-537, +511], build the axis as the exact bit pattern (1023+k)*2^52 (i.e. 2^k), call so3_from_axis_angle(hvec3_new(0,0,2^k), 0.5) and assert BIT-EXACT R[0][1] == 0x3FDEAEE8744B05F0 and R[0][0] == 0x3FEC1528065B7D50 -- a bit compare, never f64_to and never a tolerance. 1049 samples, 3.32 per decade over 315 decades. IT BRACKETS EVERY THRESHOLD A REPAIR MIGHT PLAUSIBLY CHOOSE, each killed at the first power of two below it: 1e-6 at 2^-20 = 9.5e-7, sqrt(eps) = 1.49e-8 at 2^-27 = 7.5e-9, 1e-9 at 2^-30 = 9.3e-10, the CURRENT 1e-12 at 2^-40 = 9.09e-13 (measured: shipped code passes 2^-39 and returns identity at 2^-40), eps = 2.22e-16 at 2^-53 = 1.11e-16, 1e-100 at 2^-333, 1e-300 at 2^-997. Only a threshold at or below 2^-538 survives the whole sweep, and every such threshold is behaviourally identical here, so DBL_MIN is the honest one. MIRROR UPWARD: the sweep already runs to 2^511 = 6.7e153, which kills any repair that clamps large axes -- and it stops one binade short of the overflow rather than at the filing's arbitrary 1e+150, so it also DOCUMENTS the high-end fabrication instead of hiding it (2^512 returns cos(0.5)*I; assert that separately as a known-open second defect, or extend the sweep past 2^511 once the hypot prescale lands). BOTH BOUNDS ARE DERIVED, NOT FUDGED, unlike the filing's empirical 1e-150: 2^-537 squared is 2^-1074, exactly the smallest subnormal; 2^-538 squared is 2^-1076, which flushes to zero, so a correct guard legitimately returns the identity there and the sweep must not reach it. 2^512 squared is 2^1024, which overflows to +Inf.

defects.guarded_quantity: theta = |omega|, the rotation angle in radians of the caller-supplied so(3) element. Dimensionless — unchanged by any change of LENGTH units — but unbounded downward and not clamped to [0,pi]. Compared against EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 (error.cyr:26).
defects.protects: Nothing at this site. so3_exp performs no division; it returns m3_identity() or tail-calls so3_from_axis_angle(omega, theta). The only division on the path is inv = 1/norm at :119, whose owner carries an IDENTICAL guard on the IDENTICAL quantity at the IDENTICAL threshold. MEASURED, not inferred: build B (":200" mutated to F64_TINY, ":119" left at EPSILON_F64) produces output byte-identical to the shipped build across all 305 sweep points and all 7 spot values. The filed site is therefore unobservable in isolation — :119 is the site that binds.
defects.why: SUBSTANCE CONFIRMED, SCOPE AND EVIDENCE CORRECTED. I could not refute the core: the guard pair discards ~296 decades of exactly representable rotation and fabricates a plausible answer, which is the class error.cyr:28 itself defines (EPSILON_F64 is for a "dimensionless, BOUNDED quantity"; theta is dimensionless but unbounded downward, and the only thing that can actually fail is the 1/norm division at norm == 0, i.e. DBL_MIN). It is the same shape as 2.11.1's hquat_inverse/hquat_normalize repair. Measured on cyrius 6.6.2, omega = (0,0,t), reading m3_get(R,0,1) which must be sin(t): SHIPPED gives exactly 0 for t = 1e-13, 1e-20, 1e-100, 1e-150 and 276 of 305 half-decade points from 1e+2 down to 1e-150; with BOTH guards at F64_TINY the same sweep gives EXACTZERO = 0 — the general Rodrigues path is capable across the whole range, so the guard is the sole cause. FOUR CORRECTIONS to the filing. (1) The class label is a stretch and the filing admits it: theta does not move under a change of units, so this is not the geo.cyr scaling family; it is an absolute epsilon on an unbounded-range quantity whose divisor fails only at zero. (2) The motivation is arithmetically INVERTED: the guard cuts at 1e-12 rad = 0.206 microarcsecond, and 1 uas = 4.85e-12 rad, so every discarded rotation is SMALLER than a microarcsecond, not "two orders of magnitude larger". The sound motivation is the second one — a sub-stepped angular-velocity integrator (omega*dt < 1e-12) loses each step entirely, and the group law confirms the repaired path accumulates correctly (10 composed 1e-13 steps == so3_exp(1e-12) bit-exactly, diff = 0). (3) The stated round-trip impact is MISATTRIBUTED (see fabricates). (4) The repair cannot be applied at this site alone: on build C (so3 pair repaired, su2_exp untouched) the documented, test-pinned cover invariant su2_to_rotation_matrix(su2_exp(w)) == so3_exp(w) — asserted at modules.tcyr:5909 and stated at lie.cyr:147 — HOLDS today at w = (0,0,1e-13) because both sides fabricate identity, and is VIOLATED after the narrow repair (su2 gives 0, so3 gives 1e-13). The existing test samples only |w| ~ 0.63 and would not announce it. No existing test blocks the repair: abuse.tcyr:2530-2532's zero generator still returns a non-null identity with m3_get(Z,0,0) bit-equal to f64_from(1) on build C (0 < DBL_MIN), and modules.tcyr's so3/se3/su2 tests all use angles >= 0.2 rad under LOOSE_TOL_M.
defects.fabricates: m3_identity() — no rc, no error channel; the caller reads back "no rotation". ⚠ THE FILING'S ROUND-TRIP EVIDENCE IS MISATTRIBUTED AND MUST NOT BE USED AS THE ORACLE: so3_log(so3_exp((0,0,1e-13))).z == 0 is true, but it is NOT caused by this guard and is NOT fixed by repairing it. Measured on the FULLY REPAIRED build C, so3_log returns exactly 0 for every t from 1e-8 down to 1e-14 (last nonzero: t = 3.16e-8), because so3_log's own path takes theta = acos((tr(R)-1)/2) and tr(R) = 3 - theta^2 rounds to exactly 3 below theta ~ 1e-8, then hits its own EPSILON_F64 gate at :215. So the round trip reports 100% absent at 1e-9, 1e-10 and 1e-11 too — where :200 never fires — and still does after the repair. That is a separate defect at lie_ext.cyr:215/:220 (a trace-based log is the wrong formula at small angle; the unskew branch is the fix), and folding it into this finding overstates what repairing :200/:119 buys.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, error.cyr:47) — but the repair is a SET, not this line. Minimum correct change: (a) so3_from_axis_angle:119 -> F64_TINY, since that is the divisor's owner and the only site where anything can actually fail; (b) so3_exp:200 deleted outright (0 still routes to :119 and returns identity) or lowered to F64_TINY, otherwise it becomes the binding constraint the moment :119 is fixed; (c) su2_exp lie.cyr:151 and se3_exp lie_ext.cyr:443 -> F64_TINY in the same commit, or the cover invariant at lie.cyr:147 silently becomes false below 1e-12. No small-angle series is needed (unlike se3_exp's V matrix, which divides by theta^2/theta^3): measured bit-exact-or-1-ulp down to 1e-150. Do NOT extend below that in one step — below ~1e-154 the sum of squares in the norm goes subnormal, which is a real and separate limitation of the norm, not of the guard. Leave lie_ext.cyr:215/:220 (so3_log) OUT of this repair and file it separately — it needs a formula change, not a threshold change.
defects.scale_test: ⚠ THE FILED TEST DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE AT THIS SITE AND FALSE-FAILS ON A CORRECT REPAIR — both measured. (i) It cannot see the filed site: every threshold at or below 1e-12 installed at :200 (DBL_MIN, 1e-100, 2.22e-16, deletion) yields output byte-identical to the shipped 1e-12, because :119 fires first at the same value. Mutants MUST be installed at :119, or at both sites, and the harness must grep-prove the mutant is in place before believing a count. (ii) Bit-exact is too tight: on build C, 49 of the 305 half-decade points are exactly 1 ulp BELOW f64_sin(s) — s*(1/s) evaluates to 0.99999999999999989 in the axis renormalisation, so the entry is sin(s)*(1-1ulp). The filing's own measurement paragraph shows this (t=1e-11 -> 9.999999999999998e-12, labelled "1 ulp") and then specifies an assertion that rejects it. CORRECTED TEST: for s over every half-decade from 1e+2 to 1e-150 with omega = (0,0,s), assert |bits(m3_get(so3_exp(omega),0,1)) - bits(f64_sin(s))| <= 2 (ULP compare on the raw i64 patterns, never f64_to, which maps every one of these to 0), and assert the entry is NOT exactly 0 for any s in range — the not-zero clause is what kills the mutants, the 2-ulp clause is what stops the sweep false-failing. Bracketing is confirmed: a guard at 1e-6, 1.49e-8, 1e-9, 1e-12, 2.22e-16 or 1e-100 each produces an exact 0 inside this range and dies; only DBL_MIN and deletion survive (EXACTZERO = 0 measured). Keep the group law — so3_exp((0,0,1e-13)) composed 10 times equals so3_exp((0,0,1e-12)) with diff = 0 bits on build C, and yields 0 vs 1e-12 on the shipped tree, so it discriminates and pins the accumulation case the astrometry framing got wrong. ADD the cover invariant at tiny angle, absent from the filing and the reason a partial repair regresses silently: for the same s sweep, su2_to_rotation_matrix(su2_exp((0,0,s)))[0][1] must equal m3_get(so3_exp((0,0,s)),0,1) to <= 2 ulp — it passes vacuously on the shipped tree (both 0) and FAILS on a so3-only repair, which is exactly the mutant no existing test catches. DO NOT use so3_log as the oracle anywhere in this sweep: it returns exactly 0 for all |theta| <= 1e-8 even after a correct repair, so any so3_log-based assertion fails on the fix and passes on the defect.

defects.guarded_quantity: |A_ij| — f64_abs of one dense matrix entry read via ganita_mat_get, compared against EPSILON_F64 (= 1e-12, src/error.cyr:26) with f64_gt. Dimensions: whatever the caller's entries carry (stiffness N/m, compliance m/N, covariance, metres). Degree 1 in the problem scale: not squared, not normalised, not bounded, not a ratio.
defects.protects: Nothing that can fail. There is no division, sqrt, acos or iteration in this function — it is a sparsification DROP-tolerance choosing which entries are "structurally zero" (header comment, line 75). It cannot even be defended as protecting the allocation: it only makes count SMALLER, and the nnz = 0 / alloc(0) path is already exercised by tests/abuse.tcyr:915.
defects.protects_note: verified by reading the whole function body (lines 77-121): no arithmetic other than the compare itself.
defects.why: CONFIRMED by measurement; every refutation avenue was tried and closed. (1) Not dimensionless: the quantity is a raw caller matrix entry, degree 1 in the caller's unit, so re-expressing the same matrix in mm rather than m moves every entry by 1e3 and moves the SPARSITY PATTERN across a fixed 1e-12. (2) Not normalised by a caller: `csr_from_dense` has ZERO internal callers — grep over all of src/ finds the name only at its own definition line 77 — so it is a bare public entry point in dist/hisab.cyr reached directly by consumers, with no normalisation anywhere in the call chain. (3) Not a convergence tolerance: there is no loop to converge, no iterate, no residual; it is a one-shot data-structure conversion. (4) Measured on the shipped tree with a 4x4 fixture M0 (five dyadic nonzeros 1.0, 2^-10, 2^-5, 2^-10, 1.0; k = 5) scaled by c = 2^p: nnz is 5 at p = 0, +-20, -29 and +1000, falls to 3 at p = -30, and is 0 at every p <= -40 — a matrix whose entries are all ~1e-12..1e-13 converts to a structurally EMPTY CSR returned as a valid non-null handle. csr_spmv on it then returns exactly +0.0 for row 0 (bits 0) where the truth is 4427042831751708672 = 9.10e-13, with no error channel anywhere. (5) A NaN entry is silently dropped too (measured: f64_gt(f64_abs(NaN), EPSILON_F64) == 0, so a 2x2 with one NaN yields nnz = 1) — poisoned data is converted into a clean finite product. Because nothing here divides, there is no scale this guard could legitimately own; the only scale-free predicate for "structural zero" is exact equality with zero. Secondary notes, both verified: (a) the line-75 comment says "Drops entries with |value| < EPSILON_F64" while the code keeps only |v| > EPSILON_F64, i.e. it also drops |v| == EPSILON_F64; (b) the predicate is triplicated, not merely doubled — :88 (count) and :107 (emit) size and then fill the same alloc(count*8) buffers so any repair MUST change both in one edit or the emit pass writes past them (CWE-787), and csr_add:202 applies the IDENTICAL absolute drop to the merged sum while its two drain loops (lines 213-226) apply no drop at all, so csr_add is internally inconsistent about the very tolerance it claims — direct evidence this is not a principled sparsification.
defects.fabricates: A silently smaller matrix presented as a valid one: real entries omitted, and in the limit nnz = 0 handed back as a normal non-null CSR pointer so csr_spmv / csr_add / csr_transpose all answer the zero vector. Measured: csr_spmv row 0 returns bit-exact +0.0 where the correct value is 9.10e-13 (bits 4427042831751708672), a 100% relative error with rc/no error channel. Also fabricates finiteness: a NaN entry is dropped, so a poisoned matrix produces a clean finite product (measured nnz 1 instead of 2).
defects.correct_threshold: Exact zero, written as `f64_eq(v, f64_from(0)) == 0`, applied IDENTICALLY at :88 and :107 in one edit (and at csr_add:202). Three near-miss formulations are measurably wrong and must not be used: (i) `|v| >= DBL_MIN` — NOT equivalent to v != 0; it drops subnormals, measured nnz 5 -> 3 at c = 2^-1013 and 2 at c = 2^-1022 where the exact predicate keeps all 5; (ii) `f64_gt(f64_abs(v), f64_from(0))` — drops NaN (measured f64_gt(f64_abs(NaN), 0) == 0), converting poisoned data into a structural zero; (iii) a raw `load64(...) != 0` bit compare — KEEPS -0.0 (bits 0x8000000000000000) as a stored nonzero, whereas f64_eq(-0.0, 0.0) == 1 correctly drops it (both measured; this is exactly the negative-zero trap 2.13.0 already found in an antiparallel cross product). Verified non-breaking: ganita_mat_new zero-fills explicitly (lib/ganita.cyr:78-82), so the modules.tcyr 3x3 fixture has exactly 5 entries that are not exactly zero (test asserts 5, "not 9") and the abuse.tcyr all-zero 2x2 has 0 (test asserts 0) — the exact-zero predicate changes NO existing assertion. If a drop tolerance is genuinely wanted it must be RELATIVE and caller-visible: a pre-pass computing scale = max|A_ij| over the whole matrix, then `var tol = f64_mul(EPSILON_F64, scale)` — the idiom this repo already uses at src/linalg_precision.cyr:442 — with the SAME tol value reused by both passes; a per-row scale in one pass and a global scale in the other desynchronises count from emit and overruns alloc(count*8).
defects.scale_test: Fixture M0 (4x4): entries (0,0)=1.0, (0,2)=2^-10, (1,1)=2^-5, (2,0)=2^-10, (3,3)=1.0, remaining 11 cells exact +0.0; k = 5. x = (1,1,1,1). ⚠ M0's entries and x MUST be exact powers of two — the original filing's "entries spanning 1.0 down to 2^-10" does not guarantee that, and a general 53-bit mantissa loses bits once c pushes products subnormal, which breaks assertion (2) for a CORRECT implementation. Sweep c = 2^p for p in {0, +-20, -29, -30, -40, -41, -42, -43, -53, -200, -322, -400, -1000, -1012, -1013, -1022, -1064, -1069, -1074, +400, +1000}. Assert (1) csr_nnz(csr_from_dense(c*M0)) == (the number of entries of c*M0 that are not exactly zero) — COMPUTED FROM THE SCALED MATRIX, not fixed at k. ⚠ This is the original filing's one real error: it asserts nnz == k at every c, and at p = -1074 the 2^-10 and 2^-5 entries genuinely underflow to exact zero, so a measured correct repair returns 2 there and the filing's own test would report the correct repair as FAILING (measured exact-zero column: 5 through p = -1064, 3 at -1069, 2 at -1074). Assert (2) csr_spmv(csr_from_dense(c*M0), x)[i] == c * csr_spmv(csr_from_dense(M0), x)[i] BIT-EXACTLY, restricted to |p| <= 1000 where no product is subnormal — beyond that gradual underflow breaks exact covariance for any implementation. Threshold bracketing, MEASURED on the shipped tree rather than estimated (columns: shipped 1e-12 / DBL_EPSILON / 1e-100 / DBL_MIN / exact-zero): shipped is intact at p = -29 and already loses 2 of 5 at p = -30, total loss (nnz = 0) from p = -40 on; a DBL_EPSILON repair is intact at -41, loses 2 at -42/-43, total at -53; a 1e-100 repair is intact at -200 and total by -400 (analytic crossing p ~ -322, NOT the -290 originally claimed); a DBL_MIN repair is intact at -1012, loses 2 at -1013, keeps 2 at -1022, total at -1064; the exact-zero repair keeps all 5 through -1064 and thereafter loses only what truly underflowed. Every candidate a repair might plausibly choose is therefore separated at a distinct, identifiable c: -30/-40 kills the shipped guard, -41 vs -53 separates DBL_EPSILON, -200 vs -400 separates any arbitrary small constant, -1012 vs -1013/-1022 separates DBL_MIN from exact zero. Control that kills a guard-deleted (keep-everything) mutant: M0's 11 exact-0.0 cells must still be omitted, i.e. nnz must be 5 and never 16, at every c — measured on the modules.tcyr fixture as 5, not 9. Second control, for the coupling: after the repair, run tests/modules.tcyr:7392-7418 and tests/abuse.tcyr:904-923 unchanged (they must stay green), and mutate ONLY :88 to the new predicate while leaving :107 shipped — the emit pass must then be shown to overrun alloc(count*8), proving the two sites are load-bearing together.

At 1e-13 and below: csr_from_dense returns a non-null, valid-looking CSR handle with nnz = 0, nrows = 2, ncols = 2, and NULL col_idx/values pointers (alloc(count*8) with count = 0 hits `if (size <= 0) { return 0; }` in lib/alloc.cyr:224) — the entire matrix destroyed, reported as a successful conversion; csr_spmv on it then returns an all-zero y. Do NOT write it as `|v| >= DBL_MIN`: the filing offered `v != 0.0` and `|v| >= DBL_MIN` as if equivalent and they are not, measured — a DBL_MIN build returns nnz = 0 for the same matrix at scale 1e-320, so it still destroys the whole matrix, just three hundred decades further down. src/error.cyr's F64_TINY comment states the rule this violates: DBL_MIN is the threshold for a guard protecting a DIVISION, and this guard has no denominator. `f64_gt(f64_abs(v), 0)` is also the negative-zero-correct spelling: f64_abs(-0.0) = +0.0 which is not > 0, so -0.0 is dropped, matching IEEE `v != 0.0` and avoiding the -0.0 trap 2.13.0 found. Change BOTH sites in ONE edit, ideally by extracting `_csr_keep(v)` — line 202 is the third instance, so the project's own third-instance rule fires (note 202 in csr_add has NO safety coupling: it writes into an upper-bound allocation of nnz_a + nnz_b and reports `pos`, so csr_add is already structured safely and csr_from_dense is the lone exact-count site). Two structural fixes belong in the same edit, because a shared helper only prevents drift it is actually used by: bound the EMIT loop by `count` so an over-emit cannot write past the allocation at all (this is the mutation-proof half — 2.12.0 proved the tempting other half leaves the silent write intact), and hand csr_new `pos` rather than `count` so nnz and row_ptr[nrows] cannot disagree. defects.scale_test: Two parts, both corrected from the filing — its version does not discriminate as written. PART A, the scale sweep, must NOT be delegated to line 88's test and must reach SUBNORMALS: assert nnz == 4 for the same dense [[1,2],[3,4]] built at scale factors 1e0, 1e-9, 1e-11, 1e-12, 1e-13, 1e-16, 1e-100 and 1e-320 (exact f64 bit patterns; the matrix is one problem in eight unit systems). So a sweep bottoming at 1e-13, which is all the filing's "entries in (0, 1e-12]" fixture reaches, PASSES the DBL_MIN mutant and brackets nothing below it. The 1e-12 row is load-bearing on its own: it is the only one that catches the strict-vs-non-strict boundary (nnz 3, not 0). PART B, the de-synchronisation control, needs its OWN fixture — the filing's cannot express it. Measured: installing the de-sync (line 88 kept at EPSILON_F64, line 107 relaxed, install proven by `sed -n 88p` / `sed -n 107p` before running) and running all five existing suites gives 3611/3611 PASSING, not because the overrun is undetected but because no existing fixture holds a single entry in (0, 1e-12], so the divergent branch is never taken — mutating the existing suite proves nothing here. And the filing's proposed M0 (all entries in (0, 1e-12]) is the wrong fixture: count = 0 makes alloc(0) return NULL and the first store64 faults at address 0 — a loud SIGSEGV any harness catches. The fixture that exhibits the SILENT overrun must have count > 0: a 4x4 with 4 diagonal entries above eps and 12 entries at 1e-13, which runs to completion with no error and reports nnz = 4 while row_ptr[4] = 16 (16 entries into 32-byte buffers). Assert `row_ptr[nrows] == csr_nnz(c)` on THAT matrix — it is the assertion that fails on the de-sync and passes on both the shipped and the repaired build. Prove the mutant is installed with a grep before believing any of these counts, and beware `$?` after a pipe: in this session a `cyrius test` that SIGSEGV'd reported `harness exit: 0` because the exit code came from grep.

defects.guarded_quantity: |s| where s = a_ij + b_ij — the magnitude of the SUM of two stored matrix entries at a coinciding column, computed at line 201 and tested at 202 as `f64_gt(f64_abs(s), EPSILON_F64) == 1` (EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12, src/error.cyr:26). Dimensions: the entries' own units, degree 1 in the problem scale. Unbounded above and below.
defects.protects: Nothing that can fail. There is no division, sqrt, acos or normalisation anywhere in csr_add — s is stored straight into out_v. It is a pure drop-tolerance on a returned value, and the function's own header comment (line 149) states the contract as "Drops zeros", not "drops small entries", so the tolerance is undocumented as well as absolute.
defects.why: All five refutation routes were tried and each is closed by measurement (probes under scratchpad/eps/refute/, run against the shipped tree). (1) NOT dimensionless/bounded: s is a user-supplied matrix entry sum. Measured sweep over c = 2^p on a fixture whose merged row is {overlap sum = c, A-only = c, B-only = c}: 10 of 23 scales lose the overlap entry, first bad at p = -40. nnz is not invariant in c and csr_spmv is not covariant in c. (2) NO caller normalises: `grep -rn csr_add src` returns only the definition — csr_add has ZERO internal callers; it is a public entry point taking any CSR, and csr_new (also public) imposes no invariant on values. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: no iteration, no residual; the value is emitted, not iterated. Contrast the genuine tolerance uses at lines 741 and 858 in the same file. (4) The proposed exact repair changes NO existing test — measured, not assumed: the only value-bearing fixture is modules.tcyr:7392-7413 (A = [[1,0,2],[0,3,0],[4,0,5]], A+A), every entry of whose sum is > 1e-12, so nnz = 5 and the spmv row2 = 18 assertion are identical under `s != 0.0`; abuse.tcyr:908-911 checks only the 0 / non-0 return. (5) The scale_test does discriminate, but had two defects of its own, corrected below. The project's own doctrine already decides this case at src/error.cyr:40-45: EPSILON_F64 "remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity — a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]". A matrix-entry sum is none of those. Two sub-claims of the original filing, adjudicated: the drain-loop inconsistency is REAL and measured (at c = 2^-41 the three output entries have IDENTICAL magnitude 2^-41 and the shipped code emits 2 of them), though reaching it requires csr_new-built input, since csr_from_dense's own guards at lines 88/107 pre-filter operands to |v| > 1e-12; the value destruction, however, is reachable with NO csr_new anywhere — A = [[1.0]] and B = [[-(1 - 2^-41)]] both built by csr_from_dense, both entries far above the drop threshold, true sum exactly 2^-41, and csr_add returns nnz = 0.
defects.fabricates: A CSR that is not A+B, returned as a normal valid handle (csr_add's only failure channel is the designed 0 for dimension mismatch, not raised here). Measured on the public dense-only path: csr_nnz(csr_add(A,B)) = 0 and csr_spmv(...)[0] = +0.0 where the true value is 2^-41 = 4.547473508864641e-13 — a structurally missing entry and a fabricated zero, silent. On the scale sweep, 10 of 23 scales return the wrong nnz and the wrong spmv.
defects.correct_threshold: Exact `s != 0.0` — and explicitly NOT `|s| >= DBL_MIN` / F64_TINY, which the original filing offered as equivalent. They are not: measured, s = 2^-1030 is a genuine nonzero sum for which `f64_gt(f64_abs(s), F64_TINY)` returns 0, so a DBL_MIN guard fabricates a missing entry too, just 300 decades lower down. F64_TINY is the right threshold only where the guard protects a DIVISION and the failing thing is a zero/subnormal denominator (src/error.cyr:39-45 says exactly this); csr_add divides by nothing, so the only scale-free test is exact zero. The exact test is also what the function's own comment already promises ("Drops zeros") and is self-consistent with the two unfiltered drain loops at lines 213-226. If a noise-drop is genuinely wanted it must be relative to the operands actually summed — `EPSILON_F64 * (|a_ij| + |b_ij|)` — and must then be applied to the drain loops too and to csr_from_dense:88/107, or the inconsistency merely moves.

This is the first correction: csr_from_dense (lines 88, 107) carries the IDENTICAL absolute `|v| > EPSILON_F64` drop, and measured, a 1x3 dense fixture at scale 2^-40 comes back with nnz = 0, so a from_dense-built sweep fails identically no matter what line 202 does and blames the wrong guard. Fixture (1x3 suffices; 4x4 adds nothing): A = {col0: 3c, col1: 1c}, B = {col0: -2c, col2: 1c}, so the merged row is {col0: c (overlap sum), col1: c (A-drain), col2: c (B-drain)} — all three output magnitudes identical by construction, and 3c - 2c = c is bit-exact for every c = 2^p, verified down to p = -1070. Assert for every p: (1) csr_nnz(csr_add(cA,cB)) == 3, (2) csr_spmv(...)[0] == 3c bit-exactly. Exponents p in {0, ±20, ±40, ±41, ±53, ±60, ±100, ±200, ±400, ±600, ±800, ±1000, −1030, −1040, −1060, −1070}.
