Second, SCALE-INDEPENDENT assertion at c = 2^-41 alone: the three output entries have identical magnitude, so nnz must be 3 or 0, never 2 — shipped returns 2, which discriminates a drop-tolerance from an exact test without any scaling argument at all. Third, a reachability assertion that uses no csr_new: A = [[1.0]] and B = [[-(1 - 2^-41)]] via csr_from_dense (both stored, both >> 1e-12), true sum exactly 2^-41; assert csr_nnz == 1 and csr_spmv[0] == 2^-41 — shipped returns 0 and +0.0.

defects.guarded_quantity: wj_norm = _lext_norm(wj, n) — the Euclidean LENGTH (already un-squared; _lext_norm takes the sqrt at src/linalg_ext.cyr:312) of the Arnoldi vector wj = A*v_j - sum_i h_ij*v_i after modified Gram-Schmidt. Every v_i is unit-length, so wj carries the units of A's ENTRIES: degree 1 in ||A||, i.e. ||A|| times a dimensionless quantity, bounded above only by ||A||_2. REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED: it is not dimensionless, not bounded by 1, and no caller normalises — solve_gmres is a public entry point shipped in dist/hisab.cyr (grep: only tests/*.tcyr call it in-tree), and A reaches it only as the opaque callback A_fn, so hisab never sees, let alone rescales, the operator.
defects.protects: The division f64_div(f64_from(1), wj_norm) at line 472 that normalises the next Krylov basis vector. It is NOT a convergence tolerance — tol is a separate parameter, tested at lines 411, 518 and 557; this branch body does nothing but the reciprocal and the scaling loop.
defects.why: CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not by argument (probe: scratchpad/eps/refute/tree/tests/{scale,probe}.tcyr, cycc 6.6.2; the repo tree was copied to scratch and left byte-identical, md5 572273090611bc28f557dabcf03d9eb2). GMRES is exactly covariant under (A,b,tol) -> (cA,cb,c*tol): the Krylov basis and the returned x are UNCHANGED and H scales by c, so with c a power of two every intermediate scales by an exact factor and x must come back BIT-IDENTICAL. The only scale-breaking comparisons in the whole function are the three absolute guards at 471, 499 and 536. Measured on a well-conditioned 8x8 SPD tridiagonal(-1,4,-1), b=1, x0=0, tol0=1e-12, m=8, budget=64: x is bit-identical for c=2^p over p in [-38,+509] and BREAKS AT p=-39 (c~1.8e-12), exactly where wj_norm crosses 1e-12. It returns 0.428571428571 (=3/7) at p=-39..-41 and 2^p (~2.8e-14 at p=-45) from p<=-45, against the true 0.366013071895 — and it reports CONVERGENCE while doing so, because the fabricated Givens rotation (cs=1, sn=0 from the sibling guard at 499) makes g[k] exactly 0, which returns x at line 558. ⛔ AND THE DEFECT IS NOT ONLY ABOUT UNITS: it is reachable at c = 1 with no rescaling at all. A = diag(2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19), b = e1 + 1e-14*e2, tol = 1e-18 gives wj_norm ~ 1e-14 at j=0; the shipped gate fires, v_1 is stored unnormalised, and x comes back with x1 = 1e-14 instead of 1e-14/3 and relative residual 5e-15 against the 1e-18 the caller asked for. tests/hisab.tcyr:2544 already passes tol = 1e-18 to this function, so that regime is not hypothetical. The branch body is wrong independently of the threshold whenever the guard fires on a NONZERO wj_norm: line 479 stores wj into v_basis[j+1] unconditionally, so the 'orthonormal' basis contains a vector of length ~1e-14 and every later h_ij = <w,v_i> and the back-substitution are computed against it.
defects.fabricates: An x built on a non-orthonormal Krylov basis, returned through the normal success path with the solver reporting convergence. Measured, c = 2^-45: x = (2.8e-14, ...) where the answer is (0.366013071895, ...) — thirteen orders of magnitude wrong; c = 2^-40: 3/7 instead of 0.366013071895; c = 1 near-breakdown: relative residual 5e-15 for a requested 1e-18. solve_gmres's only failure channel is the designed 0 from the two allocation guards (n > ALLOC_MAX/8, m+1 > (ALLOC_MAX/8)/m), so the caller gets a wrong solution with no error signal at all. ⚠ CORRECTION to docs/audit/2026-08-11-v2.11.0-full.md, which records this function's fabrication as 'the initial guess': the initial guess here was 0 and the returned vector is not it — what comes back is an arbitrary wrong vector, which is strictly harder to notice than an unchanged x0.
defects.correct_threshold: `f64_gt(wj_norm, F64_TINY)` — DBL_MIN, src/error.cyr:45, the smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is still finite; guard exactly what makes the DIVISION fail and nothing more. It is earned, not merely conservative: at c = 2^-534/2^-535 a deleted-guard mutant returns NaN (1/subnormal -> inf -> 0*inf) where the DBL_MIN gate returns finite, so the guard has a real job at a real input. ⭐ THE REPAIR MUST COVER ALL THREE SIBLING GUARDS, measured: repairing 471 alone only moves the scale-sweep kill from p=-39 to p=-42, because line 499 (r_val, the Givens radius) and line 536 (|hii|, the back-substitution pivot) are the same quantity class and fabricate an identity rotation and a skipped divide. With all three on F64_TINY the sweep is bit-identical across p in [-509,+509]. ⚠ AND THE 'RELATIVE DEFLATION TEST BESIDE IT' IS NOT A DROP-IN: measured, a relative gate `wj_norm > EPSILON_F64 * r_norm` with the SHIPPED branch body fails the c=1 near-breakdown control identically to the shipped absolute gate (same wrong x1 = 1e-14, same 5e-15 residual). A deflation test is only a repair if firing BREAKS the inner loop at k = j+1; as a threshold swap it reproduces the defect. ⚠ Existing tests do not constrain the choice — measured, not assumed: with F64_TINY installed at all three sites (installation proven by grep) all five suites pass with counts identical to the pristine tree (hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776, 0 failed both ways). The suite is blind to this. ⚠ ADJACENT, OUT OF THIS GUARD'S SCOPE BUT FOUND BY THE SAME PROBE: `inv_r = f64_div(f64_from(1), r_norm)` at line 416 has NO guard at all; with tol <= 0 and an exact happy breakdown, `f64_lt(r_norm, tol)` is false at r_norm = 0 and every gate choice returns NaN through that site.
defects.scale_test: PRIMARY (scale sweep, measured to bracket): fix the 8x8 SPD tridiagonal(-1,4,-1) with b0 = 1, x0 = 0, restart m = 8, max_iter = 64, tol0 = 1e-12. For c = 2^p assert solve_gmres(c*A0*, c*b0, x0, 8, c*tol0, 64, 8) is BIT-IDENTICAL to the c=1 run (x is invariant, not covariant, so no rescaling of the compared value and the compare is exact). Measured first-failing p, all three guards set to the same rule: shipped 1e-12 -> p = -39; DBL_EPSILON -> -51; 1e-100 -> -331; F64_TINY/DBL_MIN, a relative rule, and no guard at all -> survive to -509. USABLE WINDOW p in [-509, +509]: outside it _lext_norm's sum of SQUARES overflows (upward, entries 4c, (4c)^2 >= 2^1024 at p = +510) or goes subnormal (downward, p = -510), so the test would measure the HELPER. p in [-500, +500] is safely inside and brackets every plausible repair. ⛔ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL TEST DESIGN, both measured. (1) THE SWEEP DOES NOT ISOLATE LINE 471 — it is a whole-function property; a 471-only repair still fails at p = -42, so a repairer must patch 471, 499 and 536 together or will read a real fix as a failure. (2) THE PROPOSED EXACT-BREAKDOWN CONTROL DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE AND MUST BE REPLACED. defects.guarded_quantity: r_val = sqrt(hjj^2 + hj1j^2) — the Givens rotation RADIUS, the 2-norm of a two-element column segment of the Hessenberg after the previous j rotations have been applied. The sqrt IS taken, so this is a length, not a squared quantity; the class is scaling, not squared-vs-unsquared. Degree 1 in ||A||: the v_i are unit vectors by construction, so H entries are v_i^T·A·v_j and carry the units of A's entries. Measured on A0 = tridiag(1,4,1) scaled by c: r_val at j=0 is exactly (16/3)·c, and the guard's firing point tracks c to the decade (see scale_test bracket).
defects.protects: The two divisions `f64_div(hjj, r_val)` and `f64_div(hj1j, r_val)` on lines 500-501 forming the rotation cosine and sine. Note r_val >= max(|hjj|, |hj1j|) by construction, so BOTH quotients are bounded by 1 in magnitude and neither can overflow or lose precision at any scale — the one and only failure mode is 0/0 when both operands are exactly zero. That confirms this is a pure divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance (the happy-breakdown test on the subdiagonal is a separate guard, line 471), and it is why the correct magnitude is DBL_MIN and not any tolerance.
defects.why:
CONFIRMED as a scaling defect, but the filing's reasoning is wrong in three places and its probe would not have shown any of this. All numbers below are measured on pristine `git show HEAD` sources, cycc 6.6.2, mutants grep-verified installed before each run.

(1) The defect is real and I isolated it. Line 499 cannot be exercised alone: line 507 OVERWRITES H[j][j] with r_val, so the `hii` tested at line 536 (back-substitution) IS r_val, compared against the SAME EPSILON_F64 — the two guards fire in lockstep on the same quantity, and line 471 (wj_norm, also EPSILON_F64) fires earlier still. Repairing 471+536 and leaving 499 shipped isolates it cleanly: bit-exact correct down to p = -42, then FLAT WRONG from p = -43 to p = -500 — 2 matvecs of a 30 budget (i.e. convergence declared after one Arnoldi step) and a true relative residual of 8.813e-2. Repairing all three restores bit-exact covariance across the entire p ∈ [-500, +500] window.

(2) REFUTED — "the branch body is correct at r_val == 0 ... so ONLY the threshold is wrong." Measured false. Singular fixture A0 = [[0,0],[0,1]], b0 = e_0 makes r_val EXACTLY 0 at j=0 at every scale. Shipped, DBL-MIN-at-499, 471+536-repaired and all-three-repaired are IDENTICAL on it: 2 matvecs of a 50 budget, x = [1,0], true residual 1.0 — the MAXIMUM achievable, since A is singular and b is outside range(A) — reported as converged. The else-branch writes g[j+1] = -0·g[j] = 0, so the line-518 residual test reads exactly 0 whenever g[j] != 0. The threshold is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT; the fallback fabricates convergence at r_val == 0 too.

(3) REFUTED — "DBL_MIN and relative-to-||A||_F survive the window." Not as scoped. DBL_MIN at line 499 ALONE never produces the right answer at any p <= -42: it only changes the failure mode (30 matvecs = budget exhausted at -42..-100, then back to 3 matvecs with a 100% residual at p <= -300, where line 471's unnormalised basis vector cascades into an exact-zero r_val and the fabricating else-branch of (2) takes over).

(4) REFUTED — the proposed control does not kill a guard-deleted mutant (see scale_test).

(5) CONFIRMED, and the filing understates it: NO existing test constrains this guard. On HEAD's 3574 assertions (776/233/351/416/1798), the DBL_MIN repair is green AND deleting the guard outright is green. Nothing in five suites reaches it.
defects.fabricates: A converged-looking x, with no error channel — solve_gmres returns only the solution array and has no rc. The identity rotation sets g[j+1] = -sn·g[j] = 0, so the residual estimate |g[k]| that line 518 tests is exactly 0 and the routine returns the current iterate as an exact solution. Measured with line 499 isolated (471/536 repaired), A0 = tridiag(1,4,1), b0 = (1,1,1), c = 2^-43: returns after 2 matvecs of a 30 budget with a true relative residual of 8.813e-2, flat at that value all the way to c = 2^-500. In the fully shipped configuration the co-firing line-536 guard skips the back-substitution division too and the true relative residual is 1.000 — a 100%-wrong answer reported as exact.
defects.scale_test:
The filed test does not discriminate — it fails identically for every candidate threshold — and its control kills nothing. Four measured corrections:

(1) tol MUST be scaled: tol = c·tol0. With tol fixed, line 413's `f64_lt(r_norm, tol)` short-circuits and solve_gmres returns the UNTOUCHED initial guess. Measured: x bits = 0x0 at every p <= -42 under shipped, DBL-MIN-at-499, and all-three-repaired alike. The assertion fails everywhere for every threshold and brackets nothing.

(2) The sweep MUST be run with lines 471 and 536 already repaired, or line 499 is invisible behind them: shipped, m499, and 471+499 all fail identically at p <= -43. This is the only configuration in which the guard is observable.

(3) Bracket, measured in that isolated configuration on A0 = tridiag(1,4,1), b0 = (1,1,1), x0 = 0, restart 3, budget 30, c = 2^p, asserting x bit-identical to the c = 1 run (r_val at j=0 = (16/3)·c, so the firing point is T·3/16):
    1e-12 (shipped): last good p = -42, first bad p = -43
    DBL_EPSILON:     last good p = -54, first bad p = -55
    1e-100:          last good p = -334, first bad p = -335
    DBL_MIN:         survives to p = -500 (and +500)
  A step-50 grid over [-500, +500] does bracket all three losers (-50, -100, -350 respectively); the filing's extra p = ±40, ±41, ±53 points are mis-chosen — none of them is the edge. Keep the window at ±500: the `_lext_norm` sum-of-squares underflows below p ≈ -513 (measured: all-three-repaired is bit-exact at -500 and breaks at -510) and overflows above p ≈ +511.

(4) Add the second observable the filing is right to want, but make it the MATVEC COUNT via a counting callback, not the true residual: the fabrication announces itself as an early return (3 matvecs when correct, 2 when it falsely converges), and that count is what separates line 499 from line 536 — 536 corrupts x without changing the iteration count.

(5) CONTROL — the filed one is refuted. A0 = I, b0 = e_0 does NOT kill a guard-deleted mutant: measured bit-identical 0x3ff0000000000000 with and without the guard, no NaN, because GMRES converges and RETURNS at j = 0 (r_val = 1, 2 matvecs); step j = 1, where the filing expects hjj = hj1j = 0, is never reached. Use instead the singular fixture A0 = [[0,0],[0,1]], b0 = e_0, n = 2, budget 50: r_val is exactly 0 at j = 0 at every scale, and with the guard deleted x0 comes back 0xfff8000000000000 (NaN) after burning all 50 matvecs, versus 0x3ff0000000000000 with it. Assert on that fixture BOTH that x is not NaN and that the routine does not report convergence (matvecs must reach the budget) — the second half is what fails on the threshold-only repair and is the assertion that would have caught defect (2) in `why`.

defects.guarded_quantity: |H[i][i]| — but specifically it is the value stored at line 509, i.e. r_val = sqrt(hjj^2 + hj1j^2) computed at line 498, the Givens-rotated R diagonal. Units of A's entries: H[i][j] = <A·v_i, v_j> on UNIT Arnoldi basis vectors, so degree 1 in ||A|| and degree 0 in b. A plain magnitude, not squared. f64_abs is redundant on it (sqrt is non-negative).
defects.protects: The division `yi = f64_div(yi, hii)` on line 537 in the upper-triangular back-substitution H·y = g. f64_div is a raw IEEE intrinsic, not a safe-div (lib/ganita.cyr:660 uses f64_div(0,0) deliberately to manufacture a NaN), so an unguarded hii == 0 yields inf/nan.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FAILED, TWO CAME BACK SUPPORTING. (a) Not dimensionless: nothing normalises A — A_fn is an arbitrary caller callback, and normalising r into v0 rescales g, not H, so hii is degree 1 in ||A||. (b) No caller normalisation exists; b is not normalised either. (c) Not a convergence tolerance: tol is a separate caller parameter (lines 411, 517, 556); line 536 runs after the Arnoldi loop has ended and guards a division only. (d) No existing test blocks the repair — 11 solve_gmres assertions (abuse.tcyr:951-996, hisab.tcyr:2548-2559) use fixtures 2I (_ab_matvec) and tridiag(1,4,1) (_gmb_A) at unit scale, giving hii = 2 and 4.24, so the guard is never reached; and every one of those assertions is on the returned POINTER or the matvec count, never on x's values, so y_i = 0 cannot flip any of them. (e) The scale_test partially fails to discriminate — see scale_test; that sharpens the test, it does not save the guard. ⛔ WHAT THE REFUTATION PASS ADDED: hii is not merely "an R diagonal", it is EXACTLY the r_val tested three lines earlier at 499 against the IDENTICAL EPSILON_F64, and r_val >= |H[j+1][j]| = wj_norm tested at 471 against the same constant. So line 536 can NEVER fire without 499 and 471 having already fired at that same step j, and since the 499 else-branch sets sn = 0, g[k] = -0 and the solver then takes the `f64_lt(f64_abs(g[k]), tol)` exit at 556 — the fabricated answer is returned through the success path AND labelled converged. One defect, three sites. ⛔ And it is reachable at c = 1 with no scaling at all: A = 0 with b = [1,2,3] gives hii == 0 exactly, and the shipped code returns x = b = [1,2,3] reporting convergence for a system with no solution; the nilpotent shift [[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[0,0,0]] with b = [1,0,0] returns [1,0,0] (residual 1.0) and reports converged while a zero-residual solution [t,1,0] exists. [measured: python replica of lines 400-556, scratchpad sim3/sim4, 2026-09-09]
defects.fabricates: y_i left undivided — the numerator returned as if the pivot were 1.0 — so x is short of the true step by exactly the factor |hii| (a ratio of 1/|hii| >= 1e12 at the threshold). Measured on A = tridiag(1,4,1)·2^p, b = [1,2,3]·2^p, x0 = 0: x(1) = [0.2222, 0.1111, 1.4444], x(2^-45) = [2.84e-14, 5.68e-14, 8.53e-14]. defects.guarded_quantity: |A[i][i]| — a diagonal entry of the caller-supplied system matrix, read via ganita_mat_get(A, i, i). defects.why: Verdict survives every refutation avenue I could construct. (1) NOT dimensionless: aii is a raw entry of a caller-owned matrix; the header comment (lines 704-712) states only "A: stdlib matrix (n x n)" — no normalization contract, no unit convention, no bound. (2) NO caller normalises: grep over src/, tests/, examples/ finds ZERO in-repo callers of solve_pgs — it is a public library entry point reached only by tests/hisab.tcyr:1576/1605 and tests/abuse.tcyr:940-948. collision_core's contact path uses sequential_impulse, not this. Nothing can normalise A before the call. (3) NOT a convergence tolerance: line 741 IS the convergence tolerance and uses the SAME constant — that is the confusion, not a defence. Line 720 sits immediately in front of a division and has no other consumer. (4) Covariance verified numerically, not argued: PGS is invariant (not covariant) in x under (A,b) -> (cA,cb) with lo/hi fixed, and for c a power of two the invariance is BIT-EXACT — a 4x4 fixture reproduces the identical x for p in [-1019, +1021] with the guard removed entirely. So aii scales by c exactly while 1e-12 does not, and the same contact problem in kg vs tonnes crosses the threshold at a different point. Measured on a 4x4 with diag (4,3,2,1): at c = 2^-40 row 3 alone is skipped and x[3] stays frozen at the initial 0.0 where the answer is 0.29166666666666663 — the rest of the vector solved around it; at c = 2^-45 every row is skipped, max_change is never written (the skip path at 721-723 does not touch it), the line-741 early-out fires on the FIRST sweep, and the function returns rc = 0 with x still the caller's x0. Documented as "Returns: 0 on success", and solve_pgs has no error channel at all (both returns are literal 0).
defects.fabricates: Uniformly small-scale system: the caller's own initial guess x0, unmodified, returned as rc = 0 (measured: c = 2^-45 returns [0,0,0,0] for a well-conditioned SPD system whose answer is [0.25, 0.5833…, 0.29166…, 0.29166…]). Single small diagonal: that one component frozen at its initial value while every other row is solved around it — a plausible-looking partial answer (measured at c = 2^-40). Additionally, if the guard is loosened without an error channel, a subnormal aii against an O(1) sigma divides to ±inf, and f64_clamp (lib/math.cyr:431-435 — `if x<lo return lo; if x>hi return hi`) converts that into hi or lo, i.e. a fabricated BOUND value rather than an inf the caller could detect.
defects.correct_threshold: For the division proper the exactly-right condition is `aii != 0.0` — that is the only input on which f64_div fails to produce the best available answer; a subnormal aii yields a correctly-rounded quotient (or an honest ±inf on genuine overflow). `|aii| >= DBL_MIN` is one notch conservative and acceptable, but it is NOT behaviourally identical and must be chosen deliberately: it is discriminated from `aii != 0` at aii in the subnormal range (see the n=1 companion in scale_test, where DBL_MIN dies at p <= -1023 and `aii != 0` survives to 2^-1074). If a small-pivot POLICY is wanted at all it must be relative to the row: `|aii| > EPSILON_F64 * sum_j |A[i][j]|` — dimensionless by construction, invariant under (A,b) -> (cA,cb). ⚠ CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED — the threshold change alone breaks NO existing test: tests/hisab.tcyr's two PGS fixtures have diagonals (4,3) and (1,1); tests/abuse.tcyr:948 passes an all-zero matrix whose aii = 0 fails `>= DBL_MIN` and `!= 0` alike, so the skip and the rc = 0 both survive. ⛔ But the ERROR-CHANNEL half of this repair DOES break a currently-passing assertion: tests/abuse.tcyr:948-949 asserts `solve_pgs(ganita_mat_new(3,3), …) == 0` with the message "all-zero diagonal skipped, not divided by" — that assertion PINS the silent-skip-returns-success contract this finding calls a defect. Returning a nonzero code for a structurally singular row requires updating that assertion in the same change; it is not collateral damage, it is the test having pinned the fabrication.
defects.scale_test: A0 = 4x4 SPD, diag (4,3,2,1), off-diagonals O(1) powers of two (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125); b0 = (1,2,1,0.5); x0 = 0; lo/hi = ±1e6. SET max_iter = 1 so the line-741 early-out cannot influence the result — with max_iter = 1 the loop exits after one sweep either way, isolating this guard from the tolerance at 741. Assert x after the single sweep is BIT-EXACTLY x(A0,b0) for c = 2^p. ⛔ TWO CORRECTIONS to the proposed sweep, both measured: (1) the claimed "full double range is usable" is FALSE, and the limit is not sums of squares — it is SUBNORMAL PRODUCTS A_ij·x_j. With the guard deleted entirely (pure arithmetic control), exact covariance holds at p = -1019 and BREAKS at p = -1020, while holding to at least p = +1021. Since DBL_MIN fires only near p <= -1024 for an O(1) diagonal, the proposed p = -1022 / -1074 points lie inside the broken window: the recommended repair "fails" there for reasons that are not the guard, and the sweep as written cannot bracket DBL_MIN at all. (This also disproves the test's own premise that bounds "wide enough" never bind: ±inf binds against ANY finite bound.) Use instead: with A0[2][2] = 0.0 at c = 1, assert x[2] is bit-exactly its initial 0.0 AND x[3] == 0.3645833333333333 — the mutant misses both by six orders of magnitude, because the fabricated hi propagates into the next row.

defects.guarded_quantity: max_change = max_i |x_i^new − x_i^old| over one sweep — the sup-norm change in the SOLUTION vector. defects.protects: Nothing. It is the convergence early-out for the sweep loop ("Early out if converged (use EPSILON_F64 as tolerance)", line 740). No division, sqrt or domain is protected — the divide at line 732 is guarded separately at line 720.
defects.why: VERDICT HELD, BUT THE FILING'S OWN TEST WAS REFUTED. All five refutation paths were run against a built probe (replica of lines 713–746, instrumented to return the sweep count; A0=[[4,1],[1,3]], b0=[1,2], x0=0, lo/hi=±2^1000). (1) Dimensionless/bounded — REFUTED: dimensioned in x; with b scaled by 2^-40 the shipped guard returns after ONE sweep at 175.0% relative error on x0 with rc = 0, where the unit-scale run takes 13 sweeps. (2) Caller normalises — REFUTED: `grep` finds NO in-tree caller; solve_pgs is a public entry point and A, b, lo, hi are all caller-supplied, with lo/hi (±1e6 in the test) carrying the solution scale independently of A. (3) "It is a tolerance, not a divide-guard" — TRUE as stated and it is why this is milder than the ten division guards, but it does not make an ABSOLUTE tolerance correct: a stopping criterion that accepts an iterate with zero correct digits is not a tolerance, it is a tolerance in the wrong units. (4) Proposed repair breaks a passing test — REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, checked not assumed: the relative form returns BIT-IDENTICAL x and the same sweep count on both hisab.tcyr fixtures (line 1566 unbounded, 13 sweeps, x0 = 0x3fb745d1745d1c4c; line 1590 clamped, 2 sweeps, x = [2,2]) and leaves the abuse.tcyr rc = 0 paths unchanged (zero-solution and n = 0 both still terminate on sweep 1 with a DBL_MIN floor). defects.fabricates: An under-converged iterate returned with rc = 0 ("Returns: 0 on success"). MEASURED: A0=[[4,1],[1,3]] with b = 2^-40·[1,2] returns after ONE sweep with x0 175.0% relative error against the exact 1/11 scaling — no correct digits — while the identical system at unit b takes 13 sweeps and lands 2e-13 from exact. The severity stays below the division guards only because the max_iter path returns 0 as well, so the caller could never distinguish converged from not-converged in any case.
defects.correct_threshold: Not DBL_MIN — nothing fails here. Relative, or caller-supplied as solve_gmres already takes a `tol`. Measured working form: `max_change < max(EPSILON_F64 * max_i |x_i|, DBL_MIN)`. The floor is load-bearing and must be a value an exactly-zero max_change still passes: with the DBL_MIN floor the all-zero-solution and n = 0 fixtures still fire on sweep 1 (0 < DBL_MIN), so abuse.tcyr:942–949's rc = 0 assertions are untouched; a floor of 0, or a `<=`-free formulation, would instead burn all max_iter sweeps on every frozen system. In-tree precedent: src/linalg_precision.cyr:442 `var tol = f64_mul(EPSILON_F64, scale)`. ⚠ Known limit of the relative form, measured: eps·max|x| denormalizes once max|x| < ~2.2e-296, so bit-exact scale invariance holds only for |p| <= ~800 in b = 2^p·b0 — at p = -1000 the correct repair itself takes 8 sweeps and is not bit-exact. State that band in the repair's comment rather than claiming unconditional invariance.
defects.scale_test: ⛔ THE ORIGINAL scale_test IS REFUTED — IT PASSES ON THE SHIPPED DEFECT. Scaling A AND b by c leaves x = A⁻¹b invariant, hence max_change bit-invariant, hence line 741 UNREACHABLE by that perturbation: measured on the shipped tree, sweeps = 13 and x bit-identical to the c = 1 run at every p in {0, ±20, ±40, -41, +53, +100}. The only failures it produces (p <= -42: 1 sweep, x = 0x0, the untouched initial guess) are LINE 720 firing on |c·4| < 1e-12 — the guard it explicitly claims to have isolated away, so its one failure signal is misattributed. Its premise is unsatisfiable besides: c·A0's diagonal IS c·4, so "A0's diagonal held at unit magnitude" cannot hold while A is scaled. Its bracketing predictions (-40 / -53 / -332 knees) are predictions about b-only scaling, which is not what it scales. And its success criterion is wrong: a correct relative repair does NOT hold across ±1000 (see correct_threshold), so it would REJECT a correct repair. REPLACEMENT (measured, discriminating): hold A = A0 = [[4,1],[1,3]] FIXED (diagonal 4 and 3 — 720 provably silent, which is what actually isolates 741), scale b ONLY: b = 2^p·[1,2], x0 = 0, lo/hi = ±2^1000, max_iter = 2000. x then scales exactly by 2^p. Assert (a) x(2^p)/2^p bit-equal to x(1), (b) the sweep count invariant in p, and (c) the relative error of x0 against 1/11 stays at 0. Measured sweep counts [p: shipped-1e-12 | DBL_EPSILON-abs | 1e-100-abs | relative] — 1000: 17|17|17|13, 300: 17|17|17|13, 100: 17|17|17|13, 20: 17|17|17|13, 0: 13|16|17|13, -20: 7|11|17|13, -39: 2|5|17|13, -40: 1|5|17|13, -51: 1|2|17|13, -52: 1|1|17|13, -100: 1|1|17|13, -200: 1|1|17|13, -331: 1|1|2|13, -332: 1|1|1|13, -400: 1|1|1|13, -800: 1|1|1|13. Every absolute candidate has its own collapse-to-one-sweep knee (1e-12 at p = -40, DBL_EPSILON at p = -52, 1e-100 at p = -332) AND over-iterates at large scale (17 vs 13), while only the relative form is flat — so p in {0, ±20, ±40, ±52, ±100, ±332, ±400, ±800} brackets all three candidates in both directions. CAP AT |p| <= 800. The headline assertion is the value, not the count: at p = -40 the shipped code returns 175.0% relative error on x0 with rc = 0.

defects.site: src/linalg_ext.cyr:886 (the division it protects is at :893, not :892; the sibling absolute epsilon is set at :858 and applied at :900 — NOT :872, which is `i = i + 1;`)
defects.guarded_quantity: |max_val| — largest-magnitude component of w = A·v, where v is the previous iterate renormalised by its own max component (v = e_0 initially). Degree 1 in ||A||, degree 0 in the scale of v: a plain matrix-entry-scale magnitude, not squared, not bounded, not dimensionless. ⚠ The finding's premise "v's largest component is exactly 1" is NOT true by construction — line 896 multiplies by the reciprocal, and x*(1/x) != 1 for 27,022 of 200,000 random x (13.5%). It happens to be exactly 1 for the suite's inputs (hisab.tcyr:1510 asserts that bit-exactly and passes). Covariance is unaffected: under A -> cA with c = 2^p every mantissa is bit-identical and only the exponent moves, so max_val(cA) == c·max_val(A) EXACTLY — which is what makes a power-of-two sweep a clean bisection.
defects.protects: The reciprocal `inv_max = f64_div(f64_from(1), max_val)` at :893 and the renormalising multiply `w[i] * inv_max` at :896. It is a divide/overflow guard, not the convergence test — the convergence test is a separate comparison at :900 against `tol` (:858), and both were given the same EPSILON_F64.
defects.why: NOT REFUTED — the class holds, and every refutation angle was tried and failed. The quantity is degree 1 in ||A||: the caller does not normalise (eigen_power is a public entry point, exported at dist/hisab.cyr:17124; the 17 test call sites all pass raw matrices), the guard is not the convergence tolerance (that is :900, on a different quantity), and the reciprocal at :893 fails only at max_val = 0 or below ~1/DBL_MAX. Measured on [[2,1],[1,2]] scaled by c = 2^p, the shipped 1e-12 returns NO_CONVERGENCE from p = -41 down for a matrix with a cleanly separated dominant eigenvalue. BUT the finding is materially wrong in four measured particulars, and acting on it as written would make the function WORSE. (1) Its value assertion fails on SHIPPED code with no repair at all: at c = 1 the returned lambda is 2.9999999999997375, relative error 8.749e-14 — outside the proposed 1e-14 — and on the matrix the suite actually uses the error is 2.5e-13, which tests/hisab.tcyr:1504 already records in its own comment ("measured error is 2.5e-13"). eigen_power's accuracy is set by its stopping rule, not by this guard, so a 1e-14 assertion fails for every candidate threshold at every scale and brackets nothing. (2) The top-end caveat is false: measured p = +16 … +1000 all return rc = 0 with relative error EXACTLY 0.0 in 35 iterations, for every candidate threshold including shipped — because an absolute tolerance on a huge magnitude cannot fire until the f64 iteration reaches an exact fixed point, which yields the correctly-rounded eigenvalue. Nothing fails at the top for :900's reason or any other. (3) "Hold the tolerance constant" is precisely the condition under which the proposed DBL_MIN repair FABRICATES: with :900 left absolute, DBL_MIN at :886 returns rc = 0 and out_val = 2c (the first column's max) where the truth is 3c — a 33% error, silently — at p = -41, -60, -100, -400, -1000 and -1022, i.e. over 980+ binades. Repairing this guard alone is strictly worse than shipping it. (4) The silent-wrong band already exists ABOVE the guard: on shipped code p = -20 returns 2.9999995818c (rel 1.4e-7), p = -30 returns 1.0e-4 off, and p = -39/-40 return 2.5c — rel error 1.67e-1, the WRONG eigenvalue, with rc = 0. So :900's `|dlambda| < EPSILON_F64` is the same defect class on the same covariant quantity and is the LARGER of the two, because it fabricates where :886 merely errors. :886 is real but is the second defect in this function, and the two must be repaired together or not at all. Also corrected: the finding's parenthetical that "even DBL_MIN is slightly permissive for a RECIPROCAL" is backwards — 1/DBL_MIN = 4.4942e307 is finite by construction, so no is_inf check is needed; measured, DBL_MIN is slightly CONSERVATIVE, rejecting p = -1024 (max_val = 2^-1023, subnormal, 1/it = 2^1023 finite) where a nonzero-only guard returns the exactly right answer.
defects.fabricates: As shipped: none — it reports HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE and writes neither out_val nor out_vec. The error is nonetheless FALSE (the matrix is well-conditioned and 1/1e-13 = 1e13 is an ordinary double), and it is unit-dependent rather than iteration-dependent, so a caller reading NO_CONVERGENCE as "no dominant eigenvalue" is misled. ⚠ But this field is only true because the second absolute epsilon at :900 is standing behind it: repair :886 to DBL_MIN alone and the function starts fabricating out_val = 2c (33% wrong, rc = 0) at every p <= -41 — measured. And on shipped code the fabrication already occurs just ABOVE the guard, at p = -39/-40 (returns 2.5c for a true 3c, rc = 0, out_vec written).
defects.correct_threshold: PAIRED — either both or neither. (a) :886 guard: replace the multiply-by-reciprocal at :893/:896 with a direct divide `store64(v + i*8, f64_div(load64(w + i*8), max_val))`, after which the only correct guard is `max_val != 0`. Measured: this is exact at every scale from p = +1000 down to p = -1030, removes the reciprocal-overflow mode entirely, and makes v's max component exactly 1.0 by construction — which tests/hisab.tcyr:1510 asserts bit-exactly today and currently gets only by luck (x*(1/x) != 1 for 13.5% of x). If the reciprocal is kept for speed, `f64_abs(max_val) >= DBL_MIN` is correct and needs NO is_inf check (1/DBL_MIN = 4.4942e307 is finite); it is conservative by ~2.4 binades, not permissive. A genuinely zero max_val does mean A·v = 0 and NO_CONVERGENCE is the right report. (b) :858/:900 stopping test, which must move in the same commit: `|new - old| < EPSILON_F64` is the same defect on the same degree-1 quantity and is the one that FABRICATES. Make it relative: `f64_abs(f64_sub(new_eigenvalue, eigenvalue)) < f64_mul(tol, f64_abs(new_eigenvalue))`. Verified against the existing suite: all eigen_power value assertions go through `f64_approx_eq(..., EP_TOL = 1e-11)` / `_AB_TOL`, and the relative rule moves [[2,1],[1,3]] from 3.6180339887501418 to 3.618033988751586 and the 3x3 from 5.9999999999993179 to 5.999999999994543 — both still inside 1e-11, so no existing assertion in tests/*.tcyr breaks. The one bit-exact assertion (:1510, v[1] == 1.0) is made safer, not riskier, by the direct divide.
defects.scale_test: A0 = [[2,1],[1,2]] (lambda_1 = 3, lambda_2 = 1, ratio 1/3), n = 2, max_iter = 500, c = 2^p so the scaling is EXACT (mantissas bit-identical, exponent only). p in {+1000, +400, +100, +20, 0, -20, -30, -39, -41, -54, -100, -334, -400, -1000, -1022, -1024, -1030} — note -1024 and -1030 are ADDED; the finding's list stops at -1022 and therefore cannot separate DBL_MIN from a nonzero-only guard at all (measured: DBL_MIN and nonzero-only agree at -1000, -1010 and -1022, and first differ at -1024). Assertion (ii) is the half the finding omitted the force of and is what makes the sweep discriminate, because rc alone REWARDS the fabricating repair. Never compare through f64_to. Measured brackets, first p at which rc != 0 (relative stopping rule in place): shipped 1e-12 -> -41; DBL_EPSILON -> -54; 1e-100 -> -334; DBL_MIN -> -1024; nonzero-only/direct-divide -> never in range (entries underflow to 0 at p <= -1075); relative (EPSILON_F64 * ||A||_inf) -> never. Every neighbouring pair is >= 12 binades apart except DBL_MIN vs nonzero-only, which is ONE binade (-1024) — so that pair is separated only by including p = -1024, not by sweep width. Measured brackets on assertion (ii), which is what exposes the fabrication and what the finding missed entirely: with :900 left absolute, out_val/c = 3.0 only for p >= -10; it is 2.9999995818 at p = -20, 2.999695 at p = -30, and 2.5 at p = -39 and -40 — all with rc = 0 on SHIPPED code — and 2.0 at every p <= -41 once :886 is repaired alone. With the paired repair, out_val/c = 2.999999999999213 at every p from +1000 to -1030, identical to 16 digits. defects.why: CONFIRMED by measurement on cycc 6.6.2; all five refutation routes were tried and failed. (1) Not dimensionless: an eigenvalue is degree 1 in ||A||, so scaling A by an exact power of two scales |dlambda| identically while the 1e-12 threshold stays put. (2) No caller normalises: `eigen_power` has ZERO in-tree callers — it is a public entry point reached only from tests/. (3) "It is a convergence tolerance, not a divide-by-zero guard" is true as a description and does not exonerate it: an ABSOLUTE tolerance on a covariant quantity makes the routine's answer unit-dependent in both directions, and it reports rc = 0 while doing so. Measured on the suite's OWN fixture A1 = [[2,1],[1,3]] (hisab.tcyr:1502, abuse.tcyr:865), c = 2^p, max_iter = 500: p = 0 relerr 6.8e-14; p = -10 1.5e-10; p = -20 1.3e-7; p = -30 1.1e-4; p = -40 out/truth = 0.6909830056250525, i.e. 30.9% LOW with rc = 0. Top end: p = 0..+11 fine, p = +12 and every p above through +300 return rc = -8 (HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE) — at p = +12 the matrix entries are 8192 and 12288, an utterly ordinary magnitude, and lambda's ulp (2.2e-9) is three orders above the 1e-12 stop, so the iterate limit-cycles between adjacent floats and no max_iter can help. The finding UNDER-claimed the top end (it said "about +40" and hedged "input-dependent"); it is +12 on a fixture already in the suite. (4) The proposed relative repair breaks NO existing test: patching line 900 to `f64_mul(tol, f64_abs(new_eigenvalue))` and re-running the three suites that include linalg_ext.cyr gives 416 + 776 + 1827 = 3019 passed, 0 failed, identical to baseline — the suite compares through EP_TOL = 1e-11, so a 3.6x-looser stop is invisible to it. (5) The scale_test WAS wrong, in three measurable ways, and is rewritten below rather than being grounds to drop the verdict. NOTE the shared floor: even repaired, every candidate threshold dies at p <= -41 on both fixtures, because line 886's `|max_val| < EPSILON_F64` is a SECOND absolute-on-scaling guard at a separate site; repairing 900 alone leaves eigen_power returning a false NO_CONVERGENCE for any ||A|| below ~2^-41.

Measured at c = 2^-40 — A1 = [[2,1],[1,3]] returns 69.1% of the true eigenvalue (30.9% low); A0 = [[2,1],[1,2]] returns 83.3% (16.7% low, out/truth = 0.8333333333333334, i.e. it stopped at 2.5 where the answer is 3). Assert two things per p: (1) SCALE COVARIANCE — `out_val / c` is BIT-IDENTICAL to the p = 0 result, and out_vec bit-identical (this is the load-bearing assertion; it is exact under a relative rule and cannot be satisfied by an absolute one); (2) an accuracy FLOOR at relative 1e-11, the suite's own EP_TOL, not 1e-14. Measured first-bad-p under that assertion, which is the bracket: SHIPPED abs 1e-12 -> bad going UP at p = +12 and DOWN at p = -8 (fails BOTH ends); absolute DBL_EPSILON -> bad at p = 0 (500 iterations exhausted, never converges at any scale); absolute 1e-100 -> bad at p = 0 (same); relative EPSILON_F64 -> clean through +300, bottom floor -41; relative DBL_EPSILON -> clean through +300, bottom floor -41. Only the two RELATIVE forms survive, and they survive identically — so the test brackets every plausible repair and isolates relativity as the property under test. ⚠ An f64_to compare would be vacuous here and an ABSOLUTE compare would itself be the scale-dependence under test; the covariance assertion sidesteps both.

defects.guarded_quantity: r00 = |R[0][0]| from ganita_mat_qr of Z = A*Q — the growth factor of the dominant direction over one step. Q is orthonormal every iteration, so r00 = ||A*q1||, carrying the units of A's entries: degree 1 in ||A||, a plain magnitude, not squared. MEASURED, not argued: with the guard neutralised, out(c*A0) - out(A0) reproduces ln(c) to <= 1.4e-15 relative at every p in {0, +-20, -39..-60, +-100, -200, -332, +-400, +-600, +-800, +-1000, -1010, -1022}, which is only possible if r00 scales exactly linearly with c.

defects.why: Refutation attempted on all five avenues and all five fail against measurement. (1) NOT dimensionless: r00 has the units of A and scales exactly with it (above). (4) The proposed repair breaks NO existing test — measured, not assumed: with the guard replaced by `r00 > 0.0`, the three suites that include linalg_ext.cyr return hisab 416/416, abuse 776/776, modules 1827/1827, byte-identical to the shipped baseline. The two lyapunov tests are unreachable by the change (identity gives r00 = 1; iterations = -5 never enters the loop). defects.fabricates: Two distinct fabrications, both measured on the shipped tree. (a) TOTAL firing: every iteration skipped, count == 0, the else-branch at 1054-1055 stores exactly +0.0 (bit pattern 0x0) and returns rc = 0 — a Lyapunov exponent of zero, i.e. 'marginally stable', for a system contracting at -27.7 nats/step. Measured at p = -40 and every p below, down to -1022. (b) PARTIAL firing, which is subtler, worse, and NOT bit-identifiable: with a non-normal fixture whose transient r00 straddles 1e-12, only the contracting iterations are dropped and the mean is taken over the biased survivors. A0 = [[0.5, 0],[10, 0.9]] at p = -40 returns -26.351213 where the truth is -27.725887 — off by +1.374674 nats — and at p = -42 by +2.358899, always biased UPWARD, i.e. a contracting system reported as less stable than it is, with rc = 0 and no indication samples were dropped. A test that only checks 'is the result exactly 0.0' passes on this.
defects.correct_threshold: `r00 > 0.0` — guard exactly the ln domain and nothing more. ⚠ The filing's parenthetical 'equivalently r00 >= DBL_MIN' is REFUTED by measurement and must be dropped: a DBL_MIN variant fabricates 0x0 at p = -1022, where `r00 > 0.0` returns -708.396418532 correct to 1.4e-15 relative. Subnormal r00 is a perfectly good ln argument and must not be excluded. Second half of the repair, which the threshold alone does not fix: a dropped sample must not silently shrink the divisor. Either return an error code (or -inf) when any iteration is skipped, or divide by `iterations` rather than `count` — otherwise the partial-firing bias above survives any threshold, including a relative one, whenever the dominant direction genuinely collapses on some steps. A truly zero r00 means the dominant direction collapsed exactly; the honest report is -inf or an error, never a smaller sample count.
defects.scale_test: TWO fixtures, both required; measured on cyrius 6.6.2, ganita 1.2.4. Build c = 2^p exactly as bits (1023+p) << 52 so the scaling is bit-exact, n = 2, iterations = 64. (4) Breaks an existing test: CHECKED, not assumed — the only in-tree cmat_inverse assertions are tests/abuse.tcyr:347 (m=0), :353 (capped cmat_new), :420 (non-square), tests/modules.tcyr:8749 (m=0) and tests/hisab.tcyr:1430 (250x500 over cap). With matrix scale pinned at 1, absolute and relative thresholds COINCIDE, so the "conditioning is relative" defence cannot apply and only the squaring remains: sqrt(1e-12) = 1e-6 is the real cutoff on |pivot| where the constant reads 1e-12. defects.fabricates: On the low side: none — it reports an error, but the error is FALSE and its channel is overloaded. cmat_inverse returns the designed 0, the SAME value it returns for a null argument, a non-square argument and an over-cap augmented alloc, so a caller cannot distinguish "you passed garbage" from "hisab decided your cond-1e6 matrix was singular"; a caller that stores through it null-derefs, one that checks reports a nonexistent singularity. ⚠ CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: on the HIGH side it does fabricate. Measured, cmat_inverse(c·I) first returns a non-null WRONG matrix at c = 2^512 (1.34e154): max_norm overflows to +inf, `inf < 1e-12` is false so this guard passes, and cx_inv then computes d = inf and returns cx_new(re/inf, ...) = exactly zero, so the pivot row is annihilated and the ZERO MATRIX is returned with no error. That fabrication is cx_inv's squaring, not this guard's — but it is on the same path and bounds the test window (q <= 511 all correct, measured).
defects.correct_threshold: Un-square first, then make it relative, AND floor it — three parts, the third of which the original claim omitted and a probe caught: reject when `max_norm < DBL_MIN` (0x0010000000000000, the `_GEO_F64_TINY` constant 2.10.2 settled on, src/geo.cyr:26) OR `sqrt(max_norm) <= EPSILON_F64 * scale`, where scale = max |entry| of the current column or of m. ⚠ The claim's bare relative form `sqrt(max_norm) < EPSILON_F64 * max|entry|` REGRESSES a behaviour measured green today: for the all-zero matrix, max|entry| = 0, so the threshold is 0, `0 < 0` is false, the guard does not fire, cx_inv(0) fabricates cx_zero and the function returns a zero MATRIX where it currently returns 0 (probe2 control (A): all-zero 3x3 -> 0, passes on HEAD). The DBL_MIN floor and the `<=` both fix that. ⛔ AND THE REPAIR IS NOT LOCAL: cx_inv (src/complex.cyr:92-95) has its OWN squared-vs-squared guard that returns cx_zero() for |z| < 1e-12 — measured to fire at exactly 2^-40 (9.09e-13) and to be clean at 2^-39. Its stated window p in [-500,+500] with five distinct kill points (shipped p≈-20, un-squared p≈-40, DBL_EPSILON p≈-53, DBL_MIN p≈-505, relative never) does not exist: cx_inv's own 1e-12 flush at p = 40 (measured) means EVERY candidate repair of line 1150 fails from p = 40 down — the un-squared-absolute by returning 0, the DBL_MIN and relative forms by returning the all-zero matrix — so the sweep's real discriminating window is p in [20, 39] (c in 9.1e-13 .. 9.5e-7), SIX decades, not 485, and it separates shipped-from-repaired only, never repaired-from-repaired. Use this instead, in three parts. (A) FIXED-SCALE KILL, no units change needed and immune to the conditioning defence: for k = 0..60, M_k = 2x2 complex diag(1, 2^-k) — matrix norm exactly 1, cond 2^k, inverse exactly representable — assert cmat_inverse(M_k) != 0 and inv[1][1] == 2^k bit-exactly. (B) SCALE COVARIANCE, run only after cx_inv is repaired as above, otherwise it measures cx_inv: M0 = 3x3 identity (cond 1), c = 2^p, assert cmat_inverse(c*M0) != 0 and c * inv[i][j] == M0inv[i][j] bit-exactly (the inverse is covariant as 1/c, so the compared value must be rescaled by c; powers of two make it exact, no tolerance needed). Sweep p in [-1000, +511]: on HEAD this fails from p = -20 (MEASURED) and, at the top, first returns a non-null WRONG (all-zero) matrix at p = +512 (MEASURED, norm_sq overflow inside cx_inv) — so +511 is the hard ceiling of the window, not +500 by estimate. With cx_inv repaired the candidates re-separate: un-squared-absolute kills at p = -40, DBL_EPSILON at p = -53, DBL_MIN-on-norm_sq at p = -512 (norm_sq underflow), relative never. (C) CONTROLS killing a guard-deleted mutant, both of which the repair must keep green: the all-zero 3x3 must still return 0 (passes on HEAD, MEASURED — and is exactly what the claim's bare relative form breaks), and a 3x3 with an exactly-zero first column and unit diagonal elsewhere must return 0 rather than nan/zero entries.

defects.guarded_quantity: vtv = v^T v for the left Householder vector after v[0] += sign(v0)*||x||, i.e. exactly 2*||x||*(||x|| + |x0|), bounded in [2||x||^2, 4||x||^2] where x is the tail of column k (rows k..m) of the working matrix W. Dimension: LENGTH SQUARED, degree 2 in matrix entries. Measured on A(c) = diag(1) (+) c*[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,10]]: the k=1 reflector has vtv = 148*c^2, k=2 has ~6*c^2, k=3 (length-1 tail) has 0.174*c^2 — pure c^2, confirming degree 2. Reachable range is bounded BELOW by the :225 norm gate: norm_l > 1e-12 forces vtv > 2e-24 whenever line 240 is reached at all.
defects.protects: The division two_over_vtv = f64_div(F64_TWO, vtv) on line 241, and the reflector application W -= (2/vtv)*v*(v^T W) plus the Vt/U accumulations that use it. Nothing else in the branch has a floor.
defects.why: A squared quantity is compared against the unsquared EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12, so the effective cut is on ||x|| ~ 7.07e-7, six decades above the 1e-12 the sibling gate at :225 applies to the UNSQUARED norm of the same vector — the pair is self-inconsistent by construction, the class repaired at six sites in geo.cyr in 2.10.1/2.10.2. 2/vtv is finite down to vtv ~ 1.1e-308 and :225 already guarantees vtv > 2e-24, so no division can fail here: the guard is mathematically redundant and only its wrong threshold has any effect. All four refutation routes were tested and failed. (a) NOT dimensionless: measured to scale as c^2 exactly. (b) The caller DOES normalise — svd_golub_kahan:787 balances by _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)) — but that bounds only the GLOBAL max; a block-scaled/graded matrix has max = 1, sc = 1, and its column tails are still O(c), so balancing does not reach this quantity. (c) NOT a convergence tolerance: it guards a division one line below. (d) NO existing test constrains it: with :240 changed to vtv > 0, tests/hisab 416, foundation 351, modules 1798, edge_cases 233, abuse 776 = 3574/3574 pass, and the three-site repair passes 3574/3574 too. The positive proof is a one-line mutation on a pristine `git archive HEAD` tree: at c = 1e-7 the shipped code returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE and the same tree with line 240 reading `f64_gt(vtv, f64_from(0))` returns HSB_ERR_NONE with S/c = 17.412505 / 0.875161 / 0.196867, every value correct. Internally the effect is larger: with the guard and its two siblings repaired, _lp_bidiagonalize is bit-stable scale-covariant (d_i/c and f_i/c constant) from c = 1e-1 to c = 1e-12, while the shipped code perturbs the bidiagonal at c = 1e-6, loses the k=2 reflector at 1e-7, and collapses to the raw matrix entries at 1e-8. defects.why: SURVIVES, but the original reasoning is wrong in its operative half and I have replaced it. (1) The scaling argument is REFUTED by the caller. _lp_bidiagonalize has exactly one caller in the tree (svd_golub_kahan:790), which balances first: sc = _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)), As = A/sc, so ||As||_max is in [1,2) and the divisor is an exact power of two. Measured on the isolating matrix below: rescaling A by 2^-80, 2^-10, 2^+40, 2^+200 gives singular-value ratios that are BIT-IDENTICAL (max deviation 0.000e+00) and a reconstruction error identically 1.000e-07 at every scale. A units change therefore cannot reach this guard at all, and post-balancing the absolute EPSILON_F64 at :288 is a relative-to-||A||_max drop policy that is defensible on its own terms. (2) What is NOT defensible is the squaring, and that is the whole defect: :288 declares the policy "an entry below 1e-12*||A|| is negligible" on a degree-1 quantity, and :301 applies the SAME constant to a degree-2 quantity three lines later, which moves the identical policy's cutoff to sqrt(1e-12) = 7.07e-7*||A|| -- a silent five-to-six-order inflation of the accepted backward error, with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE. Dead band (balanced units): ||x|| in (1e-12, 5e-7..7.07e-7), where :288 says "keep" and :301 says "skip". The division itself cannot fail there: :288 having passed implies vtv_r >= 2e-24, and 2/vtv_r stays finite down to vtv_r = 1.11e-308, so the guard protects nothing and only its threshold acts. The same file already states the correct principle at :424 ("The zero test must be RELATIVE to the block"), and the only relative reference available here is ||As||_max ~ 1, which :288 uses correctly and :301 squares.
defects.fabricates: Corrected -- the original overstated it. defects.why: CONFIRMED, and causally isolated by a control build. Three lines above, the deflation loop at :543 tests THE SAME ENTRIES against the relative threshold EPSILON_F64*(|d_i| + |d_{i+1}|); this loop tests them against the bare absolute EPSILON_F64. They disagree exactly when EPSILON_F64*(|d_i|+|d_{i+1}|) <= |f_i| < EPSILON_F64, i.e. for any sub-block with |d_i|+|d_{i+1}| < 1 — the relative test correctly KEEPS a coupling this loop then walks past, leaving a superdiagonal entry that is still nonzero and now never gets zeroed or chased. Verbatim the defect repaired in the sibling _lp_tridiag_qr in 2.7.0, documented at :1064 ('a second loop whose test was an ABSOLUTE EPSILON_F64, inconsistent with the RELATIVE threshold the deflation test above uses ... the block bounds and the deflation test could contradict each other'); the SVD path never received it. All five refutation avenues were tested and closed: (1) the quantity is degree 1, not dimensionless; (2) the caller DOES normalise but only the global max — measured, the probe defeats it with sc == 1.0 exactly; (3) it being a convergence test rather than a divide guard is the reason an absolute epsilon is wrong, not a defence; (4) the repair breaks NO existing test — all five suites, 3611 assertions, pass identically on the shipped tree, the :580-repaired tree, and the fully-repaired tree (so the suite is also blind to the defect); (5) CAUSALITY ISOLATED: a control tree that makes the Givens guards at :650/:692 scale-free while leaving :580 absolute is correct for every c down to 1e-12 and silently wrong from c = 1e-13 — the cliff sits at exactly EPSILON_F64.

defects.guarded_quantity: r = sqrt(y*y + z*z), the norm of the RIGHT Givens vector. On the first pass of every chase (k == p_lo) y = d[p_lo]^2 - mu and z = d[p_lo]*f[p_lo] -- entries of B^T*B - mu*I, dimension MATRIX-ENTRY SQUARED (degree 2). On every later pass y = superdiag[k], z = -sn*f[k+1], degree 1. The file proves this against itself: on later passes that same r is stored straight into superdiag[k-1] at :658, i.e. it IS a matrix entry there, while on the first pass :657's `k > p_lo` suppresses that store because r is not one. One variable, two dimensions, one absolute threshold.
defects.protects: Nothing. cs = f64_div(y, r) and sn = f64_div(-z, r) are computed at :648-649, ABOVE the test, and merely overwritten at :651-652; the division is never gated. The guard only substitutes the identity rotation (cs=1, sn=0). It is not the deflation/convergence criterion either -- that is :543, and it is already correctly written relative to |d[i]|+|d[i+1]|.
defects.why: CONFIRMED, and the squared-vs-unsquared dimension is now proven QUANTITATIVELY rather than argued. Substituting cs=1,sn=0 makes the implicit-shift step the identity (bulge = -sn*d[k+1] = 0), the block is reproduced unchanged, and the outer loop spins to max_iter -- the same failure the file already documents at :406 for the zero-diagonal case, reached by the guard instead of by a zero. Isolation: swapping ONLY this one constant to F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, already defined at src/error.cyr:45) recovers the entire 1e-7..1e-11 band on the shipped tree, so the band attributes to this line alone. Dimension proof: with r = 1.9021*c^2 on the first pass, the last-clean decade must go as sqrt(threshold). Measured over four thresholds spanning 10 decades -- 1e-6 -> 1e-3, 1.4901e-8 -> 1e-4, 1e-12 (shipped) -> 1e-6, 2.2204e-16 -> 1e-7 -- all 4 match the sqrt law exactly, where a degree-1 quantity would have given 1e-6 / 1e-8 / 1e-12 / 1e-15, off by up to 8 decades. ⚠ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING, BOTH MEASURED. (1) The caller DOES normalise, and the filing's scale-test rationale is wrong because of it: svd_golub_kahan:789 balances by _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)), an exact power-of-two divisor, so UNIFORM rescaling is exactly invariant -- probe B measured c*[[1,1,0],[0,1,1],[0,0,1]] over 20 decades and got identical singular values at every one, which is also why the existing suite's 1e-200 / 1e+200 / 1e-10 tests pass. A true "same problem in different units" test can NEVER reach this guard. The quantity that scales is the ACTIVE BLOCK's magnitude relative to ||A||_max -- the condition number, not the unit -- so the discriminating input must be MIXED-scale. The filing's matrix is right; its stated reason is not. (2) The filing's 150-decade span is not satisfiable by ANY repair at :650: below c = 1e-12 the independent ABSOLUTE EPSILON_F64 superdiagonal tests at :557/:580/:590 take over (measured: patching those as well moves the wrong-value onset from 1e-13 to 1e-12), so those decades test other guards and do not attribute. Refutation avenues checked and all closed: the quantity is not bounded (:658 proves it), the normalisation does not reach it, it is not a convergence tolerance, and the proposed repair breaks no existing test -- 3611/3611 assertions pass across all five suites both before and after, identical counts.

Record that as a known gap rather than claiming full coverage; separating that pair requires probing _lp_bidiag_qr directly with a hand-built diag/superdiag, or repairing :557/:580/:590 first.

defects.guarded_quantity: r = sqrt(y*y + z*z) for the LEFT Givens rotation, y = diag[k] (the value just stored at :670, new_dk = cs*dk - sn*fk) and z = bulge = -sn*d[k+1] (:667). Dimension: MATRIX ENTRY, degree 1 — it is the 2-norm of rows (k,k+1) of column k of the working bidiagonal after the right rotation. Because svd_golub_kahan divides A by _lp_pow2_floor(max|A|) at :789 before bidiagonalising, r is effectively a FRACTION OF ||A||_max, not an absolute physical magnitude; the filing's "it scales with the active block" is right in spirit but wrong in mechanism (see why).
defects.protects: cs = f64_div(y, r) at :690 and sn = f64_div(f64_neg(z), r) at :691 — both computed ABOVE the guard and then overwritten, so only the identity substitution is gated. Confirmed: the divisions execute unconditionally. Note :697 `store64(diag + k*8, r)` is also unconditional, so when the guard fires diag[k] is set to the sub-threshold r while superdiag[k]/diag[k+1] are left untouched by cs=1, sn=0 — the block is reproduced exactly.
defects.why: NOT REFUTED, but three of the filing's claims are refuted by measurement and are corrected here. (1) The quantity is degree 1 (a matrix entry of the balanced bidiagonal); the threshold is the absolute EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 (src/error.cyr:26). The division fails only at r = 0; cs, sn are bounded by 1, so there is no overflow path — 1e-12 is a chosen scale, which by the 2.10.2 rule is itself the defect. (2) REFUTED — the filing's causal story ("for a sub-block at scale c, r ~ c, so the guard fires once c < 1e-12"). Instrumented counters on a copy of the module (guard-fire counters at :650 and :692, at the relative deflation :543, at the ABSOLUTE p_hi loop :580, and at _lp_split_zero_diag) over the filing's OWN sweep, c = 1e-0 .. 1e-20: g692 = 0 at every one of 21 decades. The c in [1e-7, 1e-12] non-convergence is :650 alone (g650 = 270 = max_iter = 30n^2, rc = -8), and the silent 1.000/1.000 at c <= 1e-13 the filing attributes to THIS guard is the absolute superdiagonal test at :580 (phi_defl = 1, g692 = 0, g650 = 0) — the block is deflated away before the chase is ever entered. (3) REFUTED — a units-only scale test cannot discriminate this guard at all, because the caller DOES normalise: _lp_pow2_floor makes A and 2^k*A bit-identical (48/48 rows of a x2^+40 / x2^-40 control identical in rc, S and every counter), and a non-power-of-2 x10^-j rescale moves the fired r only within [9.4e-15, 1.6e-14] — the balancing residue in [1,2) — never changing the outcome. What the balancing CANNOT remove is INTERNAL grading, and that is the real mechanism: on 11000 random n=2..6 matrices with per-entry exponents uniform in [-E,E], the guard first fires at E = 4 and fires on 484 of 11000 overall (by E: 1/12/45/59/83/70/67/70/77 for E = 4..20). It is decisive and it is NOT shadowed by :650: on a differential run of the identical RNG stream against a copy with only :692 changed to F64_TINY, 218 trials change (rc, S), 14 are materially worse on shipped (>=10x and >1e-8 relative reconstruction error), and 11 of those 14 have g650 = 0 with split = 0 and phi_defl = 0 — this guard firing alone. Reachability mechanism: r^2 = (cs*dk - sn*fk)^2 + (sn*dk1)^2 can collapse mid-chase even though _lp_split_zero_diag guarantees every diag >= 1e-12*||block|| BEFORE the sweep, because dk1 is rewritten at :672/:704 during the chase and the split test never runs again.
defects.fabricates: Measured, and NARROWER than the filing claims. The observed mode is the STALL branch only: cs = 1, sn = 0 leaves superdiag[k] and diag[k+1] unchanged while :697 writes the sub-1e-12 r into diag[k], so the sweep reproduces the block and fires again on every one of the 30*n^2 sweeps (fixture: g692 = 480/480 for n = 4, 1080/1080 for n = 6), after which svd_golub_kahan returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE at :798 with out_S NEVER WRITTEN — the caller keeps whatever its buffer held (all zeros in the probe, and svd_golub_kahan's own tests at tests/hisab.tcyr:2197-2200 already record that this makes "s == 0" assertions vacuous). 14 of 14 materially-wrong shipped trials had exactly this shape. The filing's SECOND branch — "mid-chase, a dropped bulge with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE and singular values of a matrix that is not A" — was NOT OBSERVED: of the 484 firing trials, 0 returned HSB_ERR_NONE with a wrong answer attributable to this guard alone (all 10 fire-alone trials returned -8). So the failure is LOUD, not silent — which lowers the severity the filing assigned it, and the filing's attribution of probe2's silent 1.000/1.000 region to this guard is measured false.
defects.correct_threshold: r >= F64_TINY (DBL_MIN, error.cyr:45 — the same constant geo.cyr already uses as _GEO_F64_TINY), i.e. guard exactly what makes the division fail and nothing more. Measured against the alternatives on the 11000-trial graded corpus, bad trials (rc != 0 or reconstruction rel err > 1e-8): 1748 at the shipped 1e-12, 1743 at 1e-14, 1742 at 2.22e-16, 1741 at DBL_MIN — monotone, with 7 trials fixed and 0 broken by DBL_MIN versus shipped, and the candidates differing pairwise on 54-112 trials, so the corpus ranks them rather than merely tying them. A RELATIVE alternative (EPSILON_F64 * (|diag[k]| + |diag[k+1]|), consistent with :543) is NOT justified here and should not be adopted: the caller has already balanced, r is the very quantity the division consumes, and the identity rotation is mathematically correct only at r = 0. VERIFIED SAFE, not assumed: patching only :692 to F64_TINY in an isolated tree passes all five suites unchanged — 416/359/1827/233/776 = 3611 assertions, 0 failed, byte-identical pass counts to a control tree cut from the same snapshot with the line reverted. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. (B) BRACKET — a single fixture fires at r ~ 1.5e-14 and therefore CANNOT separate 1e-14 from 2.22e-16 from DBL_MIN; the corpus does. 11000 matrices, n = 2..6, per-entry value = mantissa in [-1,1] (3 digits) times 10^e with e uniform in [-E,E] for E = 0,2,...,20, 200 per (n,E), from a fixed LCG so it is deterministic; assert rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and reconstruction < 1e-8, and record the bad-trial count.
