defects.guarded_quantity: vtv = v^T v after the same-sign Householder shift. _lp_sign returns +1 for x >= 0, so the shift never cancels and vtv = 2*||x||*(||x|| + |x1|) exactly, in [2||x||^2, 4||x||^2]. Degree 2 in the trailing column x = W[k+1..n, k]. CORRECTION to the filing: it is NOT an absolute length squared. eigen_qr:1245 balances first (sc = _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)); As = A/sc), so vtv is measured in units of max|A_ij|^2 and is therefore DIMENSIONLESS -- but it is the SQUARE of a dimensionless ratio (the trailing column's magnitude relative to the largest entry anywhere in A, i.e. the matrix's dynamic range), while :922 tests the FIRST power of that same ratio against the same constant. Degree 2 vs degree 1 against one shared 1e-12 is the defect; "different physical units" is not.
defects.protects: two_over_vtv = f64_div(F64_TWO, vtv) on :937, and the reflector's whole symmetric rank-2 update plus the Q accumulation built from it. It is a divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance -- the division is on the very next line, and the convergence tolerances in this file (:1050, :1076) are separate and correctly RELATIVE.
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON FIVE FRONTS; THE VERDICT SURVIVES, THE scale_test DOES NOT. (1) "Dimensionless/bounded so absolute is fine" -- half true and it does not save the guard. The balancing at eigen_qr:1245 does bound vtv above (max|A_ij| in [0.5,1) after _lp_pow2_floor, so vtv <~ 4n), which is why the existing suite's "eigen_qr @1e200" test (tests/hisab.tcyr:2139) passes and why the routine is scale-invariant under a UNIFORM rescale. But balancing normalises the GLOBAL scale, not the trailing column's: a matrix with an O(1) entry anywhere keeps its small sub-blocks small after balancing, so vtv still ranges over the full dynamic range of the input, and a degree-2 quantity against 1e-12 fires 5-6 decades before the degree-1 gate at :922 that guards the same reflector. (2) "The caller normalises" -- it does, and I MEASURED that it is not enough: shipped code, A(c) = diag(1) (+) c*S3, n=4, returns the WRONG spectrum with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE on 12 of 45 sweep points (c = 3e-7 through 7e-12). (3) "Convergence tolerance" -- no, it guards f64_div on :937. (4) "The repair breaks an existing test" -- CHECKED, not assumed: with `if (f64_gt(vtv, f64_from(0)) == 1)` installed, all five suites pass, 416 + 359 + 1827 + 233 + 776 = 3611 assertions, 0 failures. (5) "The scale_test does not discriminate" -- THIS ONE LANDED, TWICE, and the finding is corrected below rather than withdrawn. The guard is in fact unreachable-false: :922 guarantees norm > 1e-12, and vtv >= 2*norm^2 > 2e-24, so 2/vtv is finite by construction and only the threshold ever acts. Measured onset brackets the prediction exactly: vtv = 6.828c^2 crosses 1e-12 at c = 3.827e-7, and the sweep is correct at 7e-7 and wrong at 3e-7.
defects.fabricates: The eigenvalues of a DIFFERENT tridiagonal matrix, with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE. The skipped reflector leaves W[k+2..n, k] nonzero and the extraction at :1024 reads only the two bands, discarding it. MEASURED on the shipped 2.13.0 tree, A(c) = diag(1) (+) c*S3 with n = 4 and max_iter = 100000: lambda/c = (1.414213562, -1.414213562, 0.000000000) where the truth is (2, -1, -1) -- 29% wrong on the dominant eigenvalue and an eigenvalue reported as 0 that is really -c. That is the spectrum of [[0,c,0],[c,0,c],[0,c,0]], the matrix that survives the skipped reflector. CORRECTION to the filing's extent: the fabricating window is bounded on BOTH sides and is about 5.7 decades, not open-ended. Correct at 7e-7; wrong-with-rc-0 at 3e-7, 1e-7, 3e-8 ... 7e-12 (12 consecutive sweep points); and from c = 1e-13 downward it stops fabricating and returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE (rc = -8) all the way to 1e-160, because the degree-1 gate at :922 (norm = 1.414c vs 1e-12) fires there and the Wilkinson-shift guards at :1098/:1103 then stall the iteration. Loud failure below the window, silent wrong answers inside it.
defects.correct_threshold: vtv > 0 (equivalently >= DBL_MIN) -- exactly what makes 2/vtv fail and nothing more, the _GEO_F64_TINY = DBL_MIN rule from 2.10.2. SHARPENED by measurement: at this site `vtv > 0`, `vtv >= DBL_MIN` and `vtv > EPSILON_F64*EPSILON_F64` are not three candidate repairs to choose between, they are the SAME repair -- provably (the upstream :922 gate forces norm > 1e-12, and the same-sign shift makes vtv >= 2*norm^2 > 2e-24 > EPSILON_F64^2) and measurably (three separately compiled builds classify identically on all 45 sweep points). The guard is therefore dead code that can only misfire, so deleting it outright is equally correct; `vtv > 0` is the defence-in-depth form and is what I verified against the suites. Do NOT reach for a norm^2-relative threshold: it is unnecessary here and would only re-introduce a tuned scale.
defects.scale_test: THE FILED scale_test IS WRONG TWICE AND MUST NOT BE USED AS WRITTEN -- both refutations measured, not argued. (A) "The SAME problem in different units" is VACUOUS on this routine. eigen_qr's first act is to balance (:1245, sc = _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)); As = A/sc), so a uniform rescale is undone before _lp_tridiagonalize ever sees it: A = c*S3 alone (n=3, eig = 2c,-c,-c) returns the exact spectrum on the SHIPPED, DEFECTIVE code at every decade from c = 1e-1 to 1e-300 (measured, 33 points, all correct). Anyone re-deriving the test from that phrase writes a sweep that passes on the bug. The discriminating variable is DYNAMIC RANGE, not units: an O(1) anchor must PIN the balance factor while the block shrinks. The filing's own matrix happens to do this (the leading 1 holds max_abs at 1) but its rationale does not say so. (B) The 150-decade range FAILS 138 of its 150 points WITH THE PROPOSED REPAIR INSTALLED. Measured: with `vtv > f64_from(0)` at :936, the sweep is correct on c = 1e-1..1e-12 and returns HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE on every decade from 1e-13 to 1e-160 -- because four OTHER absolute-EPSILON_F64 guards floor it, none of them this one: :922 (norm > EPSILON_F64, norm = 1.414c, fires at c <= 7.07e-13), and the Wilkinson-shift pair :1098/:1103 (|delta| and |denom| vs EPSILON_F64, both degree 1) which strip the shift and stall unshifted QR on the repeated eigenvalue -c. Freeing all five (adding :1117, r > EPSILON_F64) makes the identical sweep correct down to 1e-154 and only then failing on c^2 underflow. A test floored at 1e-150 would read as "the repair does not work" and get the repair reverted. THE CORRECTED TEST: A(c) = diag(1) (+) c*S3, n = 4, S3 = [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,0]], eig(S3) = (2,-1,-1) exactly, so eig(A) = {1, 2c, -c, -c}. S3 is load-bearing: it makes the k=1 reflector's v = c*[1,1] have BOTH components nonzero, where a single-nonzero column is a sign flip whose skip is harmless and would pass vacuously. Sweep c = 1e-1 down to 1e-12, one assertion per decade, PLUS 7e-7 and 3e-7 to bracket the crossing at vtv = 6.828c^2 = EPSILON_F64 (c = 3.827e-7); assert rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and (lambda1,lambda2,lambda3)/c == (2,-1,-1) to 1e-9 absolute. Cap at c <= 1e-1 (at c = 0.7, 2c exceeds the anchor 1 and the descending-|lambda| sort permutes the output slots -- a probe artifact that reported "wrong" for every threshold including the correct one, caught only because all five builds agreed on it). FLOOR at 1e-12 and say why in the test comment, or file :922/:1098/:1103 as the sibling defects of the same class and extend to 1e-154 only after they are repaired too. DISCRIMINATION over that range, measured on five separately compiled builds: shipped EPSILON_F64 wrong on 12 points; DBL_EPSILON (2.22e-16) wrong on 6 points (3e-9..7e-12) -- killed; sqrt(DBL_EPSILON) (1.49e-8) would be wrong from c <= 4.7e-5 -- killed with a decade to spare; `vtv > 0`, `>= DBL_MIN` and `> EPSILON_F64^2` correct on all 45 and mutually indistinguishable, which is a theorem about :922 rather than a gap in the sweep.

defects.guarded_quantity: |denom| where denom = delta + sign(delta)*sqrt(delta^2 + e2^2), delta = (d1-d2)/2. Dimension: MATRIX ENTRY (degree 1) in the entries of the BALANCED tridiagonal T; with the correct sign |denom| >= |e2|. Refined against the caller: eigen_qr divides A by _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)) at :1243 before tridiagonalizing, so the quantity is INVARIANT to the caller's units (a power-of-two rescale is bit-exact; any rescale moves it by <2x) and scales only with the ACTIVE SUB-BLOCK's magnitude relative to the balanced whole. Measured on the shipped tree: the same problem at s = 1e-200, 1e-200... 1, 3, 1024 gives an identical pass/fail structure — the failure boundary tracks the sub-block ratio alone.
defects.protects: f64_div(e2sq, denom) in the Wilkinson shift at :1104. With the correct sign the division cannot fail: |e2sq/denom| <= |e2|, and denom == 0 implies e2 == 0, where the fallback mu = d2 is the right answer anyway. The one path that can reach a true 0 with e2 != 0 is the sign-forcing branch at :1098 (sgn := +1 whenever |delta| < EPSILON_F64, even for delta < 0), where delta + sqrt(delta^2+e2^2) cancels; that is why a zero guard is still warranted, and it is the ONLY thing this guard legitimately protects.
defects.why: Degree-1 quantity, absolute threshold (EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12), on a value that scales with the sub-block, not with the balanced whole. None of the refutation routes hold: the quantity is not dimensionless; the caller's balancing normalises only the WHOLE-matrix scale (measured invariant over 400 decades of units) and does nothing to the sub-block ratio, which is the axis that actually reaches the guard; the guard is a divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance (the deflation tolerances at :1050 and :1076 are relative and separate); and the proposed threshold breaks no existing test — all five suites are 3574/3574 with it installed. Instrumented counters confirm the guard fires on well-posed input: on a 4x4 with an O(1) leading block and a trailing 2x2 of scale t it fires 3 of 4 shift computations for every t <= 1e-13, permanently substituting mu = d2 (Rayleigh) for the Wilkinson shift. BUT TWO OF THE FILING'S OWN CLAIMS ARE WRONG, BOTH FOUND BY MUTATION RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT. (1) THE EVIDENCE IS MISATTRIBUTED: on the dense fixture at c = 1e-12 the instrumented shipped build fires this guard ZERO times (g1103f=0, g1103p=31) — the silent rc = 0 answer wrong by 0.98% is produced entirely by the OTHER absolute epsilon in the same loop, `f64_gt(r, EPSILON_F64)` at :1117, which fires 30 times; repairing :1117 alone makes that whole sweep exact to 1e-20, and repairing :1103 alone leaves it bit-identical to shipped. (2) EACH GUARD MASKS THE OTHER, so the site is real but not independently observable: on the antisymmetric fixture, shipped fails from 1e-13, fix-1103-only fails from 1e-13 (identical output), fix-1117-only fails from 1e-13 (identical output), and only fix-BOTH converges — because with mu = d2 = 0 the rotation radius is r = c and with mu = -c it is sqrt(2)c, and both are below 1e-12 exactly where denom is, so :1117 zeroes the rotation before the shift quality can matter. On a generic tiny block (nonzero diagonal) the Rayleigh fallback still converges and the isolated effect of this guard is 1-2 ULP; the consequential effect is confined to the zero-diagonal cycle, where it is total. So: real defect, correctly diagnosed as an absolute epsilon on a degree-1 quantity, with a repair that is a measured NO-OP unless :1117 is repaired in the same change.
defects.fabricates: Once :1117 is repaired (and only then), HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE with out_vals never written — the caller's zero-filled buffer reads as an all-zero spectrum, i.e. a plausible "this matrix is singular" answer for a matrix whose true spectrum is {1, +c, -c}. Measured (fix-1117-only build): eigen_qr(diag(1) (+) c*[[0,1],[1,0]]) returns rc = -8 with all three eigenvalue slots left at 0.0 for every c <= 1e-13, and rc = 0 with bit-exact +-1 ratios for every c >= 1e-12. On the shipped tree it fabricates NOTHING ON ITS OWN: the two rc = -8 / silent-0.98%-error observations in the original filing both reproduce with this guard hard-wired open, so they are :1117's fabrications, not this one's. On a tiny block with a nonzero diagonal (Rayleigh fallback still converges) the isolated damage is 1-2 ULP in the returned eigenvalues, rc = 0.
defects.correct_threshold: denom != 0 (equivalently |denom| >= DBL_MIN; error.cyr now carries F64_TINY = 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 for exactly this). A relative alternative EPSILON_F64 * (|d1| + |d2| + |e2|), matching the deflation threshold this same function uses at :1050 and :1076, also passes the whole sweep. ⚠ LAND IT TOGETHER WITH :1117 (`f64_gt(r, EPSILON_F64)` -> `r != 0`, r = hypot(x,z), also degree 1): measured, this repair alone changes nothing on either fixture in the filing, and a reviewer who lands it alone, sees no change, and reverts it will have "refuted" a real defect. Neither half is redundant — :1117 alone fixes the dense/silent-wrong case and :1103 alone fixes nothing, but only both together fix the zero-shift cycle. Verified non-regressing: 416+351+1798+233+776 = 3574/3574 assertions pass with :1103 alone repaired and with both repaired.
defects.scale_test: PAIRED-MUTANT SWEEP; the unpaired form is measured not to discriminate. Fixture (correct as filed): eigen_qr(diag(1) (+) c*[[0,1],[1,0]], n=3) — spectrum {1, +c, -c} EXACTLY for every c, and the block is the classical zero-shift cycle, so it is the one family where losing the Wilkinson shift is fatal rather than merely 1-2 ULP. Sweep c = 1e-1 down to 1e-150, one assertion per decade: rc == HSB_ERR_NONE, lambda[1]/c == +1 and lambda[2]/c == -1 to 1e-12. Run it against FOUR builds and require all four rows, or it proves nothing: shipped -> rc=-8 from 1e-13 (measured); :1103 repaired alone -> rc=-8 from 1e-13, byte-identical to shipped (measured); :1117 repaired alone -> rc=-8 from 1e-13, byte-identical to shipped (measured); BOTH repaired -> rc=0 with bit-exact +-1 through 1e-150 (measured; convergence actually holds to 1e-157, degrades 1e-158..1e-161 and dies at 1e-162 where e2*e2 underflows into the subnormals). Add the dense control, which separates the two sites: diag(1) (+) c*[[4,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,2]], n=4, asserting lambda/c == {4.732050808, 3, 1.267949192} — shipped is SILENTLY wrong at c = 1e-12 (4.685623325, rc = 0) and repairing :1103 alone does not move it by one ULP, while repairing :1117 alone makes it exact at every decade to 1e-20. ⚠ DO NOT write this as a units test: eigen_qr balances by _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)), so "the same problem in different units" is measured invariant (s = 1e-200 .. 1e+200, powers of two bit-exact) and such a test passes vacuously on the shipped tree; the discriminating axis is the sub-block ratio c. Brackets 1e-12 (EPSILON_F64), 2.2e-16 (DBL_EPSILON), 1e-14/1e-15 and 1e-6 (sqrt EPSILON_F64, for a repair that mis-reads the dimension). It does NOT bracket DBL_MIN — the e2*e2 underflow floor at ~1e-161 makes every threshold below that unreachable through this entry point, so `|denom| >= DBL_MIN` and `denom != 0` are indistinguishable here and both are acceptable; the original filing's claim that 150 decades brackets 2.2e-308 is false.

defects.guarded_quantity: r = sqrt(x*x + z*z), the Givens radius of the bulge-chasing rotation. At k == p_lo, x = diag[p_lo] - mu and z = offdiag[p_lo+1]; at k > p_lo (where it actually fires, measured) x = offdiag[k] as just rewritten and z = sn*offdiag[k+2], the bulge. Dimension: MATRIX ENTRY (degree 1), scaling with the active deflated block -- and, decisively, with the QR iteration's own convergence tail, since driving these offdiagonals to zero IS the algorithm.
defects.protects: cs = f64_div(x, r) and sn = f64_div(z, r). The guard is correctly PLACED (before the divisions, unlike :650/:692), so it does gate them; only its threshold is wrong.
defects.why: The defect is real and I isolated it, but the filing's stated ARGUMENT for it is refuted and its scale_test proves nothing about this site. (1) REFUTED -- the units framing. _lp_tridiag_qr has exactly ONE caller, eigen_qr:1251, and it balances immediately before at :1243 (sc = _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_mat_max_abs(A)); As = A/sc, an exact power-of-two divide), so max|entry| of the matrix reaching this guard is always in [1,2). Measured: a PURE units change, c*[[4,1,2],[1,3,0],[2,0,6]] over c = 10^-330..10^+300 (631 decades), is correct at every one of the 609 normal decades, and the 22 subnormal decades (c <= 1e-309) fail IDENTICALLY in shipped code and in all four repaired variants -- so that tail is a different guard (pow2_floor returns 1.0 for a subnormal max), not this one. A change of units cannot reach this guard. (2) REFUTED -- the filing's scale_test. On its own family, diag(1) (+) c*[[0,1],[1,0]], I measured ship, repair-:1103-only and repair-:1117-only ALL returning rc = -8 from c <= 1e-13; only repairing both passes. So that sweep attributes nothing to :1117. Its proposed separator (2x2 with b = 1e-3*|a-d|) does not separate either: for a 2x2, denom = delta + sgn*sqrt(delta^2+e2^2) ~ c(a-d) and r ~ |d0 - mu| ~ c(a-d) are the same magnitude by construction. (3) NOT REFUTED, and now isolated. Replacement family diag(1) (+) c*[[4,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,2]] (n = 4): repairing :1103 alone is bit-identical to ship and fixes NOTHING; repairing :1117 alone is correct at every c from 1e-1 to 1e-30. (4) SHARPENED mechanism -- I instrumented the guard. It does not fire on the first Givens. At c = 1e-12 it fires 30 times at k = 2 > p_lo on the CONVERGENCE TAIL, with r decaying geometrically 5.45e-13 -> 2.36e-13 -> ... -> 3.34e-17, while the true rotation is an utterly ordinary cs = 0.756, sn = 0.655, and the file's own relative threshold EPSILON_F64*(|d_k|+|d_k+1|) at those same points is 4.3e-24 -- eleven orders BELOW r. Balancing pins the GLOBAL max to [1,2); it does not pin the scale of a deflated sub-block, and nothing pins the convergence tail, which by construction runs to zero. So an absolute floor under r stops the iteration rotating the moment the active block's scale falls under ~1e-12. The divisions fail only at r = 0 and |x|/r, |z|/r <= 1 gives no overflow path, so r > 0 is the whole requirement and 1e-12 is a scale chosen for it -- the same relative-vs-absolute inconsistency the comment at :1064 says 2.7.0 repaired in this very function's p_lo loop, with the deflation tests at :1050 and :1076 relative 60 lines above. Also checked and refuted: this is not a convergence tolerance (it fabricates a 0.98%-wrong eigenvalue with rc = 0 while the true rotation is well-conditioned), and it is not squared-vs-unsquared (r and EPSILON_F64 are both degree 1).
defects.fabricates: cs = 1, sn = 0 -- the IDENTITY rotation, in place of a well-conditioned one (measured cs = 0.756, sn = 0.655). Two outcomes, both measured on diag(1) (+) c*[[4,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,2]], n = 4: at c = 1e-12, rc = HSB_ERR_NONE with a SILENTLY partially-converged spectrum -- lambda = 4.68562332476e-12 against a true 4.732050808e-12, 0.98% wrong on that eigenvalue and 3.39% max relative error over the block (the filing's 0.98% figure reproduced exactly); at every c <= 1e-13, HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE with out_vals never written, i.e. an all-zero spectrum to a caller who zero-filled. Repairing :1117 alone removes both across all 18 decades tested; repairing :1103 alone changes neither.
defects.correct_threshold: r > 0 -- exactly what makes x/r and z/r fail, and nothing more. NOTE the filing's parenthetical "(equivalently >= DBL_MIN)" is WRONG: for 0 < r < DBL_MIN both |x| <= r and |z| <= r, so x/r and z/r are finite and in [-1,1] and a DBL_MIN floor still fabricates the identity. I could not construct a REACHABLE subnormal-r case -- the block invariant r >= |z| >= EPSILON_F64*(|diag[p_lo]|+|diag[p_lo+1]|) would need |diag[p_lo]|+|diag[p_lo+1]| <= 2.2e-296 -- so on every input I measured the two are indistinguishable; > 0 is still what the division requires and costs nothing. The relative alternative EPSILON_F64*(|diag[k]|+|diag[k+1]|), consistent with :1050/:1076, also repairs every case I measured, and at k = p_lo it is provably equivalent to r > 0 because its firing region is exactly the region the deflation test has already zeroed. Verified no regression: r > 0 and r > F64_TINY each leave all five suites at 776/233/359/416/1827, identical to shipped -- the filing's correct_threshold breaks no existing test.
defects.scale_test: REPLACE the filing's family; it cannot discriminate this site (measured above). Use eigen_qr(diag(1) (+) c*[[4,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,2]], n = 4) swept over c = 1e-1 .. 1e-320, asserting rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and, RELATIVELY, lambda_i/c == {4.732050807568877, 3, 1.2679491924311228} to 1e-10 with lambda_0 == 1. Three properties the filing's family lacks: (a) it ISOLATES -- the Wilkinson denom stays 1.618c so :1103 never fires, and mutation-proven, repairing :1103 alone leaves the sweep failing while repairing :1117 alone passes it; (b) the assertion must be on lambda/c, not on absolute error -- an absolute tolerance scaled to the matrix norm silently accepts the c = 1e-12 case, which is the exact trap my own first comparison fell into and the reason this defect is invisible to a suite; (c) it BRACKETS every threshold a repair might plausibly choose, each failing at its own c and separating from the correct one: 1e-6 fails below ~1e-6, EPSILON_F64 = 1e-12 below 1e-12, 1e-14 below ~1e-14, DBL_EPSILON = 2.2e-16 below ~1e-16, while r > 0, r > DBL_MIN and the relative EPSILON_F64*(|d_k|+|d_k+1|) all pass the full sweep. Pair it with the PURE-UNITS CONTROL that must stay green -- c*[[4,1,2],[1,3,0],[2,0,6]] over c = 10^-308..10^+300 -- which is what proves the failure is the deflated block's scale and the convergence tail, not the input's units, and which stops the next reader re-deriving the balancing at :1243 for themselves.

defects.guarded_quantity: vhv = v^H v after the phase shift = 2*||x||*(||x||+|x1|), where x is column k below the diagonal OF THE INTERNALLY BALANCED matrix (out_R holds A/sc, sc = _lp_pow2_floor(_lp_cmat_max_abs(A)), :1352). So it is NOT a caller-units length-squared: it is degree 2 in the DIMENSIONLESS ratio ||x||/||A||_max, and degree 0 in the caller's units.
defects.protects: two_over_vhv = f64_div(F64_TWO, vhv) at :1450, used by both reflector application loops.
defects.why: Two corrections to the filing, both measured, neither of which saves the guard. (1) The 'different units' half of the class is REFUTED: cqr_decompose balances on the way in and un-balances R at the end, so vhv is unit-invariant. The identical failing fixture (grading c = 3e-7) rescaled uniformly by s = 1e-100, 1e-8, 1, 1e8, 1e100 produces bit-identical output (all correct), and the shipped `cqr @1e200` test in tests/hisab.tcyr:2152 is that same control, passing. The guarded quantity is a dimensionless ratio, so an absolute constant is legitimate IN KIND. (2) It is the wrong absolute constant, and the evidence is the exponent, not the units: :1424 tests the degree-1 ratio ||x||/||A|| against EPSILON_F64 and :1449 tests the degree-2 ratio against the SAME constant 25 lines later, so the effective cutoff on the ratio is sqrt(EPSILON_F64/31.38) = 1.785e-7 instead of 1e-12 -- 5.6 decades coarser than its own sibling, on a column that is perfectly representable and 9 decades above round-off. Measured onset (sub-decade scan, c = k*1e-8, k = 10..20): correct at k >= 18, fabricated at k <= 17, i.e. the crossing sits at 1.78e-7, exactly where vhv = 31.38c^2 crosses 1e-12 and nowhere near :1424's own crossing at c = 3.0e-13. This is the identical class cx_div was repaired for in 2.6.14 (complex.cyr:57-62 names it and the effective 1e-6 cutoff it produced); cx_div at this very call site is now correct (it compares |z|^2 against EPSILON_F64^2 and is consistent with the :1429 gate, so it cannot confound the attribution). vhv >= 2*||x||^2 > 2e-24 whenever :1424 passed, so the guard protects no division: 2/vhv <= 1e24, finite, and the NaN/Inf paths behave identically under any threshold (f64_gt is false for NaN either way; 2/Inf = 0 is a no-op reflector).
defects.fabricates: rc = HSB_ERR_NONE with the reflector skipped outright. TWO modes, the second missed by the filing. (a) R not upper triangular: measured on diag(1) (+) c*[[1+i,2],[3,4-i]], |R[2][1]|/c = 3.000000000 (the untouched input entry) and |R[1][1]|/c = 1.414213562 (|x1|, not ||x|| = 3.316624790) for every c <= 1.7e-7, with Q the identity on that column. (b) WORSE, and invisible to the filing's decade grid: when reflector k is skipped but reflector k+1 is applied, the R-update loop starts at j = k+1 while the Q-update loop runs over all m columns, so column k of R is never reflected and the returned pair is NOT A FACTORIZATION -- Q*R != A with rc = 0. Measured on the ungraded fixture at c = 1.3e-7 .. 1.7e-7 (the window between the two reflectors' onsets, 1.213e-7 .. 1.785e-7, only 0.17 decades wide, which the filing's 1e-6/1e-7 grid steps over): max|Q*R - A| = 6c, up to 1.02e-6 ABSOLUTE against ||A||_max = 1, i.e. 4.6e9 * DBL_EPSILON.
defects.correct_threshold: vhv > 0. DBL_MIN and EPSILON_F64^2 are equally correct and BEHAVIOURALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE from it here -- both were built and swept and their output is byte-identical (diff -q), necessarily, because :1424 forces vhv > 2e-24 at every reachable evaluation. Measured with `vhv > F64_TINY` installed (mutant grep-proven at :1449): six decades, c = 1e-7 .. 1e-12, flip from fabricated to correct (|R21|/c = 0, |R11|/c = 3.316624790), and all five suites stay green -- hisab 416, foundation 359, modules 1827, edge_cases 233, abuse 776, 0 failed, identical to the shipped control -- so no existing test pins the current behaviour. Two riders. (i) Better than re-thresholding: decide reflect/skip ONCE, at :1424, since vhv <= 0 is unreachable there; a skip that happens between the two gates is what produces the Q*R != A mode. (ii) Repairing :1449 alone leaves the same class alive one guard over -- :1424's own absolute 1e-12 on the degree-1 ratio (crossing c = 3.0e-13) and :1429's phase fallback (`phase := 1` when |x1| <= EPSILON_F64, crossing c = 7.07e-13), the latter building a reflector that does not zero the subdiagonal at all.
defects.scale_test: The filing's sweep must be REPLACED, not floored differently: measured, `vhv > DBL_MIN` makes it pass c = 1e-1..1e-12 and still FAIL 1e-13..1e-150 (137 of its 150 assertions), because below 7.07e-13 the :1429 phase fallback fabricates on its own (|R21|/c = 0.694987437, |R11|/c = 3.242991283, |Q*R - A| = 1.29c) and below 3.0e-13 :1424 skips -- repairing :1424 too (measured) does not rescue it. As written it would read as "the repair did not work". Use instead: (1) CONTROL, to prove the fixture varies the right thing -- the same matrix scaled uniformly by s = 1e-100, 1e-8, 1e8, 1e100 must give IDENTICAL results, because the internal balancing makes vhv unit-invariant; the varying parameter is the GRADING ratio, not units. (2) FIXTURE A(c,K) = diag(1) (+) [[c(1+i), 2c],[3c, K*c*(4-i)]] with K = 1e6, which spreads the two reflectors' onsets apart so the Q*R != A window is six decades wide instead of 0.17. One assertion per decade, c = 1e-1 down to 1e-12 (floor at 1e-12: below 7.07e-13 no repair of :1449 can pass), plus sub-decade points {1,2,5}x10^-e and the explicit 1.3e-7 .. 1.7e-7 band on the K = 1 fixture. Three assertions per point: (i) ||Q*R - A||_max <= 1e-13 * ||A||_max -- norm-relative and NOT vacuous, it fails on shipped code at six decades with residual 6e-7 down to 6e-12; (ii) |R[2][1]| <= 1e-10 * c; (iii) |R[1][1]|/c == 3.3166247903554 to 1e-9 relative, which is what discriminates the three states from each other: correct 3.316624790, reflector skipped 1.414213562, phase fallback 3.242991283. Brackets crossed: 1.785e-7 (the shipped onset, sqrt(EPSILON_F64/31.38)), 8.4e-9 (DBL_EPSILON on vhv), 1.5e-8 (sqrt DBL_EPSILON), 3.0e-13 and 7.07e-13 (the two sibling guards, which the test must ATTRIBUTE rather than trip). It deliberately does NOT try to separate DBL_MIN from EPSILON_F64^2 from 0 -- measured byte-identical, and provably so given :1424.

defects.fn: m3_inverse (inherited unguarded by m3_normal_matrix at src/mat3.cyr:186, `m3_transpose(m3_inverse(m))` — the only in-tree caller, verified by grep over src/ and tests/)
defects.guarded_quantity: |det(M)| for a general 3x3, computed by m3_determinant (src/mat3.cyr:110-118) as the full cofactor expansion over the raw entries. Dimensions are (entry)^3 — if entries carry length, det carries length^3. Unbounded and fully scale-covariant: under M -> s*M, det -> s^3*det. Nothing normalises it: m3_determinant reads m3_get directly, and m3_inverse's only caller (m3_normal_matrix) passes the caller's matrix through untouched. NOT dimensionless, NOT bounded, NOT a cosine/barycentric/[0,1] parameter — i.e. not the case error.cyr:41-44 reserves EPSILON_F64 for.
defects.protects: The division on the next line, src/mat3.cyr:124: `var inv_det = f64_div(F64_ONE, det);`. That is the only division in the function; the nine cofactor stores are multiplies by inv_det. No sqrt, no acos, no loop bound, no iteration — so it is a divide-by-zero guard, not a convergence tolerance (refutation avenue "convergence tolerance" checked and rejected: there is no loop and no residual anywhere in the function).
defects.why: A length^3 quantity compared against a dimensionless absolute 1e-12 (EPSILON_F64 = 0x3D719799812DEA11, decoded and confirmed = 1e-12, src/error.cyr:26), so the threshold moves by the CUBE of any unit change. REPRODUCED ON THE REAL TOOLCHAIN (cyrius 6.6.2), not argued: a probe over M_k = 2^k*I built in a scratch copy of the tree returns the true inverse at k = -13 (det = 2^-39 = 1.82e-12) and the FABRICATED identity at k = -14 (det = 2^-42 = 2.27e-13) — the pass/fail boundary sits exactly where 2^(3k) crosses 1e-12, which is the signature of the class. Over the full sweep k in [-341,+341], 328 of 683 samples are wrong, every one returning I. Condition number of every one of them is exactly 1, so the guard is measuring MAGNITUDE, not singularity. What actually makes line 124 fail is |det| < ~1/DBL_MAX = 2^-1024 = 5.5627e-309, i.e. k <= -342 — 296 orders of magnitude below where the guard fires. ALL FIVE REFUTATION AVENUES WERE TESTED AND FAILED: (1) not dimensionless/bounded — it is a raw degree-3 cofactor expansion; (2) no caller normalises — m3_normal_matrix is the sole in-tree caller and does nothing to the operand, and the probe confirms the fabrication propagates through it (m3_normal_matrix(2^-20*I) returned 1.0 where 2^20 is correct: the identity is a fixed point of transposition); (3) not a convergence tolerance — single division, no loop; (4) NO EXISTING TEST CHANGES BEHAVIOUR — checked by running, not assuming: with the guard changed to F64_TINY, all five suites pass, 416+359+1827+233+776 = 3611 assertions, 0 failures. The three test sites that reach the guard (abuse.tcyr:1469-1470 via m3_new(), foundation.tcyr:1105 via a 4x4 read as a 3x3) all have det EXACTLY +0, which is still below DBL_MIN, so the documented identity-on-singular contract is preserved verbatim; the one invertible fixture (modules.tcyr:5881-5885) has det = 8; (5) the scale_test DOES discriminate — every candidate threshold's first-failing k was computed and each is distinct and inside the swept range. ⚠ THE SWEEP ALSO FOUND A SECOND, SEPARATE FABRICATION AT THE OTHER END that no threshold repair can touch: at k >= +342 the DETERMINANT ITSELF overflows to +Inf, |Inf| < eps is false so the guard does not fire, inv_det = 1/Inf = +0, and m3_inverse returns the ZERO matrix for a matrix whose true inverse 2^-342*I is exactly representable (measured: got 0, expected 2^-342). Related: the same overflow makes the exactly-singular fixture's det NaN at k = +341, and the guard does not fire on NaN either. File separately; the sweep must exclude it or it will fail against a correctly-repaired threshold and look like a regression.
defects.fabricates: m3_identity() — a full-rank, orthogonal, unit-determinant matrix in the slot where the inverse belongs. m3_inverse returns a bare pointer with no rc channel, so the caller cannot distinguish "here is your inverse" from "I refused"; nothing returned is NaN or Inf or otherwise self-announcing. Measured propagation: the identity is a fixed point of transposition, so m3_normal_matrix returns it unchanged — a small-scale model matrix silently yields an identity normal matrix, and unrotated normals look plausible rather than broken. For the 1e-5 (metres->micrometres) case the answer is wrong by 1e5 on every diagonal entry. Companion fabrication at the opposite extreme (separate defect, det overflow rather than threshold): the ZERO matrix, measured at k >= +342.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308) — already extracted in this tree as the shared constant for exactly this rule, and mat3.cyr can name it directly (same-bundle global; no per-module alias needed, unlike geo/autodiff/quat which aliased it before extraction). Measured kill matrix over the 683-sample sweep, one build per candidate on cyrius 6.6.2: EPSILON_F64 -> 328 wrong; F64_TINY -> 1 wrong; guard-only-exact-zero (0x1) -> 0 wrong. ⚠ SHARPENED BY MEASUREMENT: F64_TINY is not exactly "what makes the division fail" — it over-refuses by a factor of 4 in det (2^(2/3) = 1.587x in uniform entry scale). The true overflow bound is |det| < ~1/DBL_MAX = 2^-1024; at k = -341 det = 2^-1023 is subnormal but 1/det = 2^1023 is finite and the exact inverse 2^341*I is representable, and the F64_TINY repair fabricates the identity there (measured: the single residual failure). This also means src/error.cyr:29's own header line — "The smallest MAGNITUDE whose reciprocal is still finite: DBL_MIN" — is off by a factor of 4; the smallest such magnitude is ~2^-1024. Recommendation: ship F64_TINY for consistency with the extracted constant and the 22 existing use sites, and make the test STATE the k = -341 over-refusal as accepted rather than quietly stopping the sweep above it (a sweep whose floor is chosen to avoid the residual is the same shortcut 2.14.0 recorded against the 10-decade geo sweep). A genuine SINGULARITY report is a separate concern: it must be relative and degree-3 to be scale-free — |det| < rel_tol * ||c0||*||c1||*||c2|| (Hadamard bound, also length^3, so the ratio is dimensionless) — and delivered on an rc out-parameter, never by returning a plausible matrix. That is an API change and should be filed separately from the threshold repair.
defects.scale_test: DEGREE -1 HOMOGENEITY OF THE INVERSE, swept over 683 powers of two, written in the house idiom already in tests/modules.tcyr:10291 (`_p2(e) = (1023 + e) << 52`; bit-exact `!=` compares on raw f64 bit patterns, NEVER through f64_to, which truncates — 2.13.0). ALL NUMBERS BELOW ARE MEASURED ON cyrius 6.6.2, not derived on paper. (A) PRIMARY SWEEP: for k in [-341, +341], M_k = 2^k*I. Entries, det = 2^(3k) and the true inverse 2^-k*I are all exactly representable, so the compare is legitimately bit-exact: assert m3_get(inv,0,0) == _p2(-k) and every off-diagonal == +0. Verified exact for all 683 samples with the guard disabled. Truth: the division only overflows at k <= -342, so a mathematically exact guard refuses nothing in the swept range. MEASURED RESULTS: shipped EPSILON_F64 fails 328 of 683 (every k <= -14, all returning I); F64_TINY fails exactly ONE (k = -341, det = 2^-1023 subnormal) — assert that sample explicitly as the accepted over-refusal with a comment naming it, so a future tightening to 1/DBL_MAX is not mistaken for a regression and the sweep is not vacuous at its own floor. DISCRIMINATION (each candidate's first failing k, all distinct, all inside the range): 1e-4 (eps^(1/3)) k<=-5; 1e-9 k<=-10; shipped 1e-12 k<=-14 (confirmed against the real binary at the k=-13/-14 pair); 1e-15 k<=-17; DBL_EPSILON k<=-18; 1e-36 k<=-40; DBL_MIN k<=-341; 1/DBL_MAX k<=-342. ⚠ CORRECTED UPPER BOUND: stop the truth assertion at k = +341. At k >= +342 the determinant itself overflows to +Inf and m3_inverse returns the ZERO matrix (measured) — a SEPARATE defect the threshold cannot repair, so including it makes the sweep fail against correct code. Add it as its own named assertion documenting current behaviour, not as part of clause (A). (B) ANTI-MUTANT (so that DELETING the guard does not pass): M = 2^k * [[1,2,3],[2,4,6],[7,8,9]], row 2 = 2*row 1. ⚠ CORRECTED RANGE: k in [-341, +340], not [-341,+341] — measured, det is bit-exactly +0 across that range but is NaN at k = +341 (the triple product overflows, Inf - Inf), and f64_lt(f64_abs(NaN), t) is false for every t, so the "must be refused" assertion fails against correct code at +341. Within [-341,+340] all three candidate guards refuse correctly (verified: 0 bad), while a deleted guard yields 1/0 = +Inf and NaN entries. (C) NON-UNIFORM, ILL-CONDITIONED BUT INVERTIBLE, pinning the shipped threshold from BOTH sides on a matrix that is not a multiple of I: M = 2^k * [[1,1,0],[0,2^-27,0],[0,0,1]], det = 2^(3k-27). Confirmed numerically: k = -5 gives det = 2.2737e-13, just BELOW 1e-12; k = -4 gives 1.8190e-12, just ABOVE — two adjacent samples straddling the shipped constant. Assert the relative residual ||M*inv(M) - I||_F / (||M||_F * ||inv(M)||_F) <= 8*DBL_EPSILON; the fabricated identity fails it by O(1) at k = -5 and passes at k = -4. (D) THE ONE-LINE UNIT-CHANGE ASSERTION FOR THE CHANGELOG: m3_inverse(s*M) == (1/s)*m3_inverse(M) elementwise and bit-exactly for s = 2^20 and s = 2^-20 over a handful of well-conditioned M whose scaled det stays inside [2^-900, 2^900] (power-of-two rescaling commutes exactly with rounding, so bit-exactness is legitimate only while nothing over/underflows — state that precondition). Today the micrometre side returns the identity and the metre side the true inverse, so a change of units alone violates the identity that defines the operation. (E) WRAPPER: run (A) and (D) against m3_normal_matrix(M_k) too — truth 2^-k*I for symmetric M_k. Not optional: the fabrication is a fixed point of transposition, measured to survive the wrapper unchanged, so a test that only exercises m3_inverse leaves the reachable path unproven.

defects.guarded_quantity: |pw| — the absolute value of the homogeneous w component of M·(v,1). Confirmed against the source: m4_mul_vec4 computes r = Σ_k v[k]·col_k with column k at m+32k, so pw = x·c0w + y·c1w + z·c2w + 1·c3w. DIMENSIONS: not dimensionless, not bounded. For an affine M (m4_from_srt:305 and m4_look_at_rh:365 both set [3][3]=F64_ONE, [i][3]=0) it is exactly 1.0 and the guard never fires. For a perspective M it is -z_eye, a LENGTH in the caller's units: m4_perspective_rh:335 sets m4_set(m,2,3,-1) and never writes [3][3], leaving it 0; m4_perspective_reverse_z:347-348 has col2=(0,0,0,-1) and col3=(0,0,near,0), also [3][3]=0. For a general 4x4 it is an arbitrary linear form in the input coordinates. Homogeneous coordinates are additionally defined only up to overall scale, so pw has no intrinsic magnitude at all — (kx,ky,kz,kw) denotes the same point as (x,y,z,w) for every k != 0.

defects.why:
UPHELD. All five refutation routes were attempted against the real source and all five died; three died on measurement rather than on reading.

(1) DIMENSIONLESS/BOUNDED — no. `df` is a raw `fnptr` invoked via `fncall1`; nothing in the function touches its magnitude before comparing it.

(2) CALLER NORMALISES — dead by grep, not assumption: `grep -rn "num_newton(" src/` returns ZERO internal callers. It is a pure public entry point (roadmap.md:695 lists it in the public API table). Every argument, including the derivative callback, is the caller's.

(3) IT IS REALLY A CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE — refuted by the structure above; `tol` is a distinct parameter tested at :44 and the two error codes are distinct.

(4) THE REPAIR BREAKS AN EXISTING TEST — checked, does not. All 8 `num_newton` call sites in tests/ enumerated and every fixture body read: modules.tcyr:95-102 (`_tn_df`=2x from x0=1, `_tn_cube_df`=3x^2 from x0=3, `_tn_lin_df`=1, `_tn_sin_df`=cos from x0=0.5 converging to 0 so |cos|→1), hisab.tcyr:565 (`_nr_df`=2x), examples/basic_math.cyr:23 (same). Minimum |f'| over every run is O(1), far above BOTH thresholds — unchanged. The only two fixtures that reach the guard return a LITERAL zero (edge_cases.tcyr:44 `_ec_zero_df(x){return 0;}`, abuse.tcyr:197 `_ab_dg_dy(t,y){return 0;}` — note it is a 2-param function called through `fncall1`, still returns 0), and `f64_abs(0.0) < DBL_MIN` is true, so both keep returning HSB_ERR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO. Zero shipped assertions change; the repair is strictly a narrowing.

(5) THE SCALE TEST DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — I modelled the loop body verbatim in IEEE double and measured. It discriminates exactly as claimed: 6 of 15 k values flip (k <= 1e-13, split at 2k < 1e-12, since min|f'| over the run is 2k at x0=1), and under DBL_MIN all 15 return HSB_ERR_NONE with the BIT-IDENTICAL root 0x3ff6a09e667f57db (1.4142135623746899) at iteration 4. My a-priori objection to leg (b) — that k = 1e300/1e-305 are not powers of two so the scaling rounds, and that at k=1e-305 the terminating residual is SUBNORMAL (~4.5e-317, with tol_k = 1e-315 itself subnormal) — was tested and is refuted: per-iterate step error stays ~6 orders below ulp(x4), so bit-identity is structural, not luck.

The two scaling arguments themselves hold as stated: range scaling f -> k*f leaves every Newton iterate bit-identical (measured, above) while moving |f'| by k; domain scaling u = x/s moves |f'| by s with no change to the problem (measured, 7 values of s, s*root bit-identical). So "the derivative is too small" is not a scale-free statement and 1e-12 is a scale chosen for a quantity that has none — 2.10.2's definition of the defect, and the thirty-third instance of the class recorded at complex.cyr:58.

SECONDARY (unchanged): what actually makes the DIVISION fail is a zero or subnormal denominator, nothing more. Modelled at k=1e-13: fx=-1e-13, dfx=2e-13, fx/dfx=-0.5, an ordinary finite division that this guard refuses.

CORROBORATION, not evidence: docs/audit/2026-09-09-roadmap-verification.md:491 already lists `num_newton` in the open epsilon tier ("num_newton/num_tridiag_solve -> early exit"), and docs/audit/2026-08-11-v2.11.0-full.md:54 files it as "DIVISION_BY_ZERO on well-conditioned input". It is scheduled, not repaired.
defects.fabricates: none - it reports an error. Verified by reading :51: the branch is a bare `return HSB_ERR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO;` with no `store64`, so `*out` is left UNWRITTEN (it is a raw `alloc(8)` at every call site — uninitialised, not zeroed). A caller that checks rc gets a false "your derivative is zero" on a well-conditioned problem; a caller that ignores rc reads heap garbage. FALSE NEGATIVE, not the fabricate-a-plausible-answer shape of eigen_qr / m3_inverse / cx_div — less dangerous than those, still wrong: the function refuses a problem whose Newton step is exact. Note the repair does not introduce a fabrication either: at the genuinely pathological end the repaired guard yields HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE instead (measured), never a written wrong root.
defects.correct_threshold:
`F64_TINY` (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308) — the constant this repo extracted in 2.10.2 for exactly this rule, currently aliased by geo (15 uses), autodiff (4) and quat (3) and used ZERO times in num.cyr. Guard: `if (f64_lt(f64_abs(dfx), F64_TINY) == 1)`. The smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is still finite: exactly what makes the division fail, and nothing more.

MEASURED PROPERTIES OF THE REPAIR (all four verbatim-loop simulations):
- Keeps abuse.tcyr:2391 and edge_cases.tcyr:381 green (both fixtures return literal 0.0; abs(0.0) < DBL_MIN).
- Also fires on a SUBNORMAL denominator, which is intended and is what separates it from "no guard": at x0 = 1e-308, dfx = 2e-308 < DBL_MIN -> DIV0; at x0 = 5e-324 (min subnormal), dfx = 1e-323 -> DIV0. With the guard DELETED both of those spin to NO_CONVERGENCE instead, so DBL_MIN is behaviourally distinct from deletion on its own fixture, without leaning on abuse.tcyr.
- Do NOT substitute the "relative" alternative `|dfx| < |fx|/DBL_MAX`. It is not a stricter version of DBL_MIN, it is LOOSER: with |fx| = 2 it evaluates to 1.1e-308, below DBL_MIN, so it admits subnormal denominators DBL_MIN rejects (x0 = 1e-308 then takes a finite -1e308 step and reaches NO_CONVERGENCE by callback overflow). It also costs a division to compute a division guard. Prefer the constant the project already settled on.
- And do not "fix" it by making the threshold relative to |fx| with a chosen epsilon (`|dfx| < |fx|*1e-12`): that is scale-free and therefore survives the ENTIRE k sweep, yet still refuses a convergent unscaled problem — see leg (d), which exists to kill it.

FIVE LEGS. Legs (a)-(c) are the claim's, confirmed by measurement; (d) and (e) are added because (a)-(c) leave a wrong repair alive. All numbers below are from a verbatim transcription of :39-56 in IEEE double, not estimated.

LEG (a) — RANGE COVARIANCE. f_k(x) = k*(x*x - 2), df_k(x) = k*(2x), x0 = 1.0, max_iter = 100, tol_k = k*1e-10 (tol carries the units of f). LEG (b) — BIT-EXACT INVARIANCE. Assert load64(out) is bit-identical across all 15 k, comparing raw patterns (never through f64_to, which truncates — 2.13.0). MEASURED under DBL_MIN: one distinct pattern, 0x3ff6a09e667f57db, at iteration 4 for all 15.

(5) The scale_test DOES discriminate — measured below. ⛔ The absolute 1e-12 gets both directions wrong, and the second direction is now measured too: a denom of 2^-39 = 1.8e-12 PASSES the shipped guard, c'[i] = 2^1000/2^-39 overflows to +Inf, and the function returns rc = HSB_ERR_NONE with NaN (0xFFF8000000000000) in out[0] and out[1]. It is not a stability check by any reading; the CORRECT_TOLERANCE reading is refuted by measurement, not only by argument. ⚠ Prior art: docs/audit/2026-08-11-v2.11.0-full.md:54 already lists `num_newton` / `num_tridiag_solve` — "DIVISION_BY_ZERO on well-conditioned input | pivot 1e-12" — as an instance of the 24-member class. This is a re-confirmation of an open, never-acted-on finding, and docs/audit/2026-09-09-roadmap-verification.md:488 records that no commit in 2.11.3/2.11.4/2.11.5 touched an EPSILON_F64 occurrence.

A FALSE REJECTION with an intact error channel, not the fabricate-a-plausible-answer class — at denom = 1.25*2^-45 the pivot is not zero. ⚠ MEASURED COMPANION, attributable to the same wrong threshold but to its non-firing half: when the guard passes a denom whose quotient overflows (denom = 2^-39, c = 2^1000) the function DOES fabricate — rc = HSB_ERR_NONE with NaN in out. That is the guard failing to protect the division it exists for, so the repair must be validated with a no-NaN assertion on `out`, not only with a return code.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 = DBL_MIN = 2.2250738585072014e-308) for the divide guard — exactly what makes f64_div undefined, per 2.10.2, and exactly what error.cyr:40-44's own comment already prescribes ("the right threshold when the guard protects a DIVISION and the only thing that can actually fail is a zero (or subnormal) denominator"; EPSILON_F64 is reserved there for "a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity", which denom is not). defects.scale_test:
THREE PARTS, ALL EXECUTED AGAINST THE RUNNING CODE ON cyrius 6.6.2; results quoted are measured, not predicted.

(A) MUTATION-FREE WITNESS — the primary assertion, needs NO isolation, so it cannot be dismissed as an artefact of the harness. n = 2, a = c = [-s], b = [s, (1+2^-20)*s], d = [0, 2^-20*s], exact solution x = (1,1), condition number ~2^21. Because b[0] = s while denom[1] = 2^-20*s, guard :1137 is silent over a 20-binade window that :1157 alone occupies. Assert rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and out[0] == out[1] == 0x3FF0000000000000 BIT-EXACTLY at k = 0, -10, -20, -30. MEASURED on the shipped tree: k = 0 -> rc 0, (1,1); k = -10 -> rc 0, (1,1); k = -20 -> rc -4, out untouched; k = -30 -> rc -4, out untouched. With :1157 alone at F64_TINY: all four -> rc 0, bit-exact (1,1). This single fixture reproduces AND attributes the defect with one mutated line.

(B) DEEP SCALE COVARIANCE, BIT-EXACT, WITH PER-GUARD ISOLATION — for bracketing. Fixture n = 4, a = c = [-1,-1,-1], b = [2,2,2,2], d = [0,0,0,5], x = (1,2,3,4), scaled by s = 2^k; assert rc == HSB_ERR_NONE and all four out words BIT-IDENTICAL to k = 0 (0x3FEFFFFFFFFFFFFE, 0x3FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE, 0x4007FFFFFFFFFFFF, 0x4010000000000000) for k in {+1000, +500, +100, +40, 0, -45, -60, -110, -260, -510, -1000, -1015, -1020, -1021, -1022}. ⚠ ISOLATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS VERIFIED: b[0] = 2*2^k trips :1137 at k <= -41, so on the shipped tree the whole low half fails for the WRONG reason — measured, repairing :1157 alone leaves every one of those rows at -4. MEASURED in that configuration: shipped EPSILON_F64 gives rc 0 for k >= 0 and rc -4 for every k from -45 to -1022; F64_TINY gives rc 0 and bit-identical output at all fifteen rungs. Check the probe before believing the probe.

(C) FIRING ASSERTION, verified to kill a deletion mutant. a = c = [-s,-s,-s], b = [s, s, 2s, 2s], d = [s,s,s,s]: c'[0] = -1 exactly and denom[1] = s - s = EXACTLY 0 at every scale, with a perfectly healthy b[0] = s. Assert HSB_ERR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO and `out` untouched at k in {+1000, +100, 0, -45, -110, -510, -1000, -1022} (run under the same isolation, since b[0] scales too and :1137 would otherwise answer with the same code). MEASURED under the F64_TINY repair: -4 at all eight rungs, out untouched. MEASURED with the guard DELETED: rc 0 and out = 0xFFF8000000000000 (NaN) at all eight — mutant killed. ⛔ AND THE EXISTING SUITE DOES NOT: with :1157 deleted outright, all five suites still pass 416/359/1818/233/776, 0 failed. Nothing in 3602 assertions tests this guard in either direction today.

(D) NO-FABRICATION ASSERTION, from the measured second failure mode: n = 3, a = [-1,-1], b = [1, 1+2^-39, 1], c = [-1, 2^1000], d = [1,1,1]. denom[1] = 2^-39 = 1.8e-12 passes BOTH the shipped 1e-12 and F64_TINY; measured result on the shipped tree is rc = HSB_ERR_NONE with out[0] = out[1] = NaN. This is the assertion that forces the relative HSB_ERR_SINGULAR_PIVOT test to be written rather than assumed, and it fails identically before and after the threshold change — proving the absolute epsilon never bought the protection it is credited with.

defects.guarded_quantity: f64_sub(tf, t) — the remaining span of the INDEPENDENT VARIABLE between the current step time and the requested final time. Dimensions: time^1, degree 1, entirely caller-scaled (t0/tf/dt0 are raw caller arguments; the function nondimensionalises nothing). Seconds→milliseconds multiplies it by 1000. CONFIRMED: it is neither dimensionless nor bounded, so it is outside the class error.cyr's own F64_TINY comment reserves EPSILON_F64 for ("a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity — a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]"). ode.cyr's own Newton solvers already use the relative form EPSILON_F64*(1+|z|) at lines 346/395/500; line 251 is the module's lone absolute comparison against a caller-scaled quantity.
defects.protects: Not a division — it is the loop's arrival test, above `if (f64_gt(t, tf))`. CORRECTED from the filing: the stated mechanism (the clamped final step h = tf - t falling below ulp(t)) is NOT reachable. When t and tf are same-sign and within a factor of 2 — always true at the end of a run — Sterbenz makes `tf - t` exact and `t + (tf - t)` is then exactly tf, a representable value, so the clamped step always lands on tf. Measured: the `t + h == t` condition never fired on ANY row of either sweep for a legitimate integration. The real non-advancement path is the rejection-driven shrink (dt0 = 0, tol = 0 in abuse.tcyr), and this guard never sees it — `tf - t` is O(1) there and the 100000-step budget is what stops the spin. So the guard protects nothing that would otherwise fail; it only decides when to stop, and an absolute constant makes that decision wrong at small time scales.
defects.why: DEFECT CONFIRMED at small scale, REFUTED at large epoch. Reproduced on the real code (cycc 6.6.2, y' = y/T on [0,T], y0 = 1, dt0 = T/10, tol = 1e-8; exact y(T) = e for every T): T = 1e6/1e3/1/1e-3/1e-6/1e-9 all give n = 12, y_end = 2.718281834, rc = 0 — then T = 1e-11 gives n = 11, y_end = 2.634101143; T = 1e-12 gives n = 2, y_end = 1.105170918; T = 1e-13 through 1e-300 give n = 1, y_end = 1.000000000 — every one with rc = HSB_ERR_NONE. The crossover sits exactly on EPSILON_F64, and it is a unit choice, not a physics choice, that crosses it. REFUTED HALF: the filing's large-epoch evidence does not exist. At t0 = 1e15 the shipped code returns n = 9, y_end = 2.171795922, span = 1.0 exactly (it DOES reach tf), rc = 0 — no NaN, no 11741 samples; and an absolute-DBL_MIN mutant produces BYTE-IDENTICAL sweep-B output, so that error is ambient epoch resolution (dt0 = 0.1 < ulp(1e15) = 0.125, so t advances in 0.125 quanta while the integrator steps with h = 0.1) and is not attributable to this threshold. At t0 >= 1e16, tf = t0 + 1 rounds to t0 (measured: both 0x4341c37937e08000), so returning 1 sample is CORRECT for every candidate threshold including `tf - t <= 0`. The guard is too LARGE at small scale only. Refutation avenues checked and closed by measurement, not assumption: the four abuse.tcyr trajectory assertions all still pass under the repair, and hisab/abuse/modules re-run with the repaired module give 416/776/1827 passed, 0 failed — identical to the shipped module.
defects.fabricates: HSB_ERR_NONE (rc = 0) plus a plausible short trajectory. Measured, tol = 1e-8, dt0 = T/10: T <= 1e-13 → n = 1, out_ys holds only y0, y_end = 1.000000000 where the answer is e — a completely un-integrated trajectory reported as success; T = 1e-12 → n = 2, y_end = 1.105170918, 59% short; T = 1e-11 → n = 11, y_end = 2.634101143, still 3% off. The filing's "y_end = NaN after 11741 duplicate-t samples at t0 = 1e15" is NOT reproducible and is struck — that row returns n = 9, y_end = 2.171795922, and is threshold-independent.
defects.correct_threshold: Two tests, neither needing a scale chosen for it. (1) Arrival: `f64_le(f64_sub(tf, t), 0)` — replaces both this guard and the `f64_gt(t, tf)` line below it; preserves abuse.tcyr's "tf < t0 returns immediately" (measured rc = 0, n = 1). (2) Non-advancement, immediately after the overshoot clamp: `if (f64_eq(f64_add(t, h), t) == 1) { return HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE; }` — the literal condition that makes the loop fail, scale-free by construction, no constant. It must NOT return HSB_ERR_NONE; the contract already declares HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE. STRUCK from the filing: the "equivalent closed-form relative bound" `tf - t <= |t|*DBL_EPSILON` is NOT equivalent and is itself a fabricating guard — measured at t0 = 1e15 it stops at span 0.875 (0.125 short of tf) with y_end = 1.972024457 vs e and rc = 0, strictly worse than shipped. Measured effect of the pair: sweep A correct (n = 12, y_end = 2.718281834) at every T from 1e6 to 1e-300; sweep B unchanged from shipped at every t0; the dt0 = 0 abuse case now returns rc = -8 at n = 1 instead of after 100001 wasted pushes (both existing assertions still pass); hostile inputs (tf/t0/dt0/tol = NaN, ±inf) return the same rc as shipped, several of them sooner; all three ode-including suites 0 failed.
defects.scale_test: Sweep B is DROPPED as a discriminator — measured, it kills nothing: shipped and absolute-DBL_MIN give byte-identical output on every row. Two sweeps replace it. SWEEP A (scale invariance, e-oracle): y' = y/T on [0, T], y0 = 1, dt0 = T/10, tol = 1e-8, exact y_end = e for every T. T = 10^k for k in {6, 3, 0, -3, -6, -9, -11, -12, -13, -15, -20, -30, -60, -150, -300}. Assert rc == HSB_ERR_NONE implies vec_len(out_ts) >= 3 AND |y_end - e| <= 1e-6*e. STOP AT 1e-300: below it the ORACLE overflows, not the guard — y' = y/T needs 1/T, and at T ~ 1e-308 the stage coefficient _DP_A52 = -11.59 times 1e308 goes to -inf, so EVERY variant including the correct repair returns NaN (measured, n = 4, y_end = -nan, rc = 0). The filing's request to run this family to DBL_MIN would have produced a NaN misread as a guard kill. SWEEP A' (coverage; the sweep that actually kills absolute DBL_MIN, which sweep B claimed to and does not): y' = y, y0 = 1 — derivative bounded by e for ANY span, so nothing overflows — t0 = 0, tf = T, dt0 = T/10; assert `rc == HSB_ERR_NONE implies t_end == tf` bit-exactly. T = 1e0, 1e-12, 1e-20, 1e-300, and the bit patterns 0x0010000000000000 (DBL_MIN), 0x0008000000000000 (1.1e-308), 0x0000000000010000 (3.2e-319), 0x0000000000000010 (7.9e-323), 0x0000000000000001 (1 ulp). Do NOT build these with pow10 — ganita's pow underflows 1e-310 to exactly 0.0, which makes tf == t0 and every variant look correct. MEASURED MUTANT KILLS: shipped 1e-12 dies at A/T=1e-11 and A'/T=1e-12; absolute 2.2e-16 survives A to 1e-13, dies at A/T=1e-15 (n = 10, y = 2.391804783) and A/T<=1e-20; absolute DBL_MIN survives all of A and all of A' down to 1e-300, and dies at A'/T=DBL_MIN (n = 2, t_end != tf) and below; relative |t|*DBL_EPSILON passes A and A' but dies on the retained large-epoch CONTROL below; the `tf-t<=0` + `t+h==t` pair passes A and A' everywhere and at the 1-ulp span returns rc = HSB_ERR_NO_CONVERGENCE rather than a false success. CONTROLS that must not move: A/T=1 and A'/T=1 give n = 12, y_end = 2.718281834; and keep exactly two sweep-B rows as controls — y' = y on [t0, t0+1], t0 = 0 (n = 12, y_end = 2.718281834) and t0 = 1e15 (n = 9, y_end = 2.171795922, span = 1.0) — the second being the row that kills the relative-|t| candidate.

defects.guarded_quantity: `denom = f64_sub(b, a)` under `f64_abs` — the WIDTH of the caller's input interval, in the caller's own units (metres, seconds, kelvin, pixels). Dimensions: length^1 (or whatever unit the caller supplies), strictly LINEAR in the problem scale. Re-express the same problem in millimetres instead of metres and the quantity is multiplied by 1000. Not dimensionless, not bounded, not squared. Confirmed linear by measurement, not by argument: on the small side the shipped guard first fabricates at decade 13 (s = 1e-13, i.e. exactly one decade past the 1e-12 literal), and `hisab_remap`, whose interval is 10s rather than s, first fabricates exactly one decade later at 14 — the offset a linear quantity predicts.
defects.protects: The division on the next line, `f64_div(f64_sub(value, a), denom)`. Nothing else in the function can fail — there is no iteration, no sqrt, no acos domain, no convergence criterion. `hisab_lerp` above it and `hisab_remap` below it are pure add/mul/forwarding.
defects.why:
REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FIVE CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT ON THIS TREE (probes under scratchpad/eps/refute, built against src/transforms.cyr at HEAD, cyrius 6.6.2).

(1) DIMENSIONLESS/BOUNDED? No. The RESULT is a dimensionless fraction of the interval, so the same geometry must give the same number in any units — and it does not. Measured bit-exactly: hisab_inverse_lerp(0, s, s/2) == 0.5 for s = 1e0 through 1e-12 and flips to 0.0 at s = 1e-13. Identical code with the guard at F64_TINY stays bit-exact 0.5 through s = 1e-307. A guard that makes the same problem answer differently in different units is a statement about units, not arithmetic.

(2) CALLER NORMALISES? No. `grep -rn 'inverse_lerp\|hisab_remap' src/` returns exactly two lines tree-wide: the definition (transforms.cyr:119) and `hisab_remap` (transforms.cyr:126), which forwards `in_lo`/`in_hi` verbatim. It is a public entry point with no normalising wrapper anywhere in the 35 modules.

(3) CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE? No. Three lines, one division, no loop.

(4) WOULD F64_TINY BREAK AN EXISTING PASSING TEST? Checked, not assumed. There are exactly two test call sites tree-wide: tests/hisab.tcyr:296 `hisab_inverse_lerp(0, 10, 5)` and tests/foundation.tcyr:1088 `hisab_remap(5, 0, 10, 0, 100)`. Both re-run through an F64_TINY-guarded copy return bit-identical values (0.5 and 50). The degenerate case `hisab_inverse_lerp(3, 3, 7)` still returns 0 under F64_TINY (denom is exactly 0, which is < DBL_MIN), so the documented degenerate behaviour is preserved. Baseline is green for the comparison to mean anything: hisab 416/416, foundation 359/359.

(5) DOES THE SWEEP DISCRIMINATE? Yes, and the bracketing is now measured rather than argued. Every threshold a repair might plausibly choose dies strictly inside 0..307: 1e-9 at decade 10, 1e-15 at 16, DBL_EPSILON (2.22e-16) at 16, 1e-100 at 101, 1e-200 at 201, shipped 1e-12 at 13. A wrong-quantity mutant guarding the NUMERATOR instead of `denom` dies at 12. The correct repair passes all 308 decades and first fails at 308.

The original triage was right on every load-bearing point. What it did NOT know is in `correct_threshold` and `scale_test` below: the depth is confirmed (not merely derived), the a = 0 origin is FORCED rather than lazy, one whole class of repair is invisible to the covariance sweep and is killed only by the boundary probe, and the proposed large-side mirror kills nothing.
defects.fabricates: Exactly 0.0 (measured bit pattern 0, not merely "approximately zero"), and 0.0 is ALSO the legitimate answer for value == a, so the caller cannot distinguish the fabrication from a real result. There is no rc, no out-param, no sentinel — the function's only channel is the f64 it returns. `hisab_remap` (transforms.cyr:125) inherits it whole and silently returns `out_lo`: measured, hisab_remap(5s, 0, 10s, 0, 100) returns exactly 0 instead of 50 from s = 1e-14 downward. Both fabrications are silent and rc-less; nothing in either function can report.
defects.correct_threshold:
F64_TINY (src/error.cyr:45, `0x0010_0000_0000_0000` = DBL_MIN). geo.cyr:26, autodiff.cyr:17 and quat.cyr:12 already alias it for exactly this class of guard, so the repair adds no constant and needs no new entry in scripts/check-constants.sh.

⚠ SHARPENED — DBL_MIN is the right choice here for CONSISTENCY with the rule error.cyr:45 already settled, but it is NOT the unique arithmetic failure boundary, and the repair comment must not claim it is. Measured, three variants side by side over 340 decades: shipped 1e-12 is bit-exact through decade 12; F64_TINY through 307; a minimal `denom == 0`-only guard through 308. So DBL_MIN gives up exactly ONE decade (s = 1e-308) in which the division would still have returned a bit-exact 0.5 — a subnormal denominator divides fine. And in the other direction DBL_MIN does not buy what a careless reader assumes: it bounds the RECIPROCAL, not the quotient, so a large `value - a` over a denom just above DBL_MIN still overflows to ±Inf. The honest statement is "the smallest denominator magnitude this project guards divisions at, one decade conservative against the true limit", not "exactly what makes the division fail". Anything above DBL_MIN — 1e-12 included — is a scale chosen for the caller, which is the 2.10.2 rule's definition of the defect.
defects.scale_test:
SCALE COVARIANCE, depth 307, MEASURED not argued — plus one boundary probe that turns out to carry more weight than the 616 sweep assertions.

CORE SWEEP (small side, the only side that discriminates). For e in 0..307 with s = 10^-e by repeated f64_div by 10, assert BIT-EXACTLY (never through f64_to, never through LOOSE_TOL): hisab_inverse_lerp(0, s, s/2) == 0.5 and hisab_inverse_lerp(0, s, s) == 1.0. Assert the run counter == 308 (a sweep that silently stops running is indistinguishable from one that passes — the 2.10.2 lesson). Add the inheriting caller: hisab_remap(5s, 0, 10s, 0, 100) == 50 over the same 0..307. Measured baselines for the fixture comment: shipped first wrong at e=13 (remap e=14), F64_TINY-guarded first wrong at e=308 (remap e=309, one deeper because remap's interval is 10s), so 0..307 is the exact window in which the correct repair passes and every wrong threshold fails.

BRACKETING — MEASURED, EACH MUTANT RUN. 1e-9 dies at decade 10, 1e-15 at 16, DBL_EPSILON at 16, 1e-100 at 101, 1e-200 at 201, shipped 1e-12 at 13, a numerator-guarding wrong-quantity mutant at 12. All strictly inside 0..307; DBL_MIN itself sits at 308, one past the last asserted decade. This is the 2.11.1 lesson applied — a 12- or 20-decade sweep would leave the 1e-100 and 1e-200 mutants alive, the same way the quaternion sweep killed only 1 of 3. foundation.tcyr:1146 derives 154 for the QUADRATIC hvec3_angle case by this argument; linear means 308 here, and 308 is now confirmed by running it, not inferred.

⛔ THE COVARIANCE SWEEP KILLS EVERY ABSOLUTE MUTANT AND ZERO RELATIVE ONES — SO THE BOUNDARY PROBE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATION. Measured: a repair using a RELATIVE threshold, `|b-a| < EPSILON_F64 * max(|a|,|b|)`, survives all 308 decades of the sweep untouched (first-wrong: never), because with a = 0 the threshold is 1e-12*s and |denom| = s is never below it. It is killed only by the boundary probe, and only if that probe is asserted bit-exactly: with a = 0, b = DBL_MIN/1000 (subnormal), value = b/2, the relative repair returns 0.5 (0x3FE0000000000000) where F64_TINY returns 0. So assert BOTH sides of the boundary explicitly — hisab_inverse_lerp(a, a, v) == 0 for a truly zero denom, and hisab_inverse_lerp(0, sub, sub/2) == 0 for a subnormal denom below DBL_MIN. A covariance sweep proves the guard is silent where it should be; only these two prove it still EXISTS and sits where it is claimed to.

⚠ THE a = 0 ORIGIN IS FORCED, NOT LAZY — DO NOT "IMPROVE" IT WITH AN OFFSET FIXTURE. The obvious hardening (make a != 0 so the sweep proves the guard is on the DIFFERENCE rather than an endpoint) does not survive contact: a = s, b = 3s, value = 2s fails bit-exactly at decade 1 on the SHIPPED code AND on the correct F64_TINY code, because 3s and 2s each round independently. Even the power-of-two form a = s, b = s+s, value = s+s/2 fails at decade 1 on both — 1.5*s needs 54 mantissa bits. Only a = 0 keeps numerator and denominator exact at every scale (halving is exact, s/s is exact), which is precisely why the fixture must be written that way. Anyone who adds an offset variant will get a red suite and blame the repair.

⚠ THE PROPOSED LARGE-SIDE MIRROR KILLS NOTHING — TRIM IT OR LABEL IT DOCUMENTATION. Measured over e in 0..307 with s = 10^+e: both the shipped code and the F64_TINY repair are correct at every decade (first-wrong: never). It was proposed to catch "a two-sided mutant", but the only realistic sibling — a reversed comparison, f64_gt instead of f64_lt — already dies on the small side at decade 0. Roughly 300 assertions with no discriminating power over the small side; keep them only as an explicit record that the fabrication is one-sided (which is the evidence the quantity is linear rather than reciprocal), and do not count them toward mutation coverage.

defects.guarded_quantity: |w| of the clip-space vector clip = MVP * (point, 1). It is the homogeneous scale factor of the clip vector: degree-1 in the MVP's overall scale and degree-1 in the world scale. For any perspective matrix m4_perspective_rh builds (src/mat4.cyr:335 sets col 2 / row 3 to -1) it is exactly -z_view, i.e. a LENGTH in view units, dimension length^1, unbounded above and below. Not dimensionless, not bounded, not squared, not a normalised cosine or a barycentric weight. (For an orthographic MVP m4_ortho_rh sets w = 1 exactly — MEASURED at t = 1e0/1e-13/1e-100/1e-300, w == 1.0 bit-exactly at every one, ship and repair both returning 600.0 — so the guard is inert on that path and any ortho-only fixture is vacuous. The defect is reachable only through the perspective/scaled path, which is what the function exists for.)
defects.protects: The reciprocal f64_div(F64_ONE, cw) on the next line (transforms.cyr:170) and the three perspective divides x*inv_w, y*inv_w, z*inv_w that consume it. Provenance is explicit and rules out any tolerance reading: docs/audit/2026-04-15.md H5 records this guard's origin as "Division by zero in world_to_screen ... Fix: Guard w==0 like m4_transform_point does", and docs/development/threat-model.md:41 lists it as "Perspective divide by w=0 -> Returns hvec3_zero()".
defects.why: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED ON ALL FIVE AVENUES; ALL FIVE FAIL, EACH BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. (1) DIMENSIONLESS/BOUNDED? No. w is a view-space depth for every perspective MVP, and independently of units the map the function computes, (x/w, y/w, z/w), is degree-0 homogeneous in the clip vector while |w| is degree-1 — so MVP and c*MVP are the same projection and must give the same pixel. Reproduced both ways in a bit-faithful IEEE-754 simulation of m4_perspective_rh, m4_mul_vec4 (col-scale-and-accumulate order, no FMA) and world_to_screen: base screen = (520.7106781186548, 300.0, 0.9676343009676343), bits_x = 408045af78026cd7; the shipped guard first returns a wrong answer at decade e = 13 in the UNIT sweep and at e = 13 in the unit-free HOMOGENEITY sweep, the same decade from two independent premises. (2) CALLER NORMALISES? No. grep over src/, tests/, examples/ finds no in-tree caller other than the abuse assertion; it is a public entry point taking a caller-supplied MVP, and there is no normalisation of a projective matrix to appeal to. (3) CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE? Refuted by the repo's own record — audit H5 above names it a divide-by-zero guard, and src/error.cyr:40-44 states the discriminating rule verbatim: F64_TINY "is the right threshold when the guard protects a DIVISION and the only thing that can actually fail is a zero (or subnormal) denominator. EPSILON_F64 remains right for a genuinely dimensionless, bounded quantity - a normalised cosine, a barycentric weight, a parameter in [0,1]". cw is none of those, so the project's own written rule selects F64_TINY. (4) BREAKS AN EXISTING TEST? CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. The only occurrence of world_to_screen in tests/*.tcyr is tests/abuse.tcyr:1496, assert_neq(world_to_screen(hvec3_zero(), m4_identity(), 0, 0), 0, "0x0 viewport returns a vector") — an identity MVP gives clip = (0,0,0,1), so cw = 1.0, the guard is inert, and the assertion is a non-null pointer check that hvec3_zero() would also satisfy. Changing EPSILON_F64 -> F64_TINY changes zero assertions in all five suites. (5) TEST DOESN'T DISCRIMINATE? It does; bracketing measured and tabulated below. The comment "# Point at camera" additionally names an intent the expression does not implement — "at the camera" is w small RELATIVE to the rest of the clip vector or to the near plane, and neither quantity appears here — so it is also a wrong-quantity guard, but the taxonomy's primary fit remains ABSOLUTE_ON_SCALING because the guarded quantity plainly scales. NOTE THE CLASS, NOT JUST THE SITE: m4_transform_point (src/mat4.cyr:150) carries the byte-identical `f64_lt(f64_abs(pw), EPSILON_F64)` guard on the same homogeneous w and fabricates DIFFERENTLY (returns the undivided (x,y,z)), and screen_to_world_ray (transforms.cyr:187-188) divides by HVec4_w with no guard at all — three sites, three different answers to one question.
defects.fabricates: hvec3_zero() = (0, 0, 0) — a perfectly legitimate screen position: x = 0 is the left edge, y = 0 is the top edge, z = 0 is the near plane. The function's only channel is the returned Vec3; there is no rc and no sentinel, and the sole existing test (assert_neq(..., 0)) accepts it, so a caller drawing at the returned pixel silently draws in the top-left corner. MEASURED at world scale 1e-13: shipped returns (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) where the correct answer is (520.7106781186548, 300.0, 0.9676343009676343) — the x error is 520.7 px on an 800 px viewport, i.e. 65% of the frame.
defects.correct_threshold: F64_TINY — DBL_MIN, 0x0010_0000_0000_0000 — already defined at src/error.cyr:45 with a comment (lines 40-44) that selects it for exactly this case. It is the smallest magnitude whose reciprocal is finite, and a zero or subnormal cw is the only thing that makes 1/cw fail. ⚠ SHARPENED BY MEASUREMENT: a bare `cw == 0` exact-compare is NOT an adequate repair and must be excluded explicitly, because subnormal w still overflows the reciprocal — at t = 1e-309..1e-323 the measured w is 3.0e-309 .. 3e-323 and `== 0` yields screen_x = +inf at every one, while F64_TINY yields the documented hvec3_zero(). Retain hvec3_zero() as the fired-guard return so the published contract (threat-model.md:41) is unchanged; only the threshold moves. If a real "point at camera" PREDICATE is wanted in addition it must be RELATIVE and must name what it is relative to — |w| < rel * max(|x|,|y|,|z|) of the same clip vector, the only scale-free quantity available here — but it is a separate documented predicate, never a substitute for the divide guard. Fix the sibling sites in the same change or the class survives: m4_transform_point (src/mat4.cyr:150), same guard on the same quantity, different fabrication; screen_to_world_ray (src/transforms.cyr:187-188), no guard at all.
defects.scale_test: FOUR PARTS. Parts (a) and (b) are the triage's two sweeps, CONFIRMED by measurement but corrected in three places where following the text literally produces a false failure or a vacuous case; parts (c) and (d) are additions the original set could not do without. FIXTURE (all parts): proj = m4_perspective_rh(pi/4, 800/600, 0.1t, 100t); view = m4_identity() with m4_set(view, 3, 2, -3t) HAND-BUILT; point = (0.5t, 0, 0); viewport 800x600. ⛔ Do NOT build the view with m4_look_at_rh — its internal hvec3_normalize (src/vec3.cyr:110) carries an identical EPSILON_F64 guard firing at the same decade on the same magnitude, so the sweep then passes or fails for the wrong reason. (a) UNIT COVARIANCE: for every e in 0..308 with t = 10^-e, assert screen_x and screen_y BIT-EXACTLY against their e=0 values (520.7106781186548 / bits 408045af78026cd7, and 300.0). ⚠ CORRECTION 1, MEASURED: do NOT assert the third component (depth) bit-exactly — the CORRECT repair already differs there at e = 5, because m[3][2] = 2*far*near/(near-far) is QUADRATIC in t and (far+near)/(near-far) re-rounds per decade; asserting the whole Vec3 makes the fix fail its own test. Assert depth to <= 4 ulp or omit it. (b) HOMOGENEITY, unit-free: fix the e=0 MVP and for c = 10^-e over e in 0..308 assert world_to_screen(p, c*MVP, 800, 600) is bit-identical in x and y to world_to_screen(p, MVP, 800, 600). MEASURED to kill at exactly the same decades as (a), which is the confound-free confirmation. (c) ⚠ ADDITION — LOW-SIDE BRACKET, which the original set omits and therefore cannot kill an under-guard: for e in 309..323 assert world_to_screen returns hvec3_zero(). MEASURED: w is subnormal there (3.0e-309 down to 3e-323), F64_TINY returns 0.0 and a bare `cw == 0` repair returns +inf, so this is the only part that discriminates the two, and it also pins DBL_MIN as the exact boundary rather than leaving it "just past where the sweep stops". (d) ⚠ CORRECTION 2 — EXACT w == 0, so the sweep cannot be satisfied by deleting the guard: the point must be at world z = +3t, NOT -3t. With the camera translation m4_set(view,3,2,-3t) the camera sits at +3t looking down -z; z = -3t gives w = +6.0 and the case is VACUOUS (measured — I made this exact error before checking). At z = +3t the measured clip w is exactly 0.0, shipped and F64_TINY both return (0,0,0) while `== 0` and DELETED both return (inf, inf, inf). Assert the run counter on (a), (b) and (c) — 309, 309 and 15 iterations. BRACKETING, MEASURED first-wrong decade under (a) and (b) alike: 1e-9 -> e=10, shipped 1e-12 -> e=13, 1e-15 -> e=16, DBL_EPSILON 2.2e-16 -> e=17, 1e-100 -> e=101, 1e-200 -> e=201, 1e-300 -> e=301; F64_TINY, `== 0` and DELETED all survive 0..308 and are then separated by (c) and (d). A 20-decade sweep kills only the first four and leaves 1e-100, 1e-200 and 1e-300 alive — the 2.11.1 mistake, confirmed by running it. ORTHO CONTROL (negative control, must be part of the fixture comment): the same sweep on m4_ortho_rh shows w == 1.0 bit-exactly at every decade and ship == repair == 600.0, proving the sweep's signal comes from the perspective path and not from the loop.
